name: @wunderui/react
description: WunderUI Free — the free components of the WunderUI design system for React.

install.more: This package holds the 89 free components. WunderUI Core and Pro come with a plan (https://wunderui.com/#pricing).

plans.free: WunderUI Free: the components with tier "free" are open source under the MIT License (https://github.com/wunder-ui/wunderui) — any project, commercial included. Every "pro" component needs WunderUI Core or Pro.
plans.core: WunderUI Core: every component, commercial license.
plans.pro: WunderUI Pro: everything in Core plus UI block and template source and all agent skills.

durations.use: Tooltip dismiss, press release. Barely reads as motion.
The default exit. Hover, focus ring, checkbox, switch track.
Dropdown, popover, context menu, backdrop, collapse.
Dialog, toast, switch thumb — a surface arriving.
A side panel and a full-width panel. Rare.
Progress and meter fills. Data moving, not chrome.

easings.use: Anything arriving. Fast start, long settle. The house curve.
Anything repositioning while staying on screen.
Dialog, popover, switch. At most one per screen.
A sampled spring: one soft overshoot, then it settles. Something physical landing — a thumb, an arrow, a released sheet. Never on a data value.

amplitudes.use: Tooltip — stays glued to its anchor.

rules: **Duration and easing are class names, not numbers.** `duration-base`, `ease-entrance`. Tailwind has no `--duration-*` theme namespace, so WunderUI ships these as `@utility` rules that also set `--tw-duration` — which means they work on `animate-in` / `animate-out` too.
**Only `transform` and `opacity`.** Everything else goes through layout or paint. Height animates via `grid-template-rows: 0fr → 1fr`, never via `height`.
**Entrances decelerate, exits accelerate.** `ease-entrance` in, `ease-exit` out — and the exit is one step shorter on the duration scale, never the entrance duration reversed.
**Never fade in the LCP element.** An element at `opacity: 0` is not an LCP candidate, so a 600ms hero fade adds 600ms to your LCP. Render headline copy at full opacity; animate `transform` only.
**Restrain the travel.** Anything anchored to a trigger moves `--travel-xs` or `--travel-sm`. A menu that slides 20px looks like it fell in.

**One overshoot per screen.** `ease-overshoot` is punctuation. Two of them on one view and the interface reads as a toy. Never on a data value: a bar, gauge or bubble that swings past its number shows a wrong number for a moment.

**Reduced motion is opt-in, not a kill switch.** Wrap the animation in `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)` so the still state is the default and you cannot forget a selector. Reduced means calmer, not nothing: drop transforms and travel, keep opacity and colour changes (rule 15).

**Never `transition-all`.** Name the properties — `transition-[opacity,transform]` — or use bare `transition`, which covers colour, shadow, transform and opacity but no layout property. `transition-all` animates things you did not mean to animate, including on first paint.
**Loading keeps its height.** A skeleton occupies the same box as the content it stands in for, and crossfades — it never collapses and reflows.
**A looping ambient animation is the one place `ease-in-out` belongs.** A shimmer that runs forever has no entrance and no exit, so symmetry is correct there and nowhere else.

**Animate by frequency.** Keyboard-driven and 100+/day actions (command palette, shortcuts, moving between tooltips) get no motion; tens a day get a short fade; rare moments may delight. Tooltips skip their entrance when another one was just open (`data-open:data-instant:animate-none`).

**Anchored surfaces grow from their trigger.** Popover, dropdown, tooltip, hover card and select use `origin-(--transform-origin)`. Never start from `scale(0)` — start at 0.92–0.97 with opacity. Centred dialogs are exempt.

**Toggles stay interruptible.** Animate switches, checkboxes, tabs and other repeated state changes with transitions — they retarget from wherever they are — never with keyframes bound to the state, which restart from zero. An overshoot transition (`transition-transform duration-base ease-overshoot`) still swings past the end.

**Hover only where hover exists.** Tailwind v4's `hover:` is already gated to `(hover: hover)`; hand-written `:hover` in CSS goes inside `@media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)`, so a tap on a phone does not leave a hover state stuck.

**Reduced motion keeps the fade.** WunderUI's global rule zeroes the scale, slide, spin and blur of every `animate-in` / `animate-out` and every transform transition, and keeps opacity and colour — so do not add `motion-reduce:transition-none` or `motion-reduce:animate-none` to a fade.

recipes.Overlay enter and exit:
/* Dialog, sheet, popover, dropdown, context menu — one pattern for all of them.
   Base UI exposes data-open / data-closed; tw-animate-css turns them into keyframes. */
<Dialog.Popup className="
  data-open:animate-in   data-open:fade-in-0   data-open:zoom-in-92
  data-open:slide-in-from-bottom-2
  data-open:duration-slow  data-open:ease-overshoot
  data-closed:animate-out  data-closed:fade-out-0 data-closed:zoom-out-96
  data-closed:duration-fast data-closed:ease-exit
" />

components.title: Accordion
components.description: Show one section at a time, or several, and keep long pages scannable.

parts.name: Accordion
parts.description: Tracks which items are open: one at a time by default, several if you allow it. You pick a look (plain, divided, contained, separated) and a density.

parts.name: AccordionItem
parts.description: One section of the list. It draws the divider, the card or the hover fill, depending on the look of the list.

parts.name: AccordionTrigger
parts.description: The header row: a real button inside a heading. It can hold a leading icon, a second line, a slot for extra info and an indicator.

parts.name: Label
parts.description: The question or section name inside the trigger. It is also the button's accessible name.

parts.name: Meta
parts.description: A slot between the label and the indicator, for a counter, a status or a short value.

parts.name: Indicator
parts.description: The chevron or plus that shows whether the item is open. Its style and position follow the look of the list unless you set them.

parts.name: AccordionContent
parts.description: The panel under the trigger. It opens smoothly to the height of its content, and its text lines up with the label.

parts.name: AccordionRow
parts.description: Wraps the trigger so a control can sit beside it, not inside it: a checkbox or switch on the left, or an action button such as Edit.

parts.name: AccordionFeedback
parts.description: The loading, empty and error content of a panel, with an optional action such as Retry.

items.text: Pick one look per list: divided or plain on a page, contained as one card, separated for stand-alone sections.
Use the compact density (36 px rows) in side panels and the default (48 px rows) everywhere else.
Allow several open items when people compare answers. By default, opening one closes the other.
Write the trigger as the question or section name in sentence case, like How do refunds work? It is the button's accessible name.
Put controls beside the trigger with AccordionRow. The trigger stays a single button and the control gets its own Tab stop.
Don't put buttons or links inside the trigger. The whole row is already a button, and a button inside a button is invalid HTML.
Don't hide what people must read or do in a closed row. Required information and primary actions belong outside the accordion.

useFor: FAQs and help pages, where people read one answer at a time
Grouped settings, such as account, billing and notifications
Long forms split into sections or steps, such as a checkout

useInstead.name: Collapsible
useInstead.text: a single show-more panel

useInstead.name: Tabs
useInstead.text: peer views of one object that people switch between

useInstead.name: Dialog
useInstead.text: a task that must block the page until it is done

keyboard.intro: The trigger is a native button, so the browser provides focus and activation.
keyboard.note: Arrow keys, Home and End do not move focus between rows in this version.

rows.action: Moves focus to the next or previous trigger, and to any control placed beside it with `AccordionRow`.
Opens or closes the focused row. In single mode, opening a row closes the open one.

behavior.intro: What the list does with state, content, the DOM and motion.

items.title: Disabled rows
items.text: A disabled item stays focusable and is announced as disabled, but it cannot be toggled. It is drawn at 40 % opacity.

items.title: Closed panels are not in the DOM
items.text: Closed panels are not rendered by default, so their text is missing from page search and form values inside are lost. You can keep them mounted or let find-in-page open them.

items.title: Values are arrays
items.text: Values are always arrays of item values, even in single mode, where the array holds at most one. Allow several open rows to hold more.

items.title: Always set the look
items.text: Look and density are optional. Without a look you get the legacy spaced cards with a +/- button, and rows are 48 px high, so set both in new code.

items.title: Headings
items.text: Every trigger sits in an h3 by default. Set a heading level from 2 to 6 on the list or on one trigger so the rows fit your page outline.

items.title: Opening and closing
items.text: Panels grow and shrink with their content. Opening takes the base duration, and closing is one step faster so a dismissed panel does not linger.

items.title: Indicators
items.text: The plus, minus and cross indicators crossfade in place instead of swapping.

items.title: Reduced motion
items.text: With reduced motion on, the panel opens and closes instantly and the indicators only fade. Colour changes stay.

minimalUsage.code:
import {
  Accordion,
  AccordionContent,
  AccordionItem,
  AccordionTrigger,
} from "@/components/ui/accordion"

export function Faq() {
  return (
    <Accordion appearance="divided" density="default" defaultValue={["refunds"]}>
      <AccordionItem value="refunds">
        <AccordionTrigger>How long does a refund take?</AccordionTrigger>
        <AccordionContent>Refunds reach your original payment method within 5 to 7 business days after approval.</AccordionContent>
      </AccordionItem>
      <AccordionItem value="password">
        <AccordionTrigger>How do I reset my password?</AccordionTrigger>
        <AccordionContent>Open Settings, choose Security and select Reset password.</AccordionContent>
      </AccordionItem>
      <AccordionItem value="plan">
        <AccordionTrigger>Can I change my billing plan?</AccordionTrigger>
        <AccordionContent>You can change your plan at any time in Billing; changes apply immediately.</AccordionContent>
      </AccordionItem>
    </Accordion>
  )
}
minimalUsage.expected: You should see three rows; the first one is open.

Accordion.value.description: The values of the open items, for a controlled accordion. In single mode the array holds at most one value.

Accordion.defaultValue.description: The values of the items that start open, for an uncontrolled accordion.

Accordion.onValueChange.description: Called with the new array of open item values whenever a row opens or closes.

Accordion.loopFocus.note: Arrow keys do not move focus in this version, so there is no focus to loop.

parts.name: Avatar
parts.description: The round or square frame in five sizes. Set a colour for tinted initials or the primary variant for a filled one; interactive makes it a button, selected adds a check badge and disabled dims it.

parts.name: AvatarImage
parts.description: The photo, an img with src and alt. It shows once loaded; until then, or when the URL fails, the fallback stays in place.

parts.name: AvatarFallback
parts.description: Initials or an icon, shown while the image loads or when there is none. The text size follows the avatar size.

parts.name: AvatarBadge
parts.description: A dot on the top right corner, centred on the circle's edge or the square's corner. A status sets a presence dot with a shape per status and an accessible name that defaults to the status.

parts.name: AvatarLabel
parts.description: An avatar with a name and a second line, and optionally a capacity bar or a control at the end. It is a plain div. It replaces PersonCell and UserInfo, which still render the same row.

items.text: Use an Avatar to show who a person or workspace is, next to their name. For several people in little space, use Avatar Group.
Always add a fallback with initials, also when there is an image. It covers the moment before the photo loads and a broken image URL.
Use a circle for a person and a square for an entity such as a workspace, team or project, so the shape already tells which one it is.
Keep one colour per person. The tints are theme tokens, so initials stay readable in dark mode.
Show presence with the badge and say it in text where it matters, such as Away next to the name. Each status has its own shape, so colour is never the only signal.
Give an interactive avatar an accessible name with aria-label, for example Account menu, Nora Lindgren. Its initials are not a name.
Don't resize an avatar with your own size classes. Pick one of the sizes: initials, icon and presence dot scale with it.
Don't use colour to carry status or meaning. Tone is an identity colour; status needs the presence dot, a word, or both.
Don't combine selected with a presence dot. The check badge and the dot sit on the same corner, so one hides the other.
Next to a single 20 px line of text use size="3xs", so the avatar is as tall as the text.

useFor: Showing who a person is next to their name, a comment or an activity entry
Showing what a workspace, team or project is, with a square avatar
The account button of an app bar, or a choice of a person in a picker

useInstead.name: Avatar Group
useInstead.text: several people in a row, composed by hand with a hover effect or passed as data with people and a limit

useInstead.name: Person Cell
useInstead.text: an avatar with a name and a role in a table or a list

keyboard.intro: A plain avatar is not interactive and has no keyboard behaviour. An interactive avatar is a native button.

rows.action: Moves focus to or away from an interactive avatar. A disabled one is skipped.
Presses the avatar, for example to open an account menu or to choose a person.

behavior.intro: What the avatar does with state, content, the DOM and motion.

items.title: Image and fallback
items.text: The fallback stays in place until the image has loaded, and when the URL fails; you can delay it to avoid a flash for a fast image. The tint sits on the frame behind the image.

items.title: Size
items.text: The size sets the frame (24, 28, 36, 40 or 44 px) and scales initials, icon and presence dot with it. Initials and counts are centred on cap height, so they look centred in any font.

items.title: Presence dot
items.text: The badge sits on the top right corner: its centre is on the edge of a circle, or on the rounded corner of a square. With a status it is an image named by the status; override with aria-label.

items.title: Interactive
items.text: An interactive avatar is a button with aria-pressed from selected. Hover draws a 3 px halo in the page tone, a press the subtle tone, keyboard focus the focus ring, and disabled dims it to 40 %.

items.title: Selected
items.text: Selected adds a check badge on the top right corner, where the presence dot sits, and keeps the subtle halo on an interactive avatar.

items.title: Names for screen readers
items.text: Initials are real text, so a screen reader reads NL before the name. When the name is printed beside the avatar, hide the avatar from assistive technology and give the image an empty alt.

items.title: Motion
items.text: The avatar has no motion of its own: the halo of an interactive avatar changes at once.

items.title: Reduced motion
items.text: Nothing animates, so reduced motion needs no fallback here. In Avatar Group the hover lift is switched off.

minimalUsage.expected: You should see one round 36 px avatar with the indigo tint and the initials NL.

Avatar.size.description: The size of the frame: `sm` is 24 px, `xs` 28 px, `default` 36 px, `lg` 40 px and `xl` 44 px. Initials, icon and presence dot scale with it.

Avatar.shape.description: `circle` for a person, `square` for an entity such as a workspace, team or project. The square has a medium corner radius.

Avatar.variant.description: `plain` is a muted fill with a hairline border. `primary` fills the frame with the primary colour and sets the initials in the colour on primary.

Avatar.color.description: A soft tint for initials: the tint colour behind and the matching tint text colour on top. Use one hue per person, and do not combine it with `variant="primary"`.

Avatar.interactive.description: Renders the avatar as a `button` with hover, pressed and focus states. Pass `aria-label`, because the initials are not a name.

Avatar.selected.description: Marks the avatar as chosen: a check badge on the top right corner. With `interactive` it also draws the subtle halo and sets `aria-pressed`.

Avatar.disabled.description: Dims an interactive avatar to 40 % and removes pointer events. It has no effect on a plain avatar.

Avatar.className.description: Extra classes for the frame, merged with its own. Use it for a one-off colour such as the dark tint of a chosen row, not for the size.

Avatar.render.description: Replaces the element of the avatar, for example with a link: `render={<a href="/team/nora" />}`. Accepts an element or a function that returns one.

Avatar.style.description: Inline styles for the frame, or a function that returns them from the state of the avatar.

AvatarBadge.status.description: The presence dot: `available`, `busy`, `away`, `dnd`, `offline` or `unknown`. Each has its own shape and an accessible name by default (`Available`, `Busy`, `Away`, `Do not disturb`, `Offline`, `Status unknown`). Without `status` the badge is an empty dot for your own content.

AvatarFallback.delay.description: How long to wait before the fallback shows, in milliseconds. Use it so the initials do not flash while a fast image loads.

AvatarFallback.className.description: Extra classes for the fallback, merged with its own.

AvatarFallback.render.description: Replaces the element of the fallback.

AvatarFallback.style.description: Inline styles for the fallback, or a function that returns them from its state.

AvatarImage.keepMounted.description: Keeps the image in the DOM while it is not shown, for example while it loads or when it failed.

AvatarImage.onLoadingStatusChange.description: Called with `idle`, `loading`, `loaded` or `error` whenever the loading status of the image changes.

AvatarImage.className.description: Extra classes for the image, merged with its own.

AvatarImage.render.description: Replaces the `img` element, for example with the image component of your framework.

AvatarImage.style.description: Inline styles for the image, or a function that returns them from its state.

AvatarLabel.name.description: The name, cut to one line. The initials are taken from it when there is no photo and no `initials`. Required.

AvatarLabel.subtext.description: The line under the name, such as a role or an email.

AvatarLabel.src.description: The address of a photo. It replaces the initials and has empty alternative text, because the name stands beside it.

AvatarLabel.initials.description: The text in the avatar without a photo. Default: the first letters of the first two words of the name.

AvatarLabel.color.description: The tint behind the initials, as on Avatar. Without it the avatar is grey.

AvatarLabel.size.description: The avatar: `default` 36 px, `lg` 40 px or `xl` 44 px.

AvatarLabel.compact.description: Smaller text, 12 px for the name and 11 px for the second line, with a semibold name. On by default when there is a capacity bar.

AvatarLabel.nameWeight.description: The weight of the name: `medium` or `semibold`. Default: semibold when compact, medium otherwise.

AvatarLabel.tight.description: Removes the 2 px between the name and the second line.

AvatarLabel.capacity.description: A load bar under the text, as `value` 0 to 100 and an optional `label` such as 25h. It is a meter: green up to 80 %, yellow up to 100 %, red above.

AvatarLabel.trailing.description: A control at the end of the row, such as an IconButton that opens a menu.

components.title: Avatar Group
components.description: A stack of overlapping avatars, with an optional overflow count.
components.props: function AvatarGroup({ people, max, size, layout, children, className, ...props }: AvatarGroupProps): React.JSX.Element;

props.name: max
props.description: With `people`: how many faces show before the count. Default 3.

props.name: people
props.description: A list of people: the group renders their avatars itself, overlapping by 4 px (2 px at `sm` and `xs`, so the second initial is not hidden under the next face), cut at `max` with a "+N" avatar. Hovering a face lifts it and shows the name in…

props.name: size
props.description: With `people`: the avatar size, `sm` 24 px, `xs` 28 px, `default` 36 px, `lg` 40 px, `xl` 44 px. Default `sm`.

parts.name: AvatarGroup
parts.description: The row. It overlaps its avatars with a ring in the surface colour, or spaces them with a 6 px gap; hovering one lifts it and nudges its neighbours, except with reduced motion.

parts.name: Avatar
parts.description: Each person: an Avatar with initials or an image. Give all avatars in one group the same size.

parts.name: AvatarGroupCount
parts.description: The +N circle at the end for everyone not shown, as a static count or a button. It takes the size of the avatars.

items.text: Use an Avatar Group to show who is on a project or document, composing each avatar yourself. For people passed as data with a built-in limit, pass people, max and size instead of children (a people list lifts on hover and names each face in a Tooltip too).
Cut the list yourself and put the rest in the count as +3. The group renders every child it gets; it does not count or hide anyone.
Make the count a button when people can open the rest. Give it an aria-label such as Show 3 more people and aria-expanded.
Place the group on a surface that sets the surface colour, such as a Card. The rings take that colour, so each avatar reads as cut out of the background.
Pick overlap for a header or a row where room is short, and spaced for a short list where each face should stay whole.
Don't mix avatar sizes in one group. The overlap and the count circle assume one size for every avatar.
Don't use a group for a single person, or for a list people should read name by name. Use Avatar, or AvatarLabel with a name.
At sm and xs the faces overlap by 2 px so both initials stay readable; do not tighten them further with your own spacing.

useFor: The people on a project, document or meeting, in a header or a row
A short list of people where you decide how many faces show
A row of faces with a button that opens everyone who is not shown
A list of people passed as data, cut at a limit with a +N count worked out for you (people)

useInstead.name: Avatar
useInstead.text: one person, workspace or team

useInstead.name: Avatar label
useInstead.text: people listed with a name and a role in a table or a list

keyboard.intro: The group is a plain container. Only an interactive count is a control, and it is a native button.
keyboard.note: The hover lift follows the mouse only: moving focus with the keyboard does not lift an avatar.

rows.action: Moves focus to or away from an interactive count, and to any interactive avatar in the group, in the order they are written.
Presses the focused count, for example to open the list of the people who are not shown.

behavior.intro: What the group does with state, content, the DOM and motion.

items.title: Every child is shown
items.text: The group renders every child it gets and does not count, cut or reorder them. Later avatars sit on top of earlier ones.

items.title: Overlap and rings
items.text: In overlap layout each avatar overlaps the one before by 12 px and gets a 2 px ring in the surface colour. In spaced layout the avatars keep a 6 px gap and get no ring.

items.title: Count
items.text: A static count is a muted circle with the text you pass, such as +3. As a button it has a border: hover and open use the page tone, a press the subtle tone, disabled dims it to 40 %.

items.title: Size
items.text: The group has no size setting. The count takes the size of the avatars, 24, 28, 36, 40 or 44 px, so give every avatar the same one.

items.title: Names for screen readers
items.text: A static count is read as plain +3, so add visually hidden text like more people after it, or use an interactive count with an aria-label. Hide the avatars when names are listed elsewhere.

items.title: Motion
items.text: Hovering an avatar lifts it by 4 px and scales it to 1.05; neighbours lift less the farther away they are. Only transform animates.

items.title: Reduced motion
items.text: With reduced motion on, the lift is off: hovering changes nothing.

components.title: Badge
components.description: A small status or category label in 12 colors and 6 styles.

props.name: render
props.description: Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render.

props.name: render
props.description: Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render.

parts.name: Badge
parts.description: A short label in a rounded box, in 12 colors, 6 styles, two sizes (20 or 24 px) and a rounded or pill shape. As a button or link it gains hover, focus and press states.

parts.name: Leading mark
parts.description: A Lucide icon as a child, or a dot. The icon is 12 px on a small badge and 14 px on a medium one, follows the label color, and sits 4 or 6 px before it.

parts.name: Label
parts.description: One short line, 12 px semibold on a small badge and 14 px on a medium one. It never wraps and clips what does not fit, so keep the label to a word or two.

parts.name: Remove button
parts.description: A 16 px round button with an X, drawn when a remove handler is set. It is a separate button with its own name and the badge itself stays inert; it is left out when the badge is a button or link.

parts.name: BadgeCell
parts.description: A Badge for a table cell, made from a label string, with the light border style by default.

parts.name: BadgeCounter
parts.description: A count next to a label, or on the corner of an icon button, in neutral, brand or danger tones. Counts above 99 read 99+, and an overlay counter hides itself at zero.

parts.name: BadgeIndicator
parts.description: A small signal: unread, presence (online, away, busy, offline) or a symbol (check, warning, lock). Each kind has its own shape, not only its own color, and carries an accessible name.

parts.name: BadgeProcessing
parts.description: A running operation and its result: pending (a turning spinner), success or error. The label always names the state.

parts.name: Chip
parts.description: An interactive pill that filters, selects or opens a list. Selection shows as the indigo tint and a mark, never as color alone.

parts.name: EntityChip
parts.description: A person, team or workspace as a pill: a 24 px mark (an avatar, an image, a flag) before the name, and an optional remove button. Written `<Chip variant="entity">`; EntityChip is a deprecated alias.

parts.name: TokenChip
parts.description: One entry inside a multi-value field, such as an email address. An invalid token gets a warning icon and the red tint; the field names the error. Written `<Chip variant="token">`; TokenChip is a deprecated alias.

items.text: Use a Badge for a short status or category on a row, card or heading: Paid, Draft, Beta. For the change in a number use Trend Chip, and for a message people have to read use Alert.
Give each status one color and keep it wherever that status appears. Write the status in the label as well, so color is never the only cue.
Use the light or light border style in tables and lists, and keep the solid style for the one badge that should stand out.
Render the badge as a button when it does something. Only a button or link gets the pointer cursor, the hover ring and the focus ring.
Put an overlay counter on the corner of a relatively positioned button and name the count in the button, like Notifications, 3 unread. The counter itself stays decorative.
Use Chip for a filter or a choice. It announces its selected state and shows a mark as well as the tint.
Don't use a Badge as a selection control. A removable tag takes a remove handler; anything that selects or opens a list is a Chip.
Don't recolor a badge with classes or hex values. Every color and style pair is measured for AA contrast in light and dark mode.
Don't put two badges on one heading, or a badge on every row of a list. A badge that is everywhere says nothing.

useFor: A short status or category on a row, a card or a heading, such as Paid, Draft or Beta
A count next to a navigation label or on the corner of an icon button
A running operation and its result, such as Syncing, Synced and Failed
Chips that filter or select, a person as a chip, and the entries of a multi-value field

useInstead.name: Alert
useInstead.text: a message people need to read, with a title and an action

useInstead.name: Trend Chip
useInstead.text: the change in a number, with its direction

useInstead.name: Avatar
useInstead.text: presence on a person: the avatar draws its own status mark

useInstead.name: Segment
useInstead.text: switching between two or more views, with one always selected

keyboard.intro: A badge is a span and takes no focus. Only what does something is a control: the remove button, a badge rendered as a button or link, and the chips.

rows.action: Moves focus to the next or previous control: a remove button, a chip, a badge rendered as a link or button.
Runs the focused control: removes the tag, toggles the chip, opens the list of a dropdown chip.

behavior.intro: What the badge does itself, and what it leaves to the page.

items.title: Static by default
items.text: A badge is a plain span: no role, no focus, no pointer. It reads as part of the text around it, so the label has to make sense there.

items.title: Color and style
items.text: Tinted looks use the tint tokens of the hue, so they follow light and dark mode. Every color and style pair is measured for AA contrast; the solid style uses white or the darkest step of the hue.

items.title: A badge that does something
items.text: As a button or link, the badge shows a ring in its own color on hover, scales down on press and gets the focus ring. The remove button is left out then, so two controls never nest.

items.title: Remove
items.text: A remove handler draws the remove button and calls your function. The badge does not hide itself: take the tag out of your list, and move focus to the next tag or the field.

items.title: Counter
items.text: A count above 99 reads 99+. An overlay counter hides at zero unless you keep it and needs a relative parent, and an inline counter shows 0 in tertiary text.

items.title: Indicator
items.text: The indicator is an image with an accessible name from its label, or a default for its kind. An overlay needs a relative parent, and its ring uses the card color so it stays readable on any surface.

items.title: Processing
items.text: The processing badge is a status region, marked busy while pending, and swaps the spinner for a check or a warning sign when the work ends. The text always names the state.

items.title: Chips
items.text: A chip keeps no state of its own: pass selected and open, and change them in the click handler. They set the matching aria-pressed, aria-checked or aria-expanded.

items.title: Motion
items.text: Color and ring changes use the fast duration. A pressed badge scales to 95 %, the remove button to 90 %, and the processing spinner turns until the work ends.

items.title: Reduced motion
items.text: With reduced motion on, the processing spinner is a still icon and the remove button no longer scales on press. The state is still named in text.

minimalUsage.expected: You should see one small green pill with the word Approved.

Badge.color.description: The hue of the badge. The status tones are `grey` (neutral), `indigo` (brand), `blue` (info), `green` (success), `yellow` (warning) and `red` (danger); the others label categories.

Badge.badgeStyle.description: The look: `plain` is a solid fill, `light` a tinted surface, `light_border` a tint with a rim, `border_color` and `border_grey` a white surface with a rim, and `ghost` text only. In Figma they are Solid, Subtle, Outline and Plain.

Badge.shape.description: `rounded` has an 8 px radius, `pill` is fully round.

Badge.size.description: `sm` is 20 px high with 12 px text, `md` is 24 px high with 14 px text.

Badge.dot.description: Draws a 6 px dot in the color of the label before it.

Badge.onRemove.description: Draws a remove button after the label and calls this function when it is pressed. Ignored when the badge is rendered through `render`.

Badge.removeLabel.description: The accessible name of the remove button. Name the tag in it: `Remove Marketing`.

BadgeCell.badgeStyle.description: The look of the badge. Defaults to `light_border`, the style of a status in a table.

BadgeCounter.count.description: The number to show. Negative values and fractions are treated as 0 and cut to a whole number.

BadgeCounter.tone.description: `neutral` is a grey pill, `brand` the primary color and `danger` red.

BadgeCounter.overlay.description: Positions the counter on the top right corner of its `relative` parent and gives it a ring in the card color. An overlay counter is hidden at zero.

BadgeCounter.max.description: The largest number shown. Above it the counter reads `99+`, or `{max}+` for another value.

BadgeCounter.hideZero.description: Hides the counter at zero. Defaults to `true` for an overlay and `false` for an inline counter.

BadgeIndicator.kind.description: What the indicator stands for. Each kind has its own shape: a dot, a ring, a moon, a bar, a check, a triangle or a lock.

BadgeIndicator.size.description: `sm` is 8 px for a dot and 16 px for a symbol; `md` is 10 px and 20 px.

BadgeIndicator.label.description: The accessible name. Defaults to the name of the kind, such as `Online` or `Locked`; give it more detail when it helps, such as `New event`.

BadgeIndicator.overlay.description: Positions the indicator on the top right corner of its `relative` parent, with a ring in the card color.

BadgeProcessing.state.description: `pending` shows a turning spinner on a blue tint, `success` a check on green and `error` a warning sign on red.

BadgeProcessing.size.description: `sm` is 20 px high, `md` is 24 px high. The badge is always a pill with the `light` style.

BadgeProcessing.removeLabel.note: The processing badge has no remove button.

Chip.selected.description: Shows the chip as selected: the indigo tint and rim. With `mark="check"` a check appears before the label.

Chip.mark.description: The mark before the label: a check when selected, a radio or a checkbox, or a dashed circle for a suggestion.

Chip.trailing.description: What follows the label: nothing, a chevron for a chip that opens a list, or a remove button for an applied filter.

Chip.open.description: Shows a chip with a chevron as open: the tint, and the chevron points up. It also sets `aria-expanded`.

Chip.role.description: Use `radio` for one choice out of a group and `checkbox` for a multi-select. It sets `aria-checked` from `selected`.

Chip.onClick.description: Called when the chip is pressed. The chip keeps no state: change `selected` or `open` here.

Chip.variant.description: `filter` (default) is the filter chip: a pill that selects, filters or opens a list. `entity` is a rounded pill with a mark in `leading` and a name, for a person, team or workspace. `token` is an input token with a `state`, for an entry inside a multi-value field. EntityChip and TokenChip are deprecated aliases of the last two.

Chip.leading.description: Variant `entity` only. The mark before the name, 24 px: an `Avatar`, an image, a flag.

Chip.state.description: Variant `token` only. `invalid` adds a warning icon and the red tint, `focused` shows the focus ring of the field, `removing` fills the remove button while it is pressed.

Chip.onRemove.description: Called when the remove button of a chip with `trailing="remove"` is pressed.

Chip.removeLabel.description: The accessible name of the remove button. Name the filter in it: `Remove filter Owner: Nora`.

Chip.className.description: Extra classes for the chip, merged with its own.

EntityChip.leading.description: The mark before the name, 24 px: an `Avatar`, an image, a flag.

EntityChip.children.description: The name of the person, team or workspace.

EntityChip.onRemove.description: Draws a remove button after the name and calls this function when it is pressed.

EntityChip.removeLabel.description: The accessible name of the remove button. Name the entity in it: `Remove Nora Lindgren`.

TokenChip.children.description: The entry, such as an email address.

TokenChip.state.description: `invalid` adds a warning icon and the red tint, `focused` shows the focus ring of the field, `removing` fills the remove button while it is pressed.

TokenChip.onRemove.description: Draws a remove button after the entry and calls this function when it is pressed.

TokenChip.removeLabel.description: The accessible name of the remove button. Name the entry in it: `Remove info@wunderui.com`.

components.title: Breadcrumb
components.description: Shows the user's location in a hierarchy, in the `plain`, `contained` or `underline` look.

parts.name: Breadcrumb
parts.description: The nav landmark named breadcrumb. Variant sets the look (plain, contained or underline), and density (36 px or 28 px rows) switches to the sized layout on one line.

parts.name: BreadcrumbList
parts.description: The ordered list of items and separators. Contained draws the border and surface and underline the line below; without density it wraps to a second line when room runs out.

parts.name: BreadcrumbItem
parts.description: One step of the trail, a list item holding a link or, at the end, the current page.

parts.name: BreadcrumbLink
parts.description: A level above the current page, a link that can hold an icon before the text. Truncated limits it to 160 px with an ellipsis and the full name as its title.

parts.name: BreadcrumbSeparator
parts.description: A list item between two items, hidden from screen readers. It shows a chevron, a slash, or your own icon.

parts.name: BreadcrumbEllipsis
parts.description: A button that stands for hidden middle levels. Use it as the trigger of a Popover that lists them; it shows an open state.

parts.name: BreadcrumbPage
parts.description: The current page as text, not a link, marked as the current page. It can be truncated like a link.

parts.name: BreadcrumbSiblingTrigger
parts.description: A separate button beside a link that opens a list of sibling pages. The link still navigates; the chevron turns when the list is open.

parts.name: BreadcrumbRestricted
parts.description: A level the person cannot open. It stays in the trail with a lock, is focusable and explains itself through its title.

parts.name: BreadcrumbLoading
parts.description: A quiet placeholder for the current level while its name loads. It is a status region; there is no spinner.

items.text: Use a Breadcrumb on nested pages, such as one project's settings, so people see where they are and can step back up. For switching between sibling views, use Tabs.
End the trail with BreadcrumbPage, not a link. It is marked as the current page, so screen readers announce where the person is.
Put a separator between items yourself; the list does not add them. Each one sits in its own list item and is hidden from assistive technology.
Pass a density to get the sized layout: 36 px rows with hover underline, pressed fill and focus ring. Without it the trail is the small inline list.
Collapse deep trails to the root, the parent and the current page. Put the hidden levels behind an ellipsis that opens a list of links, in their real order.
Keep a restricted level visible with BreadcrumbRestricted instead of removing it, so the trail stays truthful.
Show the trail as one link to the parent page below 360 px of width.
Don't link the current page or mark a link as current by hand. BreadcrumbPage already marks the last step and is not clickable.
Don't show a spinner while the current name loads. Use BreadcrumbLoading, a quiet placeholder with the right accessible name.
Don't use a breadcrumb as the only way to move around. It shows the path to the page, not every page there is.

useFor: Nested pages, such as one project's assets or one invoice in a customer account
A deep hierarchy of files, folders or documentation where people need to step back up
Any page that can be reached from more than one place, so the trail names where it lives

useInstead.name: Tabs
useInstead.text: switching between views of the same page

useInstead.name: Pagination
useInstead.text: moving through the pages of one list

useInstead.name: Stepper
useInstead.text: the steps of a process, in a fixed order

useInstead.name: Sidebar
useInstead.text: the whole tree of an app, always on screen

keyboard.intro: The trail is a list of links, so the browser provides focus and activation. The ellipsis and the sibling trigger are buttons that open a Popover.

rows.action: Moves focus to the next or previous link or button in the trail, in the order they are written. The current page is not a stop.
Follows the focused link, or opens the list of hidden levels or siblings from its button.
Opens the list from the ellipsis or the sibling trigger.
Closes an open list and returns focus to the button that opened it.

behavior.intro: What the trail draws itself, and what it leaves to the page.

items.title: Landmark and list
items.text: Breadcrumb is a nav named breadcrumb around an ordered list. Separators are hidden list items, so a screen reader reads the levels and not the chevrons.

items.title: Current page
items.text: BreadcrumbPage is a span marked as the current page and disabled. It is not a link and does not react to the pointer.

items.title: Layout and density
items.text: Without density the trail is a small inline list that wraps. With density it is a 36 px or 28 px row on one line, so a trail longer than its box needs collapsing, truncating or a parent link.

items.title: Link states
items.text: A link darkens and underlines on hover, fills with the subtle tone while pressed and shows the focus ring directly on the item. In the underline look the underline turns primary on hover.

items.title: Collapsed levels
items.text: BreadcrumbEllipsis is only the button. It opens whatever you put next to it, such as a Popover with links to the hidden levels in their real order, and shows an open state.

items.title: Sibling switcher
items.text: BreadcrumbSiblingTrigger is a second button beside the link. The link still navigates; the button opens the list of sibling pages and its chevron turns while the list is open.

items.title: Restricted level
items.text: BreadcrumbRestricted is focusable, shows a lock and explains itself through its title. It is a disabled link and never navigates.

items.title: Loading name
items.text: BreadcrumbLoading is a quiet grey block that is a status region with an accessible name. There is no spinner.

items.title: Long names
items.text: Truncated limits a link or the current page to 160 px, ends the text in an ellipsis and sets the full name as the title.

items.title: Narrow screens
items.text: The trail does not shorten itself. Below 360 px of width show a single link to the parent page instead.

items.title: Motion
items.text: Color, underline and fill changes are quick. The chevron of the sibling trigger turns 180 degrees while its list is open.

items.title: Reduced motion
items.text: With reduced motion on, the sibling chevron turns without a transition. Nothing else in the trail moves.

Breadcrumb.variant.description: The look of the trail: `plain` text, `contained` in a bordered box, `underline` with a line below. `border` is the old name of `contained`.

components.title: Button
components.description: The main action trigger, in 11 variants, 2 shapes and 5 sizes.

props.name: className
props.description: CSS class applied to the element, or a function that returns a class based on the component's state.

props.name: focusableWhenDisabled
props.description: Whether the button should be focusable when disabled.

props.name: nativeButton
props.description: Whether the component renders a native `<button>` element when replacing it via the `render` prop. Set to `false` if the rendered element is not a button (for example, `<div>`).

props.name: pending
props.description: Shows a spinner in place of the leading icon and ignores presses. The button stays focusable and keeps its colour (it is not disabled).

props.name: phase
props.description: Async feedback: pending shows a spinner, success a check, error a retry icon. The label is yours (for example Saving…, Saved, Retry). Keep the width constant with a fixed width on the button so it does not jump between phases.

props.name: render
props.description: Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render.

props.name: style
props.description: Style applied to the element, or a function that returns a style object based on the component's state.

parts.name: Button
parts.description: A native button that fits its content. Variant sets the look, size the height (32 to 48 px), shape rounded or pill, and pending shows a spinner and ignores presses.

parts.name: Leading icon
parts.description: An icon before the label, with 2 px less padding on that side. It is 16 px at small and medium, up to 24 px at the largest sizes, and a spinner replaces it while pending.

parts.name: Label
parts.description: The text, 14 px medium (16 px at xl, 18 px at 2xl). Write a verb and its object, such as Save changes, and keep it on one line.

parts.name: Trailing icon
parts.description: An icon after the label, for a direction such as an arrow or a chevron.

parts.name: ButtonCell
parts.description: A small plain button for a secondary action in a table row.

items.text: Use a Button for an action on the current page, such as save, send or open a dialog. To go to another page, render the button as a link.
Give each view one primary or gradient button for its main action. Other actions are plain or links, and icon-only controls in a row, toolbar, field or card are ghost IconButtons.
Label a button with a verb and its object, like Save changes or Invite member. A destructive button repeats its action, and the one beside it says Cancel.
Show an async result on the button itself: Save changes, Saving, Saved, Retry. Give it a fixed width so it does not jump, and explain an error in a message nearby.

items.text: Use a Button Group for a few related actions that belong together, such as share, export and print, or zoom in and zoom out. For one choice that stays selected, use a Segment or a Radio Button Group.
Give the group an aria-label that names what the buttons do together, such as Zoom. It is already a group, but has no name.
Use the same variant and size on every button, and plain buttons in most cases. Shared borders only line up when the buttons have the same height and border.
Name every icon-only button in a group with an aria-label, and keep to one kind of content: all text, all icons, or all icon and text.
Use a Split Button when one action is far more common than its alternatives, and put the alternatives in its menu.
Don't wrap the buttons in extra elements. Only direct children get the joined corners, so a wrapper breaks the edges.
Don't put a primary or gradient button in the group. Joined buttons read as equals, and a view has one main action.
Don't use a group to pick an option. Joined buttons look like a choice but have no selected state, so use a Segment.

components.title: Card
components.description: A bordered container for grouping related content.

parts.description: The surface, in a default, elevated or outlined style, with 16 px padding and gaps (12 px when small) and a 16 px corner radius. It can be horizontal, interactive or selected.

parts.name: CardMedia
parts.description: An image area flush with the top edge, or the left edge in a horizontal card. Put an image inside to fill it; empty, it shows a placeholder, and a ratio replaces the fixed 160 px height.

parts.name: CardHeader
parts.description: A grid for the title, the description and an optional action on the right, with an icon tile or avatar at the left if you want one.

parts.name: CardTitle
parts.description: The title of the card. It renders a div, so put a heading inside it when the card opens a section of the page.

parts.name: CardDescription
parts.description: Secondary text under the title, in the secondary text colour.

parts.name: CardAction
parts.description: Sits top right in the header, for a menu button or one small button. It stays there however long the title runs.

parts.name: CardContent
parts.description: The body of the card. Anything goes in it: text, a list, a form, a chart.

parts.name: CardFooter
parts.description: A row of buttons with a line above it, aligned right, split with a note, equal width or stacked. The line can be removed, and the card drops its bottom padding when a footer is present.

parts.name: CardBody
parts.description: The text column of a horizontal card, next to the media. It carries the vertical padding the card does not have itself.

parts.name: CardIcon
parts.description: An icon tile for the header's leading slot: a tint surface and the icon in the tint text colour.

parts.name: CardMeta
parts.description: A row for a date, a status, a category or people, in small secondary text. It wraps on a narrow card.

parts.name: CardIndicator
parts.description: The radio or checkbox mark at the top right of a selectable card. It is decorative, since the card or its trigger carries the role and checked state.

parts.name: CardTrigger
parts.description: A button that covers the whole card, for a card that also holds other controls. It is the card's only focus stop, and the other controls sit above it.

parts.name: CardFeedback
parts.description: The data states of the whole card: loading (a skeleton), empty, error and denied, each with an optional title, description and action.

parts.name: CardBanner
parts.description: A strip at the top of a card: refreshing while the data stays visible, or an error with Retry when the last data stays visible.

parts.name: CardDragHandle
parts.description: The grip for cards in a sortable list such as a board. Every drag needs a keyboard alternative, such as a Move to menu.

items.text: Use a Card to group the content of one thing, like a project, a plan or a settings section. For a row use Item Card, for one number Metric Card, for nothing to show yet Empty State.
Leave the padding to the card. It matches the chart, stat and metric cards, and the small size suits dense grids, so don't override padding classes.
Put a menu button or one small button in the card action. It stays top right however long the title runs.
To make the whole card the target, set it interactive and give it a role (link, button or radio) and an aria-label.
When a card holds other controls, use a CardTrigger as the one target and raise the other controls above it.
Use plain buttons in a card footer when cards repeat in a grid. A view has one main action, and a gradient button on every card leaves none.
Show data states on the card: CardFeedback for loading, empty, error and no access, CardBanner when old data stays visible while it refreshes or after a failed refresh.
Pick the footer layout by content: end for a normal row of actions, between when a note sits beside them, stretch or stacked for a narrow card.
Don't put a button inside a card that is itself a button or a link. Use a CardTrigger, or keep the card static.
Don't set a white or hex background on a card. The card colour follows the theme and dark mode, and the parts inside read it.

useFor: Grouping the content of one thing, such as a project, a plan, a file or a person
A settings section or a form with a title, a short explanation and a footer of actions
A tile in a grid that opens something, or that someone selects

useInstead.name: Item Card
useInstead.text: a row with an icon, a title, a description, meta and an action

useInstead.name: Metric Card
useInstead.text: one number with its trend and an optional sparkline

useInstead.name: Empty State
useInstead.text: a whole region that has nothing to show yet

keyboard.intro: A static card has no keyboard behaviour. An interactive card is one focus stop, and a CardTrigger is a native button.
keyboard.note: Card does not move the choice between sibling cards. A group of selectable cards does that itself, as in the Plans example.

rows.action: Moves focus to or away from an interactive card or a card trigger. A static card is skipped, and the buttons inside a card keep their own focus stop.
Runs the click handler of the focused interactive card or trigger: opens the card, or toggles a selectable one.

behavior.intro: What the card does with spacing, state, content and motion.

items.title: Spacing
items.text: The default size has 16 px padding and 16 px between header, content and footer, and the small size has 12 px. With a footer, the card drops its bottom padding.

items.title: Surface
items.text: The card clips its content to its corner radius, so media and banners sit flush with the edge. Avatars, rings and marks inside use the card colour for their cut-out edge.

items.title: Interactive
items.text: An interactive card is one target with a hover surface, a pressed surface and an indigo focus ring. Enter and Space run the click handler when the card has focus.

items.title: Card with other controls
items.text: A card with a menu or button uses a CardTrigger that covers it. The trigger is the only focus stop and carries the name, while the other controls sit above it and keep their own stop.

items.title: Selected
items.text: A selected card shows the tint surface, border and text, and keeps them on hover and press. Put the role and checked state on the card or its trigger, and add a CardIndicator for the mark.

items.title: Media
items.text: Media sits flush with the top edge, or the left in a horizontal card, at 160 px high or at a set ratio. A missing image shows an icon and No preview available.

items.title: Data states
items.text: CardFeedback replaces the card content: a skeleton while loading, then an icon, title, description and action. CardBanner sits above content that stays visible, with a spinner or a Retry.

items.title: Names for screen readers
items.text: CardTitle is a div, so put a heading inside it when the card opens a section of the page. An interactive card needs an aria-label when its text is not a good name.

items.title: Motion
items.text: The surface of an interactive card changes quickly, and the selection mark changes colour the same way. The refreshing banner shows a spinning icon.

items.title: Reduced motion
items.text: With reduced motion the surface and the mark change at once, and the spinner in the refreshing banner stands still.

Card.size.description: `default` has 16 px of padding and 16 px between the parts; `sm` has 12 px, for dense grids.

Card.orientation.description: `vertical` stacks the parts, with the media on top. `horizontal` puts the media at the left and the text in a `CardBody` next to it.

Card.interactive.description: Makes the whole card one target: pointer cursor, `tabIndex=0`, hover, pressed and focus states, and Enter and Space run `onClick`. Add a role and an `aria-label`. For a card with other controls, set `tabIndex={-1}` and add a `CardTrigger`.

CardBanner.kind.description: `refreshing` is a quiet strip with a spinning icon and the role `status`; `error` is a red strip with the role `alert`.

items.text: Use a Checkbox for an on or off choice in a form, or to pick several items from a list. For a setting that takes effect at once use Switch, and for one choice out of several use Radio Group.
Give every checkbox a visible label. It is joined to the box, so a click on the text toggles it and a screen reader announces the label with the value.
Write the label as the choice itself, like Email me about new releases. Put a sentence of detail in the description under it.
Use indeterminate on a select-all box while only some rows are chosen. Work it out from the rows and state its scope, like Select all acts on the 5 members shown.
State the rule of a group above it, and put the error under the group, not on one row, like Choose at least two topics.
Show the error on a required box only after the first try to continue, and say what to do, like Accept the terms to create your account.
Don't import CheckboxField in new code. It is a deprecated alias of Checkbox, so use Checkbox with the same props.
Don't build a checkbox from a styled div. The component already handles Space, the focus ring and the larger hit area around the small box.
Don't use a checkbox for a setting that applies at once. A box looks like part of a form that is saved later, so use a Switch.
Don't offer indeterminate as a choice. It only displays a partial selection, and people can never pick it.
Don't show the error before the first try. A red box on load reads as a mistake the person has not made yet.

useFor: An on or off choice in a form, such as accepting terms or remembering a device
Picking several items from a list, such as topics or the rows of a table
A select-all box that shows a mixed state while only some rows are chosen

useInstead.text: a setting that takes effect at once, without a Save button

useInstead.name: Radio Group
useInstead.text: one choice out of several options

useInstead.name: Checkbox Button Group

keyboard.intro: A checkbox is one tab stop. Space toggles it, and Enter does nothing, as on a native checkbox.

rows.action: Moves focus to the next or previous checkbox in the order they are written. A disabled box is skipped.
Toggles the focused checkbox and calls `onCheckedChange`. A box that is `indeterminate` stays a dash until you clear the prop.

behavior.intro: What the checkbox does itself, and what it leaves to the page.

items.title: Two elements, one control
items.text: The visible box has the checkbox role and reports its checked state. Next to it Base UI renders a hidden input that carries the name, value and form state, with the labels copied onto it.

items.title: Controlled or not
items.text: Pass checked and a change handler to own the value, or a default to let the box keep it. The handler gets the new value as a boolean.

items.title: Indeterminate
items.text: Indeterminate shows a dash and reports a mixed state. You set and clear it, and it wins over checked until you remove it, so work it out from the rows you control.

items.title: One component, two shapes
items.text: Without a label, description or error, Checkbox renders the bare box. With one it renders the row, so a click on the text toggles the box, and the box keeps its focus when an error appears.

items.title: Disabled
items.text: Disabled dims the box to 40 %. In a row the label and description dim with it, once, and the row shows the not-allowed cursor.

items.title: Hit area
items.text: The click area reaches 12 px to the sides and 8 px above and below the 16 px box, so a near miss still ticks it.

items.title: Invalid
items.text: An error marks the box invalid, turns the border and focus ring red even when ticked, and shows the message under the row. Without row props, the message is yours to write.

items.title: In a form
items.text: With a name, the box submits its value (default on) when ticked, and nothing when not, unless you set an unchecked value. Required asks for a tick before the form is sent.

items.title: Motion
items.text: Fill and border change quickly. When the box is ticked the check is drawn in slowly, and unticking reverses it quickly.

items.title: Reduced motion
items.text: With reduced motion transitions are limited to colour and opacity, so the check fades in instead of being drawn.

minimalUsage.expected: You see one empty box with the label Email me about new releases. A click on the box or on the text ticks it.

Checkbox.checked.description: Whether the box is ticked. Pass it together with `onCheckedChange` to control the box; use `defaultChecked` to let the box keep the value.

Checkbox.defaultChecked.description: Whether the box starts ticked, when the box keeps its own value.

Checkbox.onCheckedChange.description: Called when the box is ticked or unticked, with the new value as a boolean.

Checkbox.indeterminate.description: Shows a dash instead of the check and sets `aria-checked="mixed"`. Use it on a select-all box while only some rows are chosen. It wins over `checked` until you clear it.

Checkbox.appearance.description: `brand` fills the ticked box with the brand colour; `neutral` fills it with the inverse surface, black in light mode and white in dark mode.

Checkbox.label.description: The visible name of the box, to its right. Joined to the box with `htmlFor` in one `<label>`. Any of `label`, `description`, `error` and `wrapperClassName` makes Checkbox render the row instead of the bare box.

Checkbox.description.description: A second line under the label in 12 px tertiary text. It is part of the label, so it dims with it when the box is disabled.

Checkbox.error.description: The message under the row in the error colour. Sets `aria-invalid` on the box, turns its border red and is linked with `aria-describedby`. It sits outside the label.

Checkbox.wrapperClassName.description: Class names for the row (or, with `error`, for the wrapper around the row and the message). `className` still goes to the box.

Checkbox.disabled.description: The box ignores clicks and keys, is dimmed to 40 % and is skipped by Tab.

Checkbox.readOnly.description: The box keeps its value and cannot be ticked or unticked. It is announced as read-only.

Checkbox.required.description: A tick is needed before a form that holds the box can be sent. It does not draw anything by itself: pass `error` to show the message.

Checkbox.id.description: The id of the hidden input. With `label` it joins the label to the box (from `useId` unless you give one); otherwise point the `htmlFor` of a `Label` at it.

Checkbox.name.description: The name of the field when a form is sent.

Checkbox.value.description: The value sent with the form when the box is ticked. The default is `on`.

Checkbox.uncheckedValue.description: The value sent with the form when the box is not ticked. By default an unticked box sends nothing, like a native checkbox.

Checkbox.form.description: The id of the form that owns the hidden input, for a box that is rendered outside the form.

Checkbox.inputRef.description: A ref to the hidden `<input>`. The component also copies `aria-label` and `aria-labelledby` onto it.

Checkbox.parent.description: Marks a box that controls a group of child boxes. WunderUI does not ship a Checkbox Group, so leave it off and work out `checked` and `indeterminate` from your rows, as the Select all example does.

Checkbox.nativeButton.description: Set it to `true` when `render` swaps the element for a native `<button>`.

Checkbox.render.description: Replaces the element of the box with another tag or component. Accepts an element or a function that returns one.

Checkbox.className.description: Extra classes, merged with the box's own. A string, or a function of the state. Use it for spacing such as `mt-0.5`, not to recolour the box.

Checkbox.style.description: Inline style for the box, an object or a function of the state.

parts.name: Switch
parts.description: The track, with the switch role: 32 by 18 px by default, 24 by 14 px small. Grey when off, brand, neutral or muted when on, with a hit area that reaches 12 px sideways and 8 px up and down.

parts.name: Thumb
parts.description: The round knob, which slides with a slight overshoot and reverses mid-way if clicked again. While saving it shows a spinner, and Switch renders it for you.

parts.name: Label
parts.description: The text that names the setting, a Label linked to the switch or the title of a Selector Item, and clicking it toggles the switch. Name the setting, never the state.

items.text: Use it for one setting that is on or off and takes effect at once, such as email notifications. For a choice that is saved later with a form, use a Checkbox.
Give every switch a visible label and link it to the switch. A click on the text then toggles it, and a screen reader announces the name with on or off.
Name the setting, not the state: Email notifications, not On. The switch role already tells screen readers whether it is on.
Set the saving state while a request runs. The knob shows a spinner and clicks are ignored until the save ends.
When a save fails, set the switch back to its previous value and say so in a message with a retry, like Couldn't save. Try again.
Use the small size in dense rows such as table cells, and the default size in forms and settings.
Don't mark a switch invalid. It has no wrong value, and a failed save is an error of the request, so put it in the message.
Don't use a Switch to choose between two named options such as Monthly and Yearly. That is a choice, not on or off, so use a Radio Group.
Don't ask people to press a Save button after a Switch. A switch that waits for a button is a Checkbox.

useFor: One setting that is on or off and takes effect at once, such as notifications
A row of settings, each with a title and a short description
A master switch that turns a group of settings on or off

useInstead.name: Checkbox
useInstead.text: a choice that is saved later with a form, or several choices from a list

useInstead.name: Radio Group
useInstead.text: one choice out of several named options

useInstead.name: Segment
useInstead.text: switching between views, with one always selected

useInstead.name: Selector Item
useInstead.text: a whole row with a title, a description and a switch

keyboard.intro: A switch is one tab stop. It is a button in all but name, so Space and Enter both toggle it.

rows.action: Moves focus to the next or previous switch in the order they are written. A disabled switch is skipped.
Toggles the focused switch and calls `onCheckedChange`. A switch that is `saving` or `readOnly` ignores both keys.

behavior.intro: What the switch does itself, and what it leaves to the page.

items.title: Two elements, one control
items.text: The visible track is a switch element, with a hidden checkbox input beside it that carries the name, value and form state. Labels are copied onto it so page checkers see a named input.

items.title: Controlled or not
items.text: Pass a checked value and a change handler to own the value, or a default to let the switch keep it. There is no indeterminate state.

items.title: Names
items.text: A Label linked to the switch names it and makes the text a click target. Inside a Selector Item the title names it, and otherwise you pass an aria-label.

items.title: Hit area
items.text: The area that takes a click reaches 12 px to the sides and 8 px above and below the track, so a near miss still toggles it.

items.title: Hover and pressed
items.text: An off track gets a rim on hover and a darker grey while pressed, and a brand track darkens on hover and again when pressed. Disabled is the rest look at 40 % opacity.

items.title: Saving
items.text: Saving puts a spinner on the knob, marks the switch busy and makes it read-only until you clear it. Set the switch to its new value first, then clear saving when the request ends.

items.title: Save failed
items.text: A failed save is not an invalid value, so the switch is not marked invalid. Set it back to its previous value and show a message with a retry next to it, as a Selector Item error does.

items.title: In a form
items.text: With a name the switch submits its value (default on) when on, and nothing when off unless you set an unchecked value. Required asks for it to be on before the form is sent.

items.title: Motion
items.text: The track changes colour quickly and the knob slides with an overshoot, swinging slightly past the end and settling. A second click reverses it from wherever it is.

items.title: Reduced motion
items.text: With reduced motion the knob no longer slides but jumps to the other end, the colour change stays, and the spinner stays as a still glyph.

minimalUsage.expected: You see one small switch, turned on, with the label Email notifications. A click on the switch or the text turns it off.

parts.description: The group: a radio group that holds the chosen value and lays the options out in a grid with an 8 px gap. Name it with an aria-label, and mark the whole group invalid if needed.

parts.name: RadioGroupItem
parts.description: One round option, 16 px across, with its own value. Its hit area reaches 12 px to the sides and 8 px above and below the circle, so a near miss still selects it.

parts.name: Dot

parts.name: Label

parts.name: Description

items.text: Use a Radio Group when people choose exactly one option from a short list they should see at once. For a long list use a menu, and for options shown as buttons use a Radio Button Group.
Name the group with a visible label and aria-labelledby, or with an aria-label. A screen reader announces the name when focus enters the group.
Give every option a visible label and join it with htmlFor and id, so a click on the text also chooses it.
Choose a sensible default when one exists. Once an option is chosen it cannot be cleared, so an empty start only helps when the choice is required.
Put the error on the group: mark it invalid and write one message under it. Do not repeat the message on every row.
Use Selector Item with a RadioGroupItem as its control when each option needs a title, a description and a price, such as plans.
Don't use two radios for on and off. A single setting that is on or off is a Switch or a Checkbox.
Don't validate before the first try. A red group on load reads as a mistake that was not made yet.
Don't split one choice into several groups, or put an unrelated control between the options. People expect the arrow keys to stay inside one group.

useFor: Exactly one choice from a short list, such as a delivery method or a plan
Options with a description, so people can compare them before they choose
A list that should stay visible instead of hiding in a menu

useInstead.name: Checkbox
useInstead.text: several choices from a list, or one on or off choice

useInstead.name: Switch
useInstead.text: a setting that takes effect at once

useInstead.name: Radio Button Group
useInstead.text: one choice shown as a row of buttons

useInstead.name: Segment

keyboard.intro: The group is one tab stop: Arrow keys move inside it and Tab moves out. Enter does nothing; only Space and Arrow keys choose.

rows.action: Moves focus into the group, to the chosen option or, with none chosen, to the first one, and out of it again. Other options are not tab stops.
Moves focus to the next option and chooses it. From the last option it wraps to the first.
Moves focus to the previous option and chooses it. From the first option it wraps to the last.
Chooses the focused option, for example after Tab put focus on a group with nothing chosen.

behavior.intro: What the group does itself, and what it leaves to the page.

items.title: One choice
items.text: The group holds a single value. Choosing an option replaces the old one, and only you can clear the choice again, not people.

items.title: Controlled or not
items.text: Pass a value and a change handler to own the choice, or a default value to let the group keep it. Each option is matched by its own value.

items.title: Arrow keys choose
items.text: Moving focus with an arrow key also chooses the option, like a native radio group, while Tab alone only moves focus. Home and End do nothing, and a disabled option is skipped.

items.title: Names
items.text: The group needs a name from an aria-label or aria-labelledby. Each radio is named by its label: a Label tied by htmlFor and id, the title of a Selector Item, or an aria-label.

items.title: Hit area
items.text: The area that takes a click reaches 12 px to the sides and 8 px above and below the 16 px circle.

items.title: Invalid
items.text: Marking the group invalid turns every radio red together, also the chosen one, and announces the error once. Write the message under the group and point to it with aria-describedby.

items.title: Disabled
items.text: Disabling the group dims every option to 40 %, and disabling one item dims that option only. A label is not dimmed for you, so add the opacity class to it.

items.title: Tint tone
items.text: The tint tone is for a radio on a surface that turns indigo when the option is chosen, such as a selected option card. The filled circle then takes the tint colours of that hue.

items.title: In a form
items.text: With a name on the group the chosen value is sent with the form. Required asks for a choice before the form is sent.

items.title: Motion
items.text: Fill and border change with a quick colour transition. The dot appears with the fill and has no motion of its own.

items.title: Reduced motion
items.text: With reduced motion transitions are limited to colour and opacity. Nothing in the group moves, so nothing else changes.

parts.description: The visible name of the field, joined to the input so a click on it focuses the field. A search field with no room for a label takes an aria-label instead.

parts.name: Input
parts.description: The single-line field: a native input with a 1 px border and an 8 px corner, 32, 36 or 40 px high. With content inside it, an InputGroup draws the border and focus ring instead.

parts.name: Leading content
parts.description: An icon or short text before the value, such as a mail icon or https://. It isn't interactive and uses the tertiary text colour.

items.text: Use an Input for one line of free text: a name, an email address, a search term. Use a Textarea for several lines, and a Select or Combobox for a choice from a known list.
Give every Input a visible label. A placeholder disappears with the first keystroke and is not a name; a search field may use an aria-label.
Pick the type and autocomplete that match the value (email, password, cc-number). The browser then offers the right keyboard and fills the field in.
Mark a wrong value with an error and say what to do: Enter an email address like name@company.com, not Invalid input. Keep what the person typed.
Show the error after the person leaves the field or sends the form, not on the first keystroke. A red field on load reads as a mistake that has not been made yet.
Keep the label a noun (Work email) and put the rule in the helper below it as a full sentence.
Make every password field that a person types by hand revealable, and set autocomplete to current-password on sign-in or new-password on sign-up.
Don't import TextField or PasswordField in new code. They are deprecated aliases of Input; use Input with the same props.
Don't use a placeholder as the label, and don't put the format example only there: it is gone once the field is filled.
Don't size a field with height classes. Use the size prop (sm, default, lg), so a field and a Button of the same size line up in both densities.
Don't disable a value people need to read or copy. A read-only field can be focused and copied; a disabled one can't, and it is dimmed.
Don't use a number input for codes, phone numbers or card numbers. Use text with numeric input mode, so leading zeros survive.

useFor: One line of free text, such as a name, an email address or a search term
A value with a known format, such as a URL, an amount or a card number
A field with something attached, such as an icon, a unit, a shortcut or a copy button

useInstead.name: Textarea
useInstead.text: text over several lines, such as a message or feedback

useInstead.name: Number Field

useInstead.name: Select

useInstead.name: OTP Field
