useInstead.text: several sections that people read in turn and that can be open together

useInstead.name: Sidebar
useInstead.text: the pages of the product, where each choice is a route

keyboard.intro: The tabs are native buttons with one tab stop. Tab enters the row once and arrow keys move inside it.
keyboard.note: By default arrow keys only move focus, and Enter or Space selects. Turn on activate on focus to select a tab as soon as it gets focus.

rows.action: Moves focus into the row, onto one tab, and out of it again to the panel. The other tabs are not tab stops.
In a horizontal row: moves focus to the next or previous tab. From the last tab it wraps to the first, and from the first to the last, unless `loopFocus` is off.
In a vertical list: moves focus to the next or previous tab, with the same wrapping. Left and Right do nothing there.
Moves focus to the first or the last tab.
Selects the focused tab and shows its panel. A disabled tab can take focus but cannot be selected.

behavior.intro: What the tabs do with the selected value, the panels, the looks, overflow and motion.

items.title: Selected value
items.text: Tabs holds the selected value, which you start with a default or control yourself. Each tab and its panel share one value, a string or number.

items.title: Panels are not kept
items.text: Only the selected panel is rendered. A hidden panel leaves the DOM, so its text is missing from server HTML and form values inside it are lost unless you keep it mounted.

items.title: Two looks
items.text: The default look draws every tab as a bordered button, with the selected one tinted indigo. The line look draws bare labels over a 1 px baseline, with a 2 px indigo underline under the selected one.

items.title: Sizes
items.text: Size sets the height of the row and its tabs: small, medium and large are 32, 36 and 40 px at compact density and 36, 40 and 44 px at comfortable, like Button.

items.title: Focus
items.text: Keyboard focus shows the shared focus ring on a bordered tab, and inside the label on a line tab. The panel also takes focus, so a long panel scrolls with the keyboard.

items.title: Overflow
items.text: A row with more tabs than fit scrolls sideways, without a scrollbar, instead of widening the page.

items.title: Vertical
items.text: In vertical orientation the list stacks beside the panel. Bordered tabs fill the list's width with the label at the start, and the line look draws a rail on the left.

items.title: Disabled tabs
items.text: A disabled tab can still be reached with arrow keys and is announced as disabled, but it can't be selected. It uses the tertiary text colour and ignores the pointer.

items.title: Motion
items.text: Switching tabs only fades which tab shows its underline, and the grey baseline never moves. Tab colours fade too, and panels swap without animation.

items.title: Reduced motion
items.text: With reduced motion the underline appears without the fade. Colour changes stay.

minimalUsage.expected: Two bordered tabs, Overview selected and tinted indigo, with the text 12 open tasks, 3 due this week under them. Click Activity, or arrow to it and press Enter, to swap the text.

TabsList.variant.description: `default` draws every tab as a bordered button. `line` draws bare labels over a baseline, with an underline under the selected one.

TabsList.size.description: The height of the row and of its tabs: `sm` (the default), `md` or `lg`, the Button heights.

TabsList.shape.description: `rounded` (the default) gives the bordered tabs 8 px corners, `pill` rounds them fully. It has no visible effect on the `line` look.

TabsTrigger.count.description: A number after the label, in an indigo pill that is shown on the active tab only. In the `line` variant an inactive tab also draws a grey underline on hover.

components.title: Agenda
components.description: A time-ordered list of scheduled events.

parts.name: Agenda
parts.description: The bordered, rounded list, one row per item in array order. It does not sort by time.

parts.name: Row
parts.description: One entry with 16 px padding and a line below it, except the last. Rows are text only, with no click or focus state.

parts.name: Time
parts.description: The time string as written, in a narrow fixed column on the left. A long value wraps.

parts.name: Colour bar
parts.description: A 2 px bar the height of the row, in the item's colour (the primary colour if none is set).

parts.name: Title
parts.description: The title in semibold text. A long title wraps.

parts.name: Description
parts.description: An optional line under the title in smaller secondary text, for a place, a person or a status.

items.text: Use an Agenda for a short, read-only list of what happens when. For past events in order use Timeline; for rows with guests, a menu or a click, use Agenda Event.
Sort the items by time before you pass them in. The list renders them in array order and never reorders.
Use one short time format across the list, such as 09:30. The time column is 56 px wide, so a range such as 09:00 to 10:30 wraps onto a second line.
Set the colour to a CSS variable such as var(--brand-secondary), not a hex. Only a token follows the theme and dark mode.
Say what an entry is in its title or description, like Cancelled or Review. The bar is only a colour and does not reach people who cannot tell hues apart.
Don't make the Agenda clickable by wrapping it in a link or button. Rows have no hover or focus state; use Agenda Event when an entry opens something.
Don't put the Agenda inside another bordered card. It already has its own border and background, so a second box doubles the lines.

useFor: A short, read-only list of what happens when, such as a day's meetings
A programme or run of show with one time per row
A compact Today list on a dashboard or in a side panel

useInstead.name: Agenda Event
useInstead.text: rows with guests, a menu or an action that opens the event

useInstead.name: Timeline
useInstead.text: events that already happened, with a status and an exact date

useInstead.name: Calendar
useInstead.text: picking a day or browsing a month

behavior.intro: What the list does with order, content, the DOM and motion.

items.title: Order is yours
items.text: Items render in array order. The list does not sort by time or group by day.

items.title: Time is plain text
items.text: The time is printed as written, not parsed: no time zone, no 12 or 24 hour format, no relative time. The column is 56 px wide; longer values wrap.

items.title: Colour is an inline style
items.text: The colour goes straight into the bar's background. Use a token such as var(--success), since a hex ignores theme and dark mode; the default is primary.

items.title: Rows are static
items.text: A row has no hover, pressed, focus or selected state and is not in the tab order, but its text can be selected. For a row that opens something, use Agenda Event.

items.title: Plain markup
items.text: The list and rows are plain divs, with no list or time elements, so a screen reader reads each row as text, time first. Put a heading near the list.

items.title: Long text
items.text: Long titles and descriptions wrap and the bar grows with the row. Nothing is truncated.

items.title: Empty list
items.text: With no items the list draws an empty bordered box with no height. Show an Empty State when there is nothing to list.

items.title: Motion and reduced motion
items.text: Nothing animates: rows appear, change and leave without a transition. There is nothing to reduce.

minimalUsage.expected: You should see a bordered list of three rows, each with its time on the left, a coloured bar and a title with a description.

Agenda.items.type: { id: string; time: string; title: string; description?: string; color?: string }[]
Agenda.items.description: The entries, in the order they appear. Each has an `id` (the React key, unique in the list), a `time` shown as written, a `title`, an optional `description` under it and an optional `color`, a CSS colour for the bar, best a token such as `var(--success)`. Without `color` the bar is `var(--primary)`.

Agenda.className.description: Extra classes for the list, merged after the defaults. Use it to set a width such as `w-80`, or a margin. The list fills the width of its parent otherwise.

components.title: Action Bar
components.description: A bar of bulk actions for a selection. It sits where you place it, so fix it to the bottom of the page yourself if it should float.

parts.name: ActionBar
parts.description: The bar itself: a bordered card row with a shadow. It does not position or animate itself, so place it yourself, for example above a list or at the bottom of a table card.

parts.name: Label
parts.description: The text such as 3 selected, in 14 px medium. Without a label the separator goes too.

parts.name: Separator
parts.description: A 1 px vertical line between the label and the actions. It shows only when there is a label.

parts.name: Actions
parts.description: The buttons, in one row with an 8 px gap. Use small plain buttons and icon buttons; 8 px of right padding keeps a last icon button even.

items.text: Use an Action Bar for bulk actions on rows someone has selected: export, archive, delete. For actions that are always available, use Toolbar.
Show the bar only while something is selected and put the count in the label, like 3 selected. The count tells people what the buttons act on.
Keep to two to four actions that all make sense for any selection. Put the destructive one last.
Give icon-only buttons an aria-label. The bar has no name of its own, so each button must carry its own.
Place the bar yourself: above the list, or fixed and centred near the bottom. Reserve its room so content does not jump when it appears.
Switch to icon buttons on narrow screens. The bar does not wrap, and a label with three text buttons is wider than 320 px.
Don't run a destructive bulk action straight from the bar. Confirm it in an Alert Dialog that says how many items go, like Delete 3 invoices?
Don't use the bar for one-off page actions such as Save or Share. Those belong in the page header or a toolbar.
Don't leave the bar on screen when nothing is selected. A bar saying 0 selected with live buttons invites mistakes.

useFor: Bulk actions on rows someone selected in a list or table, such as export, archive or move
Actions on a multi-selection of files, messages or cards
A short set of actions that all apply to the whole selection

useInstead.name: Toolbar
useInstead.text: actions that are always available, with or without a selection

useInstead.name: Dropdown Menu
useInstead.text: the actions of one row, behind a button

useInstead.name: Toast
useInstead.text: a confirmation after the action ran, such as 3 files archived

keyboard.intro: The bar is a plain container, so the browser provides focus and activation for the buttons inside it.
keyboard.note: The bar has no toolbar role, so arrow keys do not move focus between its buttons.

rows.action: Moves focus to the next or previous action in the bar, in the order they are written.
Runs the focused action.

behavior.intro: What the bar does, and what it leaves to the page that uses it.

items.title: Shown by you
items.text: The component only draws the bar. Render it while something is selected, and clear the selection once an action has run.

items.title: Position
items.text: The bar does not position itself. In a flex row or a centred wrapper it hugs its content; otherwise it fills the width of its parent.

items.title: Label and separator
items.text: With a label, the bar shows it and a separator before the actions. Without one, both are gone and the actions start at the left padding.

items.title: No name, no role
items.text: The bar has no role or name and is not announced when it appears. Name icon-only buttons and announce the selection change yourself, for example in a polite live region.

items.title: Width
items.text: The content does not wrap. A bar with a label and three text buttons is wider than 320 px, so show icon buttons on narrow screens.

items.title: Motion
items.text: The bar has no motion of its own. The examples fade and slide it in from below when the first row is selected.

items.title: Reduced motion
items.text: With reduced motion on, the examples skip the slide and the bar appears in place.

minimalUsage.code:
import { ActionBar } from "@/components/ui/action-bar"
import { Button } from "@/components/ui/button"

export function SelectionBar() {
  return (
    <ActionBar label="3 selected">
      <Button variant="plain" size="sm">
        Archive
      </Button>
      <Button variant="plain" size="sm">
        Delete
      </Button>
    </ActionBar>
  )
}
minimalUsage.expected: You should see one bar with the label 3 selected, a vertical line and two buttons, Archive and Delete.

ActionBar.label.description: The text before the actions, usually the count of selected items such as `3 selected`. When it is set, a vertical separator follows it. Leave it out for a bar of actions only.

ActionBar.children.description: The actions, laid out in one row with an 8 px gap. Use small plain buttons and icon buttons.

ActionBar.className.description: Extra classes for the bar, merged with its own. Use it for the width and the placement, such as `w-fit`. The bar takes no other props: `style`, `id` and event handlers are not passed on.

components.title: Carousel
components.description: A horizontally scrollable row of items with arrow controls.
components.props: function Carousel({ children, className, label, navigationShape, showArrows, slideSize, autoPlay, index, onIndexChange, drag, }: CarouselProps): React.JSX.Element;

props.name: autoPlay
props.description: Advances one slide every this many milliseconds and starts over after the last one. It stops while the pointer or the keyboard focus is inside, while the tab is hidden and with reduced motion. 0 or undefined turns it off.

props.name: drag
props.description: Drag the slides left or right with the mouse or a pen; touch already swipes. The row follows the pointer and, on release, springs to the nearest slide (a quick flick goes one slide further). Turn it off when the slides hold content that ne…

props.name: index
props.description: The slide the row shows, for dots and thumbnails that control it (controlled).

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name of the scrolling region.

props.name: navigationShape
props.description: Shape of the two arrow buttons: a rounded square or a circle.

props.name: onIndexChange
props.description: Called with the number of the slide the row now shows.

props.name: showArrows
props.description: Show the two arrow buttons. Turn them off when dots or thumbnails do the navigating.

props.name: slideSize
props.description: "auto" keeps every slide at its own width, "full" makes each slide as wide as the row.

parts.name: Carousel
parts.description: A row with a previous button, the slide strip and a next button. It snaps to each slide, takes the width of its parent and pauses autoplay while the pointer or focus is inside.

parts.name: Previous button
parts.description: A plain icon button on the left, square or round, that steps one slide back. It stays visible but disabled on the first slide, and is hidden but keeps its place when nothing overflows.

parts.name: Slide strip
parts.description: The focusable region, named by its label. It scrolls with arrow keys, swipes on touch and drags with a mouse or pen, and announces the visible items, such as 2 to 4 of 6, once a scroll stops.

parts.name: Slide
parts.description: Each child sits in a snap point. Slides keep their own width, or each fills the strip in full-width mode.

parts.name: Next button
parts.description: The same icon button on the right. It steps one slide forward and is disabled, not hidden, on the last slide.

items.text: Use a Carousel for a row of similar items people browse, such as project cards, screenshots or template previews. When every item matters or needs comparing, use a grid.
Set the label to what the row holds, such as Recent projects. The default Carousel tells nobody what is inside.
Keep the arrows beside the row. They never sit on top of a card, so a slide can hold its own buttons and links.
Drive dots, thumbnails or a counter through the index and its change handler instead of scrolling the strip yourself. The carousel springs to the slide and reports the one in view.
Show how many slides there are, with a counter like Slide 2 of 5, dots or thumbnails. Arrows alone do not tell people where they are.
Offer a pause button next to autoplay, and use autoplay for images, not text. It already pauses on hover, focus, a hidden tab and reduced motion, but moving slides are hard to read.
Don't put the only way to reach important content inside a carousel. People skip it, and a grid shows everything at once.
Don't leave drag on when slides hold controls that need the mouse, such as a slider. Turn it off; touch still swipes.
Don't autoplay in a dashboard or on a page people read. Moving content competes with the text.

useFor: A row of similar items that people browse, such as project cards, screenshots or template previews
One slide at a time, for a gallery or a short product tour driven by dots, thumbnails or buttons
A row of cards that is wider than its container, on a narrow screen

useInstead.name: Card
useInstead.text: a grid of cards when every item matters or the numbers need comparing side by side

useInstead.name: Tabs
useInstead.text: a few different views that people switch between

useInstead.name: Stepper
useInstead.text: the steps of a process that someone moves through in order

keyboard.intro: The slide strip is a focusable region, so the browser scrolls it with arrow keys. The two arrows are buttons.

rows.action: Moves focus through the previous button, the slide strip, the controls inside the slides and the next button, in that order. An arrow at either end of the row stays focusable.
With focus in the slide strip, scrolls the row to the left or right. It snaps to the start of a slide when it stops.
Presses the focused arrow and steps one slide. On a disabled arrow nothing happens.

behavior.intro: What the carousel does with its slides, its arrows and the scroll, and what it leaves to you.

items.title: Slides
items.text: Each child snaps to the start. A slide keeps its own width by default, so a row of cards shows part of the next one, and full-width mode shows one slide at a time.

items.title: Arrows
items.text: An arrow steps to the next slide, or back to the nearest one, and stays focusable but disabled at an end. When nothing overflows, both arrows are hidden but keep their place.

items.title: Scroll and snap
items.text: The strip snaps to slides. Arrows and the index move it with a spring that settles in about a second, and touch, the wheel and a drag take over at once.

items.title: Drag
items.text: With a mouse or pen the row follows the pointer after 5 px and springs to the nearest slide on release. A quick flick goes one further, and the click ending a drag opens nothing.

items.title: Controlled index
items.text: The index scrolls to a slide and the change handler reports the one in view, so dots, thumbnails, a counter and buttons stay in step. You write those controls yourself.

items.title: Autoplay
items.text: Autoplay moves one slide per interval and starts over after the last. It waits while the pointer or focus is inside or the tab is hidden, and does not run with reduced motion.

items.title: Names for screen readers
items.text: The strip is a region named by its label, and after a scroll stops a polite live region reads the visible items, such as 2 to 4 of 6. Name your own dots and thumbnails.

items.title: Motion
items.text: The row scrolls with a critically damped spring of about a second. The arrows fade when they become disabled, and your dots and thumbnails should animate colour only.

items.title: Reduced motion
items.text: With reduced motion the row jumps to its target at once and autoplay does not start.

minimalUsage.expected: You see a row of project cards between two arrow buttons. The cards are wider than the row, so the next arrow works and the previous one is disabled.

Carousel.children.description: The slides. Each child becomes one slide in its own snap point, so pass one element per slide, such as a card.

Carousel.label.description: The accessible name of the slide strip, such as `Recent projects`. The default is `Carousel`.

Carousel.slideSize.description: `auto` keeps every slide at its own width, so part of the next slide shows. `full` makes each slide as wide as the strip, one slide at a time.

Carousel.showArrows.description: Shows the previous and next buttons beside the row. Turn them off when dots, thumbnails or your own buttons do the navigating.

Carousel.navigationShape.description: The shape of the two arrow buttons: `rounded` is a rounded square, `circle` is a circle.

Carousel.index.description: The slide the row shows, for dots, thumbnails and buttons that control it. A new value scrolls to that slide with the spring, and the row stays free to scroll on its own.

Carousel.onIndexChange.description: Called with the number of the slide the row now shows, counting from 0. It also fires when someone swipes, drags or uses an arrow, so the controls outside stay in step.

Carousel.autoPlay.description: Advances one slide every this many milliseconds and starts over after the last one. It stops while the pointer or the keyboard focus is inside, while the tab is hidden and with reduced motion. `0` or leaving it out turns it off.

Carousel.drag.description: Drags the slides left or right with a mouse or a pen. The row follows the pointer and springs to the nearest slide on release; a quick flick goes one slide further. Touch swipes either way. Turn it off when slides hold controls that need the mouse.

Carousel.className.description: Extra classes for the row, merged with its own `flex w-full items-center gap-3`. Use it for a width such as `max-w-xl` or a margin.

components.title: Brand Logo
components.description: The logo of a product or service (Slack, GitHub, Stripe …) at 16, 20 or 24 px, for list rows, integrations and buttons.
components.props: function BrandLogo({ name, size, label, className, ...props }: BrandLogoProps): React.JSX.Element;

props.name: name
props.description: Which brand.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name. Defaults to the brand name; pass "" when the text beside it already names the brand.

props.name: size
props.description: `sm` 16 px (beside small text and in buttons), `md` 20 px (default, list rows), `lg` 24 px.

props.name: name
props.description: Which product mark to draw.

parts.name: BrandLogo
parts.description: An svg with the image role and the brand's name, 16, 20 or 24 px. With label="" it is hidden from screen readers.

parts.name: BrandMark
parts.description: The bare mark on a 20 px grid, decorative unless it gets an aria-label. The same component as integration mark; integration logo puts it in a 36 px tile with a Tooltip.

items.text: Use Brand Logo to show which product a row, a card or an action is about: an integration, a connected account or a share target.
Pass label="" when the brand's name is written beside the logo, so a screen reader does not read it twice.
Use the 16 px size in buttons and beside small text, 20 px in list rows.
Don't recolour a logo or put it on a coloured tile. Brand colours are the brands' own; the one-colour logos already follow the text colour.
Don't use a brand logo for a payment method. Payment Logos draws Visa, Klarna and the others on their cards.
Don't use a logo alone as a button. Put it in a Button with a label, or give an Icon Button an aria-label.

useFor: An integrations or connected-accounts list
A button that acts on another product, such as Share to Slack
The source of a record, a message or a file

useInstead.name: Payment Logos
useInstead.text: a card or payment method

useInstead.name: Icon Tile
useInstead.text: a category or a feature of your own product

useInstead.name: Avatar
useInstead.text: a person or a team

behavior.intro: What the logo does with its name, size and colours. It is display only: no hover, focus or keyboard behaviour.

items.title: An image, not a control
items.text: BrandLogo is an svg with the image role and the brand's name, so it has no focus stop. Put it in a Button when the logo stands for an action.

items.title: Colour and dark mode
items.text: Brand colours stay as the brand draws them. OpenAI, GitHub, Linear, Vercel and X are one colour and use the current text colour, so they turn white in dark mode.

items.title: Brands
items.text: BRAND_NAMES lists the 36 brands; BRANDS gives each a category and one line of text, ready for an integrations list.

items.title: Old names
items.text: IntegrationMark is the same component as BrandMark, and IntegrationLogo, IntegrationName and INTEGRATION_NAMES keep working.

items.title: Motion and reduced motion
items.text: Nothing is animated, so there is nothing to reduce under reduced motion.

minimalUsage.expected: You see the Slack logo at 20 px beside the word Slack.

BrandLogo.name.description: The brand, one of `BRAND_NAMES`, such as `Slack`, `GitHub` or `Stripe`.

BrandLogo.label.description: The accessible name. The brand name by default; pass `""` when the text beside the logo names the brand.

BrandLogo.className.description: Added to the svg, for a margin or a colour for the one-colour logos.

components.title: Empty State
components.description: Placeholder shown when a list or search has no results.

props.name: variant
props.description: Frame style — mirrors the Figma Empty State "Style" variants.

parts.name: EmptyState
parts.description: A centred block of icon, title, description and action, with 40 px of padding. Four frames are available: dashed (the default), outline, none, or a muted background fill.

parts.name: Icon
parts.description: The icon, drawn in a round 48 px well at 24 px. Pass a Lucide icon.

parts.name: Title
parts.description: One short line on what is missing, such as No invoices yet. It renders as a paragraph, not a heading, so it does not change the outline of the page.

parts.name: Description
parts.description: The text under the title: why the place is empty, or what will appear here.

parts.name: Action
parts.description: Below the text, usually one Button that fills the empty place or undoes the filter. It takes any node, also a row of two buttons or a link.

items.text: Say what is missing, why and what to do next, then offer one action: No invoices yet, Invoices appear here as soon as the first one is sent, and New invoice.
For a search without results, name the query and offer a way out: No results for Anders, with a Clear search action.
For a failure, say what failed and offer the retry as the action: Couldn't load invoices with Try again. Show the pending state on the button while it runs.
Use the frameless look inside a card or panel that already has a border, and the dashed default where the empty state stands on the page.
Wrap an empty state that appears after typing in a status region, so a screen reader announces the change.
Don't show a bare No results line. Without a reason and a next step, an empty place looks broken and leaves people stuck.
Don't use it while data is still loading. A Skeleton shows that something is on its way; an empty state says that nothing is.
Don't offer two equal calls to action. One primary button, with at most a plain secondary one or a link to help.

useFor: A list, table or search that has nothing to show, for the first time or after a filter
A region that failed to load, or that the person may not open, with a way on

useInstead.name: Skeleton
useInstead.text: content that is still loading

useInstead.name: Alert
useInstead.text: an error or a notice next to content that is still there

useInstead.name: Toast
useInstead.text: a short message that something happened and needs no action

behavior.intro: What the empty state does with content, the page and motion.

items.title: Not a region
items.text: EmptyState is a plain div with no role, and its title is a paragraph. Put it inside the empty section, and wrap it in a status region when the result changes while someone types.

items.title: Frame
items.text: Dashed draws a dashed 1 px border with a 16 px radius, outline the same with a solid border, default no frame at all, and background a muted fill with a 24 px radius.

items.title: Size
items.text: The empty state fills the width of its container, centres its content and keeps 40 px of padding on every side. Give it a container with a width, such as a card or a column.

items.title: Action
items.text: The action sits 12 px below the text and can be any node. Buttons in it keep their own focus ring and keyboard behaviour.

items.title: Motion and reduced motion
items.text: The empty state has no motion of its own. If you animate the swap, use the base duration and entrance curve on opacity and transform, with a reduced motion fallback.

minimalUsage.expected: You see a dashed frame with a round icon, the title No invoices yet, a line of text and a New invoice button, all centred.

EmptyState.title.description: One short line on what is missing. Required.

EmptyState.description.description: Why the place is empty or what will appear here, in one or two sentences.

EmptyState.icon.description: A Lucide icon, drawn in a round 48 px well above the title.

EmptyState.action.description: The node below the text: a Button, a row of buttons or a link.

EmptyState.variant.description: The frame: `dashed` (default), `outline`, `default` without a frame, or `background` with a muted fill.

components.title: File Tree
components.description: An indented list of folders and files: a tree with arrow-key navigation whose folders open and close, and onSelect reports the chosen file or folder.
components.props: function FileTree({ data, "aria-label": ariaLabel, onSelect, selectedId, className }: FileTreeProps): React.JSX.Element;

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Accessible name of the tree.

props.name: onSelect
props.description: Called when a file or folder is activated (click, Enter or Space).

props.name: selectedId
props.description: The selected node (controlled). Without it the tree keeps its own selection.

parts.name: FileTree
parts.description: A bordered panel that draws the data as rows, named Files by default. Top-level folders start open and deeper ones closed, and one row is the tab stop while the arrow keys move between visible rows.

parts.name: Folder row
parts.description: A tree item with a chevron, a folder icon and the name. Choosing it opens or closes its children and selects it; Right opens it or enters the first child, Left closes it.

parts.name: File row
parts.description: A tree item with a file icon and the name, cut with an ellipsis when too long. Choosing it selects it and calls your select handler, and the selected row has a subtle fill.

parts.name: Children
parts.description: The nested rows, indented one step per level. While closed they are inert and the arrow keys skip them, so focus never lands inside a closed folder.

items.text: Use a File Tree to show a folder structure people look through, such as the files of a template or an export. For items people search, sort or select in bulk, use Table.
Give every node a unique, stable id. It is the React key and the selection value, and a reused id mixes up which folders are open.
Mark a folder with a children array, even an empty one. A node without children is drawn as a file.
Keep the choice in your own state when something else on the page depends on it, such as an open file. Without it the tree keeps its own selection.
Name the tree with an aria-label when the page has more than one, such as Project files. The default name is Files.
Don't use it for multiple selection, drag and drop, renaming or icons per file type. It selects one row at a time and draws the same two icons.
Don't expect it to load children on demand. The tree draws the data it gets, so a folder that is still loading needs its own placeholder row.

useFor: The files of a template, an export or a repository, shown beside a preview
A folder structure people browse with the keyboard
A nested list with one chosen row, where the choice opens something else

useInstead.name: Table
useInstead.text: items people search, sort or select in bulk

useInstead.name: Accordion
useInstead.text: sections of text that open one at a time

useInstead.name: Collapsible
useInstead.text: a single show-more panel

keyboard.intro: The tree follows the WAI-ARIA tree pattern: one row is the tab stop, and the arrow keys move between the rows that are visible.

rows.action: Moves focus into the tree on one row: the last focused one, else the selected one, else the first. The next press leaves the tree.
Moves focus to the next or previous visible row. Rows inside a closed folder are skipped.
On a closed folder, opens it. On an open folder, moves focus to its first child. On a file, nothing happens.
On an open folder, closes it. Otherwise moves focus to the parent folder.
Moves focus to the first or the last visible row.
Selects the focused row and calls `onSelect`. On a folder it also opens or closes it.
Type-ahead: a letter moves focus to the next visible row whose name starts with it. One letter, no word search.

behavior.intro: What the tree does with state, content, focus and motion.

items.title: Selection
items.text: One row is selected at a time, and choosing a folder selects and toggles it. Pass a selected id to control the selection, and update it in the select handler.

items.title: Initial state
items.text: Top-level folders start open and deeper folders closed. After that the tree keeps its own open folders, and there is no prop to open one from outside.

items.title: Roving tab stop
items.text: Only one row has the tab stop. If a collapse hides the focused row, the nearest visible parent takes it, so focus never lands inside a closed folder.

items.title: Closed folders are inert
items.text: The rows of a closed folder stay in the DOM but are inert: they cannot be focused or clicked, and assistive technology skips them.

items.title: Empty folders
items.text: A folder with an empty children list draws a chevron and opens to nothing. There is no empty row, so add a placeholder node if people should see that it is empty.

items.title: Long names
items.text: A name that does not fit is cut with an ellipsis. Give the tree a width with a class name, since the panel is as wide as its parent by default.

items.title: Icons and metadata
items.text: Folders show a folder icon and files a file icon. There is no slot for another icon, a badge or a size column.

items.title: Focus
items.text: The focused row shows an indigo outline on the row only, not around the folder and its children.

items.title: Opening and closing
items.text: Children slide and fade in and out. Opening takes the base duration with the entrance curve, closing is a step faster, and the chevron turns 90 degrees on the fast duration.

items.title: Reduced motion
items.text: With reduced motion the children appear and disappear without sliding and the chevron does not turn. Hover and selected fills still change.

minimalUsage.expected: You see a bordered panel with an open src folder holding two files, and package.json below it.

FileTree.data.description: The nodes of the tree. A node is `{ id, name, children? }`: a node with a `children` array is a folder (empty or not), one without is a file. Ids must be unique.

FileTree.aria-label.description: The accessible name of the tree. The default is `Files`; give each tree on a page its own name.

FileTree.selectedId.description: The `id` of the selected row, for a controlled tree. Update it in `onSelect`. Without it the tree keeps its own selection.

FileTree.onSelect.description: Called with the node that was chosen by click, Enter or Space. A folder is reported too, as it is selected and toggled.

FileTree.className.description: Extra classes for the panel, merged with its own. Use it for the width, or to drop the border and fill (`border-0 bg-transparent`) when the tree sits in a pane that has its own.

components.title: Floating TOC
components.description: A table of contents for an article, with a marker that follows the section in view. It does not stick by itself: put it in a `sticky` container to keep it on screen.

props.name: scrollContainer
props.description: The element that scrolls the sections, if it is not the page.

parts.name: FloatingToc
parts.description: A nav named On this page with one link per section. It is not sticky itself, so place it in a sticky column.

parts.name: Entry
parts.description: A link to each section's id, indented 12 px per depth. The current one is darker and medium weight, and is marked as the current location.

parts.name: Active marker
parts.description: A 2 px bar on the left line that glides to the current entry. A fainter one previews the entry under the pointer or focus.

items.text: Use a Floating TOC beside a long page with several headed sections, such as documentation or a policy. For switching between separate views, use Tabs.
Give every section an id that matches its item. The links and the scroll spy find sections by that id, and a missing one is never marked.
Pass the scroll container when the sections scroll inside a panel rather than the page. Otherwise the spy watches the window and the marker stands still.
Put it in a sticky column yourself. The component draws the list and the marker, not its position.
Keep labels short, one line each, and in page order. A wrapped entry throws the marker out of line.
Leave the active section unset unless you track it yourself. Once you set it, the scroll spy is off and the marker stops following the reader.
Don't use it as the main navigation of a site. It lists the sections of one page and shows where the reader is.

useFor: Documentation and guides with several headed sections
Policies, terms and release notes that people scan for one part
Long single pages where the reader needs to see where they are

useInstead.name: Tabs
useInstead.text: peer views that people switch between, one at a time

useInstead.name: Breadcrumb
useInstead.text: the path to the current page in a site

useInstead.name: Stepper
useInstead.text: the steps of a flow with a fixed order

keyboard.intro: The entries are plain links, so the browser handles focus and activation. The article's scroll container is focusable too.

rows.action: Moves focus to the next or previous entry. The focused entry previews the marker, as hover does.
Follows the focused link: the section scrolls into view, the marker moves to the entry at once and `onSelect` is called. Space does not activate a link.
With focus in the scroll container of the article (give it `tabIndex={0}`), scrolls the article. The marker follows the section in view.

behavior.intro: How the contents react to scrolling, clicks and motion.

items.title: Scroll spy
items.text: The current section is the last one that has scrolled past a line a quarter of the way down. At the end of the scroll, the last section wins, even a short one.

items.title: Click
items.text: A click scrolls the section into view and moves the marker at once. The marker stays put until the scroll ends, so it doesn't flicker through the sections in between.

items.title: Scroll container
items.text: By default the spy watches the window and a click updates the address bar hash. Pass a scroll container to watch that element instead, and the address bar stays unchanged.

items.title: Controlled
items.text: Set the active id yourself and the spy turns off: the marker only moves when you change it. A click still scrolls and calls the select handler, so update the id there.

items.title: Missing ids
items.text: An item whose section isn't on the page is listed but never becomes current. Clicking it follows the plain link.

items.title: Hover and focus
items.text: The entry under the pointer or focus gets a fainter preview marker, showing where a click would go. It disappears on leave and blur.

items.title: Depth
items.text: Depth indents an entry by 12 px per level. Nothing else changes: no collapsing, no limit.

items.title: Marker motion
items.text: The marker glides between entries at the base duration and the preview marker moves faster. Text colour changes quickly.

items.title: Reduced motion
items.text: With reduced motion the marker jumps to the new entry and a click scrolls at once instead of smoothly. Colour changes stay.

minimalUsage.expected: You see a scrolling article with two sections and two links beside it. The marker sits on the section being read and moves as you scroll or click.

FloatingToc.items.description: The entries, in page order. `id` is the id of the section it points to, `label` is the text and `depth` indents it, 12 px per level.

FloatingToc.scrollContainer.description: A ref to the element that scrolls the sections, when it is not the page. The spy and a click then work inside it.

FloatingToc.activeId.description: The id of the current entry, for a contents you track yourself. Setting it turns the scroll spy off.

FloatingToc.onSelect.description: Called with the id of the entry that was clicked, after the marker has moved.

FloatingToc.className.description: Extra classes for the `<nav>`, merged with its own. Use it for the width or the spacing around the list.

components.title: Holo Card
components.description: A card with a soft glow that follows the mouse.

parts.name: HoloCard
parts.description: A card with a border, 16 px padding and a 16 px radius that clips its content. It tracks the pointer position for the glow, and you pass a class for the width.

parts.name: Glow
parts.description: A radial gradient 320 px across in the primary colour at 25 %, fading out. It fades in on hover, follows the pointer and sits behind the content; the figure keeps it on.

parts.name: Content
parts.description: The children, placed above the glow. Anything goes: text, an icon tile, a badge, buttons.

items.text: Use a Holo Card to make one or two showcase items stand out, such as a featured plan on a landing page. For everyday content and dashboard tiles, use Card.
Use it once or twice per view. When every card glows, none of them stands out.
Tint the glow by setting the primary colour on a wrapper, not with a gradient of your own. It follows brand and dark mode, and everything inside that uses the primary colour changes with it.
Keep the card complete without the glow. It appears only under a mouse pointer, so touch and keyboard users never need it.
Put a real link or Button inside for the action, and set the card's width with a class.
Don't rely on the glow to show the card is clickable. It is decoration with no focus state, no role and no tab stop.
Don't expect a tilt or 3D effect. The card never moves or rotates; only the glow under the pointer changes.

useFor: A featured plan on a pricing section or a landing page
One announcement or upgrade offer on a dashboard
A showcase item that should reward a closer look with the mouse

useInstead.name: Card
useInstead.text: everyday content, dashboard tiles and anything that is a list of equals

useInstead.name: Hover Card
useInstead.text: a preview that opens beside a trigger on hover

useInstead.name: Alert
useInstead.text: a message about the state of the page or a form

behavior.intro: How the card reacts to the pointer, focus and motion. It has no keyboard interaction of its own.

items.title: The glow
items.text: The glow follows the mouse and is 320 px across at any card size. It starts at the middle of the card, so it never jumps in from a corner.

items.title: Hover only
items.text: The glow shows while the pointer is over the card and fades out when it leaves. Touch screens have no hover and a keyboard never moves the pointer, so neither gets the effect.

items.title: No focus, no role
items.text: The card is a plain div: not focusable and not announced. Any link or button inside keeps its own focus ring and role.

items.title: Colour
items.text: The glow mixes the primary colour at 25 % with transparent, so it follows brand and dark mode. Set the primary colour on a wrapper to tint it.

items.title: Fade
items.text: The glow fades in and out quickly. Its position isn't animated: it jumps to the pointer on every move.

items.title: Reduced motion
items.text: Nothing on the card moves and the glow is a colour change, so reduced motion changes nothing. To drop the effect anyway, hide the glow with a class; the card is complete without it.

minimalUsage.expected: You see a bordered card with two lines of text. A soft glow in the primary colour follows the mouse while it is over the card.

HoloCard.children.description: The content of the card, placed above the glow.

HoloCard.className.description: Extra classes for the card, merged with its own. Use it for the width. Do not use it to change the glow; set `--primary` on a wrapper.

components.title: Item Card
components.description: A generic row card: icon, title, description, meta, action.

props.name: deletedAt
props.description: Type=trash — deletion line shown in red, no menu/checkbox.

props.name: thumbnail
props.description: Image preview instead of the icon tile.

props.name: color
props.description: Tint of the cover band.

props.name: cover
props.description: Icon, logo or image in the middle of the cover.

props.name: meta
props.description: One short line under the name.

props.name: deletedAt
props.description: Type=trash — deletion line shown in red, no menu/checkbox.

props.name: thumbnail
props.description: Image preview instead of the icon tile.

props.name: color
props.description: Tint of the cover band.

props.name: cover
props.description: Icon, logo or image in the middle of the cover.

props.name: meta
props.description: One short line under the name.

parts.name: ItemCard
parts.description: One framed row on the card surface: 1 px border, 8 px radius, 12 px padding and 12 px between its parts. It is a plain div with no hover, focus or click state of its own.

parts.name: Icon tile
parts.description: A 40 px indigo tint square with an 8 px radius and a 20 px icon in the tint text colour. It shows when you pass an icon.

parts.name: Title
parts.description: The title in 14 px semibold, cut to one line with an ellipsis.

parts.name: Description
parts.description: The description under the title in 13 px secondary text, also cut to one line.

parts.name: Meta
parts.description: A short fact on the right in 12 px tertiary text, such as a size or a date. It never shrinks, and a Badge works here too.

parts.name: Action
parts.description: One control at the far right, usually a Button or an icon button. It never shrinks and keeps its own focus and click behaviour.

parts.name: ItemCardGroup
parts.description: A bordered box with a 12 px radius and 8 px padding that stacks several cards 8 px apart, for a set that belongs together.

parts.name: ItemCardCover
parts.description: A clickable tile: a 96 px cover band in a tint, with an icon, logo or image in the middle, then the name and one line of detail. It is a button. It replaces ProjectCard.

parts.name: ItemCardFile
parts.description: A file tile: a 120 px preview (an icon on a tint, or an image), the name and the details, with an optional selection checkbox, a menu button and a deleted state. It replaces FileCard.

items.text: Use an ItemCard for an object on its own row, like a file, a connected app or a project, with one action. Use a Table for rows people compare by column and List View for a plain list in one frame.
Put the action in the action slot as a Button or icon button. The card takes no click handler, so the row itself isn't interactive.
Give an icon button an aria-label that names its object, such as More options for Checkout redesign, so the buttons of a set can be told apart.
Keep the title and description short, or give the full text another way. Both are cut to one line with an ellipsis.
Use the meta slot for a short fact with its unit, such as 2.4 MB or 2d ago, or for a status Badge.
Don't wrap each ItemCard in a Card. It draws its own border and padding; for a set, use ItemCardGroup.
Don't put more than one control in the action slot. Two buttons next to a long title leave no room for the text.

useFor: A file, a connected app or a project that stands on its own row
A row with one action, such as Download, Connect or a menu
A short set of related objects, framed together with ItemCardGroup

useInstead.name: List Group
useInstead.text: a plain list of rows in one frame, divided by lines

useInstead.name: Card
useInstead.text: an object with media, several parts and a footer

useInstead.name: Data Table
useInstead.text: many rows that people sort, filter or compare by column

keyboard.intro: The card is a plain container, not a control. Only what you put in the action slot can take focus.
keyboard.note: Arrow keys do not move focus between cards. Each button is a separate Tab stop, in the order the cards are written.

rows.action: Moves focus to the next or previous control in the cards, for example the action button of each card in turn.
Presses the focused action button or icon button.

behavior.intro: What the card does with state, content, the DOM and motion.

items.title: A plain row
items.text: The card is one plain div with a rest look only: no hover fill, pressed or selected look, or focus ring. Figma also draws navigational, selectable and actionable cards, which React doesn't build.

items.title: One line of text
items.text: The title and description truncate to an ellipsis instead of wrapping. The meta and action never shrink, so the text gives way first.

items.title: Icon tile
items.text: The icon sits in a 40 px square with an 8 px radius in the indigo tint, and every svg inside is sized to 20 px. The tile doesn't shrink.

items.title: Group
items.text: ItemCardGroup is a column with 8 px between cards, 8 px padding and a 12 px radius. The cards keep their own border inside it.

items.title: Density
items.text: The card ignores the density setting, so its padding and tile stay the same in compact and comfortable. A Button in the action slot follows density as usual.

items.title: Motion and reduced motion
items.text: The card adds no animation, so there is nothing to reduce. A Button or icon button in the action slot brings its own press feedback and turns it off for reduced motion.

minimalUsage.expected: You see one bordered row with an indigo file icon, the title Q3 report.pdf over its description, and 2d ago on the right.

ItemCard.title.description: The name of the object, in 14 px semibold. It is cut to one line with an ellipsis. Required.

ItemCard.description.description: A line under the title in 13 px secondary text, such as a size or an owner. Cut to one line. Leave it out for a card with a title only.

ItemCard.icon.description: An icon, shown in a 40 px indigo tint tile at the left. Pass a Lucide icon element; its size is set by the tile. Leave it out and the card has no tile.

ItemCard.meta.description: A short fact on the right in 12 px tertiary text, such as `2d ago`. It can also be a Badge. It never shrinks.

ItemCard.action.description: One control at the far right, usually a Button or an icon button. It never shrinks. The card itself has no click handler, so the control carries all interaction.

ItemCard.className.description: Classes for the card, for example a width such as `w-80`. They are merged after the card's own classes.

ItemCardGroup.children.description: The cards of the set. The group stacks them with 8 px between them.

ItemCardGroup.className.description: Classes for the frame, for example a width such as `w-80`.

ItemCardCover.name.description: The name, cut to one line. Required.

ItemCardCover.meta.description: One short line under the name, such as a task count or a due date.

ItemCardCover.color.description: The tint of the cover band: `indigo` (default), `blue`, `purple`, `pink`, `red`, `orange`, `yellow`, `green` or `alternative`.

ItemCardCover.cover.description: An icon, logo or image in the middle of the band. The icon takes the tint's text colour.

ItemCardCover.onClick.description: Called when the tile is pressed.

ItemCardCover.className.description: Extra classes on the tile, for example a width.

ItemCardFile.name.description: The file name, cut to one line. Required.

ItemCardFile.meta.description: The details under the name, such as the size and the date.

ItemCardFile.icon.description: The icon in the preview, a file icon by default.

ItemCardFile.color.description: The tint behind the icon: `red` (default) or any other tint.

ItemCardFile.thumbnail.description: The address of an image that replaces the icon tile.

ItemCardFile.selected.description: Shows the selected border. With `onSelectedChange` the checkbox is visible while selected.

ItemCardFile.onSelectedChange.description: Adds a checkbox in the top left corner of the preview, shown on hover, focus and while selected.

ItemCardFile.deletedAt.description: A red line such as Deleted 3 days ago. It hides the menu button.

ItemCardFile.onMenu.description: Adds a menu button at the end of the details.

ItemCardFile.onOpen.description: Makes the preview one button named Open plus the file name.

components.title: Timeline
components.description: A vertical sequence of dated, dot-connected events.

props.name: compact
props.description: Smaller dots and text, for milestones and long lists.

props.name: orientation
props.description: "vertical" stacks the entries, "horizontal" lays them out in a row with the time above each dot.

props.name: avatar
props.type: { src?: string; initials?: string; color?: AvatarColor }
props.description: Actor avatar (Type=event).

props.name: badge
props.description: Trailing badge/label on the title row (Type=step).

props.name: children
props.description: Extra content below the title (comment excerpt, reactions, attachments …).

props.name: last
props.description: The last entry of the list: no connector line below it.

props.name: object
props.description: Small object chip under the title (Type=event) — e.g. project name.

props.name: status
props.description: Status dot (Type=step): tone + icon.

props.name: avatar
props.type: { src?: string; initials?: string; color?: AvatarColor }
props.description: Actor avatar (Type=event).

props.name: badge
props.description: Trailing badge/label on the title row (Type=step).

props.name: children
props.description: Extra content below the title (comment excerpt, reactions, attachments …).

props.name: last
props.description: The last entry of the list: no connector line below it.

props.name: object
props.description: Small object chip under the title (Type=event) — e.g. project name.

props.name: status
props.description: Status dot (Type=step): tone + icon.

parts.name: Timeline
parts.description: Draws the entries, stacked in a column or laid out in a row, and joins them with a line. Compact makes dots, text and gaps smaller, and it is a plain div, not a list.

parts.name: Dot
parts.description: The marker of an entry: a 24 px circle (16 px when compact) in the entry's colour, with an icon or a small point inside. An avatar replaces it.

parts.name: Title
parts.description: The title of the entry in semibold text. It can be any React node, so keep it to a short sentence.

parts.name: Timestamp
parts.description: The timestamp in small tertiary text, printed as written. It sits next to the title in a column and above the dot in a row.

parts.name: Description
parts.description: The detail of the entry, in secondary text under the title.

parts.name: Connector
parts.description: A 1 px line in the border colour from one dot to the next. The last entry has none, and it isn't numbered because it runs between two dots.

items.text: Pass a stable id for every entry. It is the React key, so a list that grows at the top keeps its rows.
Give every timestamp a date or a time with its unit, such as Nov 9, 09:14 or 3 min ago. It prints as written, so format it yourself and use one style in the whole list.
Say the status in words, in the title or description: Tests failed, not just a red dot. Colour and icon are decoration for people who can see them.
Pass dot colours as tokens, such as var(--success) or var(--destructive). The glyph inside switches between white and dark so it stays readable.
Use compact for long lists and for a Timeline inside a small card. Dots, text and gaps shrink so more entries fit.
Don't use a horizontal Timeline for more than four or five entries. Each entry gets an equal share of the width, so a long row squeezes the text.
Don't put long paragraphs, buttons or links in the title or description. For one rich entry with a comment, object chip or attachments, use a Timeline Event.
Don't write times like recently or a while ago. People can't tell which entry came first.

useFor: The steps of an order, a shipment or an application, in the order they happen
Project milestones and release histories drawn from data
A deploy or an audit log, where each entry has a time and a short result
A compact activity feed with a person at each entry

useInstead.name: Agenda
useInstead.text: the events of a day with start and end times

useInstead.name: Stepper
useInstead.text: a progress indicator that people move through, such as a checkout

useInstead.name: Run Timeline
useInstead.text: the steps of an agent run with duration, tokens and input or output

behavior.intro: What the Timeline does with its data, its direction, the dot colour and motion.

items.title: Entries are data
items.text: Pass the items. Each needs an id and a title, and description, timestamp, icon, avatar and colour are optional, while the id is only the React key and isn't shown.

items.title: Vertical and horizontal
items.text: Vertical stacks entries in a column with the dot on the left. Horizontal lays them in a row with equal widths, so at about 120 px per entry scroll it or go vertical on narrow screens.

items.title: Compact
items.text: Compact shrinks the dot to 16 px, its icon to 10 px, the text to 12 px and the gap between entries from 24 to 16 px. An avatar keeps its own size.

items.title: The colour of the dot
items.text: The colour is any CSS colour, a token included, and defaults to primary. The glyph inside switches between white and dark to keep WCAG contrast, also when a token changes in dark mode.

items.title: No status prop
items.text: Completed, current, upcoming, failed and cancelled aren't props. Build them from colour and icon: green with a check, the default dot, a quiet colour with a dashed circle, red with a cross.

items.title: A person instead of a dot
items.text: A small Avatar replaces the dot and sits on the line the same way. Use it for an activity feed, and name the person in the title.

items.title: Plain markup
items.text: It is a plain div, not a list, and nothing in it is a control. Give it a heading nearby and put the status in the text, because the colour of a dot isn't announced.

items.title: Motion and reduced motion
items.text: It adds no animation: entries appear at once and nothing moves when the data changes. There is nothing to reduce, so no reduced-motion fallback is needed.

minimalUsage.expected: Two entries in a column, each with a dot, a bold title, the date next to it and the description below. A line joins the two dots.

Timeline.items.description: The entries, in order. Each is `{ id, title, description?, timestamp?, icon?, avatar?, color? }`: `id` is the React key, `title` and `description` are React nodes, `timestamp` is printed as written, `icon` goes inside the dot, `avatar` replaces the dot and `color` is the fill of the dot.

Timeline.orientation.description: `vertical` stacks the entries in a column. `horizontal` lays them out in a row, each with an equal share of the width and the time above its dot. The default is `vertical`.

Timeline.compact.description: Smaller dots, icons, text and gaps, for long lists and small cards. The default is off.

Timeline.className.description: Extra classes for the root element, merged after the defaults, for example a width or `min-w-[520px]` for a row inside a scroll container.

components.title: Widget
components.description: A generic dashboard widget shell: header, body, footer.

parts.name: Widget
parts.description: The frame of one dashboard tile: a bordered card with a 16 px radius, 16 px of padding and 16 px between header, body and footer.

parts.name: Header
parts.description: A row with the title and description on the left and the action on the right. It only renders when there is a title or an action, so a description alone doesn't show.

parts.name: Title
parts.description: The title as an h3 in bold 16 px text, so heading order stays intact under a level-two page heading.

parts.name: Description
parts.description: The description under the title in small secondary text: the period, scope or unit of the data.

parts.name: Action
parts.description: The action at the right end of the header, usually a plain View all button or an icon button with an aria-label.

parts.name: Body
parts.description: The content. The body grows to fill the tile, so in a grid row the footers of tiles with different bodies line up at the bottom.

parts.name: Footer
parts.description: The footer below a divider line: a note on the data such as Updated 2 minutes ago, or one link.

items.text: Put widgets under a level-two page heading. The title renders as an h3, so the heading order stays intact.
Keep the header to one action, such as a plain View all button or an icon button with an aria-label. More than one belongs in a menu.
Keep the frame in loading, empty and error states and swap only the body. The tile keeps its title and place, so the page doesn't jump.
Set the width on the box around the Widget or with a class. It fills its container, so a grid cell or a maximum width decides how wide it is.
Use the footer for a note about the data or one link, such as Updated 2 minutes ago or Manage plan.
Don't set a description without a title or an action. The header isn't rendered then, so the description doesn't appear.
Don't put a Card or another bordered box in the body. The Widget is already the frame, so use rows, dividers and Progress bars inside it.
Don't use a Widget for content with media, a custom header or one press target for the whole tile. Use a Card.

A group of small summaries in a grid, each with an action in the header and a note in the footer
A frame for a body you compose yourself, loading, empty and error states included

useInstead.name: Card
useInstead.text: content with media, a custom header, or a tile that is one press target

useInstead.name: List Panel
useInstead.text: a titled list with the loading, empty and error states already built in

useInstead.name: Empty State
useInstead.text: the message inside a body that has nothing to show

behavior.intro: What the Widget does with its header, its body, its width and its states.

items.title: A frame, not a layout
items.text: The Widget draws the border, card surface and spacing, and nothing else. The body is yours and takes any content, and there are no variant, size or state props.

items.title: The header appears with a title or an action
items.text: The header row renders when there is a title or an action. A description is only a second line of the title, so it needs one of the two, and with neither you get just the body and footer.

items.title: Width and height
items.text: The Widget fills its container and has no width prop. Figma names three widths, Compact 280, Default 360 and Wide 560 px, which you set with a class, and in a grid row the body grows to align footers.

items.title: Spacing
items.text: The body sits 16 px from the border, the same as the corner radius, so a framed box inside stays square or lightly rounded. The footer sits 16 px below the body with 12 px under its divider.

items.title: States are content
items.text: Loading, empty, error, stale and the other Figma body states aren't props. Keep the header and swap the body: a Skeleton, an Empty State, or a message with Retry for a failure.

items.title: Nothing is interactive
items.text: The Widget has no hover, press or focus state and takes no keyboard input. Buttons in the action, body or footer are normal controls with their own focus order.

items.title: Plain markup
items.text: The Widget is a plain div, not a landmark or a list, and the title is the only heading in it. Name a group of widgets with a level-two heading above them.

items.title: Motion and reduced motion
items.text: The Widget adds no animation. A Skeleton or Progress bar in the body brings its own motion and its own reduced-motion fallback.

minimalUsage.expected: A bordered tile with the bold title Visits, the description Last 7 days under it and the number 12,480 below.

Widget.title.description: The heading of the tile, rendered as an `<h3>` at the left of the header. With `title` or `action` set, the header row renders.

Widget.description.description: A second line under the title in small secondary text. It shows only when `title` or `action` is set.

Widget.action.description: A control at the right end of the header, usually a plain `View all` button or an icon button. It renders the header row even without a title.

Widget.footer.description: Content below a divider line: a note about the data or one link. The line and the space only render when the footer is set.

Widget.children.description: The body of the tile: a list, a chart, a meter or the content of a state. It grows to fill the height of the tile.

Widget.className.description: Extra classes for the frame, merged after the defaults. Use it for the width, for example `w-full max-w-[360px]`.

components.title: Segment
components.description: A single-select toggle group, like a compact tab bar, with a pill or a rounded-corner track.

props.name: activation
props.description: `auto` (default): the arrow keys move focus and choose the option. `manual`: the arrow keys, Home and End only move focus; Enter or Space chooses. Use it where a wrong choice has a cost (a permission, a payment).

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Names the group for screen readers, e.g. "Version".

props.name: shape
props.description: `pill` (default) or `rounded` for the square-cornered version.

props.name: slide
props.description: The selected option's pill slides to the next option instead of switching. It moves with `transform` only (the pill is laid out at its final size and animated from the old one), so it costs no layout, and it stays put when the user prefers…

props.name: wrap
props.description: The options wrap to a second row when the track is wider than its container (a phone) instead of running past the edge. One row looks the same as without it. Off by default.

parts.name: Segment
parts.description: The track: a grey bar, as wide as its options, labelled for assistive technology. Size sets its height, and shape sets the corners: a full pill, or 8 px with concentric options.

parts.name: Option
parts.description: One button per entry in the options array, with the selected option as the single tab stop. Hover uses the page fill, pressed the subtle fill, and a disabled option is dimmed and skipped by keys.

parts.name: Selected pill
parts.description: The white pill behind the selected option, drawn only when sliding is on, and it moves from the old option to the new one. Without sliding the selected option paints the white fill itself.

parts.name: Icon
parts.description: An icon you pass with an option, shown before the label at 14 or 16 px. Give a Lucide icon a 1.5 stroke, and it takes its option's text colour.

items.text: Use it to switch the view or scope of one piece of content: day, week, month, list or grid, monthly or yearly. For separate panels use Tabs, and for on or off use a switch.
Keep it to two to five options with short labels. The track does not wrap or scroll, so five long labels are wider than a phone.
Pass an aria-label, for example Time range. It names the tab list, and the options only carry their own labels.
Give an icon-only option a visually hidden label such as List. Without it the option has no accessible name.
Pick the size by place: the smaller ones inside a card or chart header, the larger ones to line up with a Button. Those heights follow the density tokens.
Turn on sliding when the options are neighbours the eye should follow, such as a period. Use the plain version for a control that changes rarely.
Don't pass a value that matches no option. The first enabled option becomes the tab stop, but none looks selected.
Don't use a Segment to open panels with their own content and URL, because it renders no panels. Tabs owns the panels.
Switch to manual activation when a choice is hard to undo or costly, such as a permission level or billing interval. Keep the default when choosing only changes a view.

useFor: Switching the view or scope of one piece of content: a period, a layout, a billing interval
A choice between two to five short options that are all visible at once
A control in a card, chart or table header that changes what is shown below it

useInstead.name: Tabs
useInstead.text: separate panels of content, each with its own heading or URL

useInstead.name: Toggle
useInstead.text: a single option that is on or off

useInstead.name: Radio Button Group
useInstead.text: one choice in a form that is submitted with the rest of the fields

useInstead.name: Checkbox Button Group
useInstead.text: a choice of several options at once

keyboard.intro: The segment is one tab list with a single tab stop on the selected option. Arrow keys move and choose as they go, and with manual activation they only move focus while Enter or Space chooses.
keyboard.note: Up and Down do nothing, typing a letter does not jump to an option, and a disabled option is skipped. The rows below describe the default automatic activation.

rows.action: Moves focus into the segment, onto the selected option (or onto the first enabled option when `value` matches none), and out of it again. The other options are not tab stops.
Selects the next enabled option and moves focus to it. From the last option it wraps to the first.
Selects the previous enabled option and moves focus to it. From the first option it wraps to the last.
Selects the first or the last enabled option and moves focus to it.
With `activation="manual"`: only moves focus to the next, previous, first or last enabled option (wrapping). The selection stays on the chosen option until Enter or Space.

Chooses the focused option, as a click does. With `activation="auto"` the arrow keys have already chosen it, so you need these only when your `onValueChange` refused the change. With `activation="manual"` this is how a focused option is chosen.

behavior.intro: What the segment does with its value, options, sliding pill, screen readers and motion.

items.title: Controlled
items.text: The segment keeps no state of its own, so you pass the value and a change handler. A click or key reports the option's value, and the selection changes when you pass the new value back.

items.title: Options
items.text: Options are an array with a value, a label and optionally an icon or disabled flag, and the label can be any node. Array order is visual order, and the track never wraps or scrolls.

items.title: Badge or counter in an option
items.text: Put a Badge or counter in the label node as the direct, last child of the option, after the label text, such as `Unread` and a counter. Only then does the option give it the same 4 px from the top, bottom and right edge, and the option's gap to the label. A badge wrapped in another element, or placed before the label, keeps the plain padding and the gaps are uneven.

items.title: Width
items.text: The track is as wide as its options. To fill a row, add a class that makes the track full width and gives each option an equal share.

items.title: Sizes and shapes
items.text: The smallest sizes are 32 and 28 px, and the two largest follow the control tokens: 36 and 40 px at compact density, 40 and 44 px at comfortable. Pill rounds fully, rounded uses 8 px.

items.title: Sliding pill
items.text: With sliding, one pill sits behind the selected option and moves to the next. Until the first paint the selected option fills itself, so server HTML never shows a track without a selection.

items.title: Activation
items.text: Automatic activation moves focus and chooses at once, so the change handler fires on each key press. Manual only moves focus and Enter or Space chooses, which suits choices with a cost.

items.title: Resizing
items.text: The pill follows a resize of the track, such as a wider container or a late font, without sliding. It slides only when the value changes.

items.title: Focus
items.text: Keyboard focus draws the standard focus ring on the option: an indigo border and a 2 px light indigo ring, following the option's radius. The sliding pill stays behind it.

items.title: Assistive technology
items.text: The track is a labelled tab list and each option a tab, but no panels are rendered. Name the content it switches nearby and announce changes in a live region.

items.title: Motion
items.text: The pill moves with a transform, and the text colour and hover fill change quickly.

items.title: Reduced motion
items.text: With reduced motion the pill does not slide. It jumps to the new option, and the selection still changes at once.

minimalUsage.expected: You see a grey pill-shaped bar with Day, Week and Month, with Week selected in white. Click Month or arrow to it and the fill moves there.

Segment.options.description: The options in the order they are shown: `{ value, label, icon?, disabled? }`. `value` is a unique string, `label` any node, `icon` an element drawn before the label (a Lucide icon with `strokeWidth={1.5}`), `disabled` dims the option and removes it from the keys.

Segment.value.description: The `value` of the selected option. Required: the segment is controlled. A value that matches no option leaves nothing selected and makes the first enabled option the tab stop.

Segment.onValueChange.description: Called with the `value` of an option when it is clicked or reached with an arrow key, Home or End. Store it and pass it back as `value`.

Segment.size.description: `xs` (32 px, chart filters), `sm` (28 px), `md` (the default, the Button height) or `lg`. `md` and `lg` follow the density tokens.

Segment.shape.description: `pill` (the default) rounds the track and the options fully. `rounded` gives the track 8 px corners and the options a concentric radius.

Segment.slide.description: Slides the selected pill to the next option with a transform instead of switching at once. On by default; pass `slide={false}` to switch at once. It does not slide when the user prefers reduced motion.

Segment.aria-label.description: Names the tab list for screen readers, for example `Time range`. Pass it every time: the options only carry their own labels.

Segment.className.description: Extra classes for the track, for example the classes that make it fill its row.

Segment.activation.description: What the arrow keys, Home and End do. `auto` (default) moves focus and chooses the option at once. `manual` only moves focus; Enter or Space chooses. Mouse and touch are unaffected.

parts.name: Select
parts.description: The root. It holds the chosen value and open state and renders nothing itself, and it reads option labels from its items, so the field shows Germany for the value de before the list ever opens.

parts.name: SelectTrigger
parts.description: The field: a button that shows the chosen option and opens the list, 36 px high with an indigo border while open. Give it a visible label or an aria-label.

parts.name: SelectValue
parts.description: The text in the field: the chosen option's label, or the placeholder in a quieter colour while nothing is chosen. An option with an icon shows the icon here too.

parts.name: Chevron
parts.description: The 16 px chevron at the right of the field. It is part of the trigger and hidden from assistive technology.

parts.name: SelectContent
parts.description: The list panel. It opens below the field at the same width and scrolls when it runs out of room, and its 12 px corner is concentric with the 8 px rows inside its 4 px padding.

parts.name: SelectItem
parts.description: One option, 32 px high. Its value is what the select holds and its children are the label, with an optional icon in front; the highlighted option gets the page fill.

parts.name: Check
parts.description: A 16 px check at the right of the chosen option.

items.text: Give the select a visible label, joined to the trigger with an id. The placeholder is a hint such as Select a status, not the name of the field.
Set a placeholder for a field that starts empty and say what is wanted: Select a status, not just Select.
Keep the labels short and parallel. The list is as wide as the field, and a long label is cut off.
Mark an invalid select as invalid on the trigger, and say why in a line under it, linked with aria-describedby.
Don't use it for a long list. Past a dozen options people scroll instead of reading; a Combobox lets them type.
Don't use it for two or three options that fit on the screen. Radio buttons show every option at once and need one click less.
Don't use it for actions. Choosing an option sets a value; a menu of actions belongs in a Dropdown Menu.

Inline: Give every trigger an aria-label that names what is chosen, such as Sort order or Status of WUI-482. There is no visible label, and the announced value alone doesn't say what the choice is for.
Inline: Don't use it as a form field. Without a border it doesn't look like an input; use Select with a label inside a Field.
Inline: Don't let long labels push the sentence around. The trigger is as wide as the current label, so text after it moves when the value changes; keep labels about the same length.

useFor: Choosing one option from a short, fixed list, such as a status, a role or a sort order
A form field that shows the chosen option in the field itself
Lists of about 3 to 12 options that people know by sight
Inline (`SelectTrigger variant="inline"`): a value inside a sentence, such as Show comments from the last 30 days
Inline: a compact choice in a toolbar, a card title or a table row, such as a sort order, a period or a status

useInstead.name: Radio Group

useInstead.name: Dropdown Menu
