keyboard.intro: The field is a native button, so the browser handles focus. Once the list is open, focus is inside it and the arrow keys move between options.

rows.action: On the field: opens the list and highlights the chosen option, or the first one.
Moves the highlight to the next or previous option. It stops at the ends.
Moves the highlight to the first or the last option.
Type-ahead: typing the start of a label moves the highlight to the next option that begins with it.
Chooses the highlighted option, closes the list and returns focus to the field.
Closes the list without a change and returns focus to the field.
Closes the list when focus leaves it.

behavior.intro: What the select does with its value, focus, the list and motion.

items.title: Options
items.text: The field is a combobox, the list a listbox and each option an option. The chosen option is marked selected and shows a check.

items.title: The label in the field
items.text: The field shows the chosen option's label, not its value. Labels come from the item children, or from an items prop when options are built inside another component, and an icon shows in the field too.

items.title: Placeholder
items.text: The placeholder shows in the tertiary text colour until an option is chosen.

items.title: Modal
items.text: A select is modal by default: the page behind it is inert and does not scroll while the list is open. Turn modal off to keep the page usable, as the previews here do.

items.title: Position and size
items.text: The list opens 4 px below the field, aligned to its start and as wide as it (8 rem at least). It flips above when there is no room and scrolls when it is taller than the space left.

items.title: Open field
items.text: While the list is open the border of the field stays indigo, so the field and its list read as one.

items.title: Invalid and disabled
items.text: An invalid trigger turns the border and focus ring red, so say why in a line under the field, linked with aria-describedby. A disabled select dims to 40% and ignores pointer and keyboard.

items.title: Previews in these docs
items.text: The real list floats over the page. The previews here draw it inside the card, only while the whole card is on screen, and behave like the real one when you point at a card or focus it.

items.title: Opening and closing
items.text: The list fades in and scales up from the field while sliding 4 px in from below. Closing is one step faster.

items.title: Reduced motion
items.text: With reduced motion the transition is off and the list appears and disappears at once.

items.title: Inline width
items.text: The inline trigger is only as wide as the current label, so text after it moves when a longer or shorter option is chosen. Keep labels of similar length.

Select.items.description: The options as data, `{ value, label }` pairs or a map from value to label. Gives the field its labels when the `SelectItem` elements are built inside another component. Read from the children when you leave it out.

Select.multiple.description: Lets people choose several options. The value becomes an array. The field shows no chips, so show the choices yourself.

Select.open.description: Whether the list is open, when you control it. Pair it with `onOpenChange`.

Select.defaultOpen.description: Whether the list starts open when you do not control it.

Select.onOpenChange.description: Called when the list opens or closes, with the reason, such as a click, a key press, an outside press or choosing an option.

Select.modal.description: When `true`, the default, the page behind the open list is inert and does not scroll. `false` leaves the page usable.

Select.disabled.description: Disables the select: it dims to 40 % and ignores the pointer and the keyboard.

Select.name.description: The name the value is submitted under in a form, through a hidden input.

SelectTrigger.variant.description: `field` (default) is the full-width form field with a border. `inline` is a compact trigger with no border that is only as wide as its label and sits inside a sentence, a toolbar, a title or a row; it replaces InlineSelect. Give an inline trigger an `aria-label`, because it has no visible label.

SelectValue.placeholder.description: The text shown in the field while nothing is chosen, in the quieter tertiary colour.

SelectContent.finalFocus.description: Where focus goes when the list closes. It returns to the field by default.

SelectItem.value.description: The value the select holds when this option is chosen.

SelectItem.label.description: The text used for type-ahead and for the field when the children are not plain text.

SelectItem.disabled.description: Stops the option from being highlighted or chosen.

items.text: Use CheckboxButtonGroup for a few short options that can be combined, like text styles or filters. For one choice use RadioButtonGroup, and for long options use Checkbox or Selector Item.
Pick the group by what the options mean. CheckboxButtonGroup is a set of toggles where any number can be on, while RadioButtonGroup is one choice that arrow keys select and cannot be cleared.
Keep the value as an array of strings and update it in the change handler. Wrapping on narrow screens is built in, so no custom breakpoints are needed.
Name the group with a visible label and aria-labelledby, or with an aria-label. A screen reader announces the name when focus enters the group.
Give every icon-only ToggleButton an aria-label such as Bold. The pressed state is announced, but the icon alone has no name.
Put the error on the group: mark it invalid and write one message under it. Do not repeat the message on every button.
Don't use it for options with a sentence of explanation. A button holds a word or two, so use a Checkbox or Selector Item with a description.
Don't set the vertical orientation without stacking the buttons, or arrow keys will move in a direction the layout does not show.
Don't use it to switch between views or pages. People expect a Segment or Tabs for that.

keyboard.intro: The group is one tab stop: arrow keys move focus inside it and Tab moves out. Only Space and Enter change a button, unlike RadioButtonGroup, where arrow keys also choose.

rows.action: Moves focus into the group, to the first button at first and to the button that had focus last after that, and out of it again. The other buttons are not tab stops.
Moves focus to the next or previous button without changing it. From the last button it wraps to the first. In a vertical group these keys do nothing.
Does the same in a group with `orientation="vertical"`. In a horizontal group these keys do nothing.

behavior.intro: What the group does itself, and what it leaves to the page.

items.title: Any number on
items.text: Pressing a button adds its value to the array, and pressing it again removes it. The array can be empty, so a rule such as at least one is yours to enforce.

items.title: Controlled or not
items.text: Pass the value and a change handler to own the buttons that are on, or a default value to let the group keep them. Each button is matched by its value.

items.title: Toggles, not radios
items.text: Each option is a button that reports a pressed state, inside a group. Any number can be on and none is valid, and the square is drawn, not an input, so the group sends no form value by itself.

items.title: Names
items.text: The group needs a name from an aria-label or aria-labelledby. A button is named by its text, an icon-only button needs its own aria-label, and the mark is hidden from assistive technology.

items.title: Wrapping
items.text: The row wraps by itself when the container is narrow, with an 8 px gap in both directions. For a column, set the vertical orientation together with column layout classes.

items.title: Invalid
items.text: Marking the group invalid turns every button that is off red together. Buttons that are on and disabled buttons keep their own look, and the message is yours to write under the group.

items.title: Disabled
items.text: Disabling the group dims every button to 40 % and skips it with Tab and arrow keys. On one button it dims only that button.

items.title: Motion
items.text: Border, fill and the check change quickly. Nothing moves, so the group has no layout animation.

items.title: Reduced motion
items.text: With reduced motion the colour and opacity changes still run as fades. Nothing in the group moves, so nothing else changes.

behavior.intro: What the group does itself, and what it leaves to the page.

items.title: One choice, as an array
items.text: The group holds at most one value, kept in an array like every toggle group: one entry, or empty while nothing is chosen. Choosing another button replaces the old one.

items.title: A choice stays
items.text: Pressing the chosen button again keeps it chosen, like a native radio, and the change handler is not called. Only an empty starting value shows nothing chosen, and the first press ends that.

items.title: Controlled or not
items.text: Pass a value and a change handler to own the choice, or a default value to let the group keep it. Each button is matched by its own value.

items.title: Keyboard
items.text: One tab stop: the chosen button, or the first while nothing is chosen. Arrow keys, Home and End move focus and choose in one step, wrap at the ends and skip disabled buttons.

items.title: Radios made of buttons
items.text: The group is a radio group and each option a radio with a checked state, so a screen reader says radio 2 of 3, chosen. It sends no value with a form by itself, so add a hidden input when it must.

items.title: Names
items.text: The group needs a name from an aria-label or aria-labelledby. A button is named by its text, an icon-only button needs its own aria-label, and the mark is hidden from assistive technology.

items.title: Wrapping

items.title: Invalid
items.text: Marking the group invalid turns every unchosen button red together; chosen and disabled buttons keep their look. Write the message under the group and point to it with aria-describedby.

items.title: Disabled
items.text: Disabling the group dims every button to 40 % and skips it with Tab and the arrow keys. Disabling one button dims that button only, and the arrow keys skip it.

items.title: Motion
items.text: Border, fill and the dot change with a quick colour transition. Nothing moves, so the group has no layout animation.

items.title: Reduced motion
items.text: With reduced motion the colour and opacity changes still run, but they only fade. Nothing in the group moves, so nothing else changes.
