parts.description: The number between the buttons, at least 32 px wide, semibold with tabular figures so it does not jiggle. It is announced politely when it changes.

parts.name: Increase button
parts.description: A 32 px plain icon button named Increase. It dims and stops at the maximum in the same way.

items.text: Name the group with an aria-label such as Adults or Quantity of canvas tote bags. The buttons only say Decrease and Increase; the group name tells a screen reader what they change.
Set min, max and step to the real limits, so the buttons stop where the values stop. The value never leaves the range.
Use the format function to add the unit, such as 15 min, so the number is not read without it.
Say why a limit was reached when it is not obvious, such as Only 5 in stock. A dimmed button alone does not explain itself.
Don't use it for a value people may want to type, such as 250. There is no text entry, so 1 to 250 takes 249 presses: use Number Field.
Don't expect arrow keys to work. It is two buttons, not a spin button, so Tab reaches each and Enter or Space presses it; use Number Field where arrow keys, Home and End matter.
Don't use it for a range where the position matters more than the number. A Slider shows where the value sits between the limits.
Don't show the number in the stepper and again in a label next to it. One place for the value is enough.

useFor: A small count changed in single steps, such as guests, items in a cart or minutes of a reminder
A value that always has a number, with limits that the buttons can show
A row in a list or a settings page, where a text field would take more room than the value deserves

useInstead.name: Number Field
useInstead.text: a number that people type, with arrow keys, a format and an error message

useInstead.name: Slider
useInstead.text: a value in a range where the position matters

useInstead.name: Input
useInstead.text: a number that is an identifier, such as a postcode

keyboard.intro: The stepper is two native buttons, so the browser handles focus and activation. There are no arrow keys, Home, End or Page keys.

rows.action: Moves focus to the minus button, then to the plus button, and out. A button at its limit is dimmed but keeps its place in the order.
Presses the focused button: it changes the value by `step` and keeps focus on the button, also when the value reaches a limit.

behavior.intro: What the stepper does with its value, its limits and motion.

items.title: Controlled
items.text: The stepper keeps no state. The value comes from you, and a press reports the new number, already clamped to the limits.

items.title: Limits
items.text: Without limits the number goes on in both directions. A press that would pass a limit lands on the limit.

items.title: Buttons at the edge
items.text: At the minimum the minus button and at the maximum the plus button dim to 40%. They stay focusable and ignore the press, so pressing Enter again does not lose focus.

items.title: Format
items.text: The format function receives the number and returns what to show, as text or a node. It does not change the value you receive.

items.title: Announcing
items.text: The number sits in a polite live region, so a screen reader reads the new value after each press without interrupting.

items.title: No disabled or read-only state
items.text: The stepper has no disabled or read-only prop. To freeze it, set the minimum and maximum to the same value; both buttons then dim.

items.title: Width
items.text: The group is as wide as its content: two 32 px buttons, 8 px gaps and a number at least 32 px wide. A longer format such as 15 min makes it wider.

items.title: Motion
items.text: The buttons change fill quickly, and a press scales the button to 97% for a moment. The number changes in place.

items.title: Reduced motion
items.text: With reduced motion the press does not scale the button. The colour changes stay.

minimalUsage.expected: You see a minus button, the number 5 and a plus button in a row, with no border. A press on the plus button makes it 6; at 10 the plus button dims and stops.

NumberStepper.value.description: The current number. The stepper is controlled, so it shows what you pass and changes only when you set a new value in `onValueChange`.

NumberStepper.onValueChange.description: Called with the new number after a press, already clamped to `min` and `max`.

NumberStepper.min.description: The lowest value. The minus button dims and stops there. Defaults to minus infinity.

NumberStepper.max.description: The highest value. The plus button dims and stops there. Defaults to plus infinity.

NumberStepper.step.description: How much one press changes the value. Defaults to 1.

NumberStepper.format.description: Turns the number into what is shown between the buttons, for example `(n) => `${n} seats``. Defaults to the plain number.

NumberStepper.className.description: Extra classes for the group, for example `w-full justify-between` to spread the buttons across a row.

components.title: Drop Zone
components.description: A drag-and-drop file upload target with a click-to-browse fallback.

props.name: hint
props.description: Line under the prompt. Defaults to the accepted types, or "Any file type". State your size limit here.

parts.name: DropZone
parts.description: A label with a 2 px dashed border around a real file input. A drop anywhere on it, or a click, hands the files to your handler, and while a file is dragged over it the border and fill turn indigo.

parts.name: Icon
parts.description: An upload icon in the tertiary text colour. It is decorative and hidden from assistive technology.

parts.name: Prompt
parts.description: The line Drop files here or browse. It is the visible name of the control.

parts.name: Browse link
parts.description: The word browse in the link colour. It is not a separate button: a click anywhere on the zone opens the file dialog.

parts.name: Hint
parts.description: The small line under the prompt, by default the accepted types or Any file type. It is where a size limit belongs and the accessible description of the file input.

parts.name: File input
parts.description: The real file input, visually hidden and always accepting several files. It takes the keyboard focus, and the focus ring is drawn around the whole zone.

items.text: State the limit in the hint, for example PNG, JPG or PDF up to 10 MB. The zone does not enforce a size, so say what you will check.
Show every file in a list under the zone, with name, size, a progress bar while it uploads and a Remove or Cancel action. The zone itself shows no files.
Say in words why a file was refused, for example that the type is not supported and which types work. Keep the row so people see which file it was.
Check the type and size of every file in your file handler. A drop passes every file, whatever the accept setting says.
Don't rely on accept to keep wrong files out. It only filters the file dialog, and a dropped file of any type still reaches your handler.
Don't make drag and drop the only way in. The zone also opens the file dialog on a click and on Enter or Space, so keep that path working.
Don't put the zone inside another clickable element, such as a button or a link. It is already a label around an input, and the click would count twice.
Don't use it for a single file in a tight form row. A Button that opens the file dialog takes less room and reads as a form control.

useFor: Uploads where drag and drop saves time, such as images, documents or an import file
Several files at once, because the zone always accepts more than one
A large target on an empty page or in a dialog, where a small button would be easy to miss

useInstead.name: Button
useInstead.text: a single file in a tight form row, with a button that opens the file dialog

useInstead.name: Progress
useInstead.text: how far a file that is already uploading has come

useInstead.name: Empty State
useInstead.text: a page with nothing in it yet, where the first action is not an upload

keyboard.intro: The zone is a label around a native file input, so the browser provides focus and activation. Dropping files needs a pointer; the keyboard path is the file dialog.

rows.action: Moves focus onto the zone and off it. The zone has one tab stop, and the indigo border and ring mark it.
Opens the file dialog of the system. The chosen files arrive in `onFiles` like dropped ones.
In the file dialog: closes it without choosing. `onFiles` is not called.

behavior.intro: What the zone does with files, the drag, state and motion.

items.title: It only receives
items.text: DropZone hands the files to your handler and does nothing else. It never uploads, previews or stores a file, and has no progress, error or disabled state of its own.

items.title: Drag over
items.text: While a file is over the zone the border turns indigo and the fill a light indigo. This ends on drop and when the file leaves.

items.title: Always several files
items.text: The input accepts several files, so a dialog or a drop can hand over any number in one call. Take the first one if you only want one.

items.title: A copy of the list
items.text: The handler gets its own copy of the file list, so it stays valid after the input is reset or the drag ends.

items.title: The same file again
items.text: The input is reset after every choice, so choosing the same file a second time calls the handler again.

items.title: Accept and drops
items.text: The accept setting filters the file dialog only. A dropped file of another type still arrives in your handler, so check it there.

items.title: Hint
items.text: Without a hint the line lists the accepted types or says Any file type. A hint replaces it and is the place for a size limit.

items.title: Motion
items.text: The border and fill change colour on the fast duration. Nothing moves.

items.title: Reduced motion
items.text: There is no movement to remove, so reduced motion changes nothing. The colour change stays.

minimalUsage.expected: You see a dashed box with an upload icon, Drop files here or browse and a hint. A file dragged over turns the border indigo, and dropping or choosing one hands it to your code.

DropZone.onFiles.description: Called with a `FileList` of the files that were dropped or chosen in the file dialog. It is a copy, so it stays valid after the call. Check type and size here.

DropZone.accept.description: The types the file dialog offers, as for `<input accept>`: `image/*`, `application/pdf` or `.csv`, separated by commas. It does not filter dropped files. It also feeds the default hint.

DropZone.hint.description: The line under the prompt. Defaults to the accepted types, or `Any file type`. State your size limit here.

DropZone.className.description: Extra classes for the zone, for example `p-6` for a tighter box. It does not hold the drag-over look; the zone adds that itself.

components.title: Rich Text Editor
components.description: A Tiptap-powered WYSIWYG editor with a formatting toolbar.
components.props: function RichTextEditor(props: RichTextEditorProps): React.JSX.Element;

props.name: aria-describedby
props.description: Id of the element that describes the editing area, such as a helper line.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Accessible name of the editing area when there is no visible label.

props.name: aria-labelledby
props.description: Id of the element that names the editing area, such as a visible label.

props.name: id
props.description: Id of the editing area. A `<label htmlFor>` cannot name it (it is not a form control): use `aria-labelledby`.

props.name: slashMenu
props.description: Typing "/" at the start of a line or after a space opens a block menu at the caret: arrow keys pick, Enter or Tab inserts, Escape closes, typing filters. `true` shows the default blocks (headings, lists, task, quote, divider, code); pass y…

parts.name: RichTextEditor
parts.description: A 16 px frame with a 1 px border around the toolbar and the editing area. It loads its engine (Tiptap) on first render, shows a skeleton until then and gets an indigo ring on focus.

parts.name: RichTextEditorSkeleton
parts.description: The empty frame with the placeholder that shows until the editor has loaded, 38 px of toolbar and 128 px of text. Export it for your own loading state.

parts.name: Toolbar
parts.description: A row of 28 px icon buttons in 6 px of padding with a 2 px gap, closed off from the text by a 1 px line. The buttons are Bold, Italic, Underline, Bulleted list, Numbered list and Link.

parts.name: Toolbar button
parts.description: A 28 px icon button with an 8 px corner. It is a toggle, shown pressed while the cursor is in text with that format, and Link asks for the address in the browser's prompt.

parts.name: Separator
parts.description: A 1 px line, 20 px high, between the text styles, the lists and the link.

parts.name: Editing area
parts.description: The editable text: a multi-line textbox at least 128 px tall with 12 px padding that grows with its content. While empty it shows the placeholder, and you name it with an aria-label.

items.text: Use a Rich Text Editor for text that people format: a note, a project description, a reply, release notes. For plain text use a Textarea; for a message to an AI assistant use a Prompt Input.
Name the editing area with aria-labelledby pointing to a visible Label, or an aria-label when there is no room. A label with htmlFor cannot reach it, because the area is not a form control.
Store the HTML from the change handler and pass it back as the content when the person returns. The content is the starting text only, so use a new key to load other content.
Sanitize the HTML on your server before you store it or show it to other people. The editor limits the tags it produces, but a server should never trust the browser.
Say what is wrong next to the editor and keep the text. The editor has no invalid state of its own, so colour the frame with the error border and link the message with aria-describedby.

Turn on slashMenu for longer documents such as notes and briefs: "/" opens a block menu at the caret (headings, lists, task, quote, divider, code). Keep it off for short replies, where the toolbar is enough.
Don't use it for text that must stay plain, such as a name, a title or a search term. The output is HTML, not plain text, and a one-line Input is easier to fill in.
Don't use it as the composer of an AI chat. That is a Prompt Input: it sends on Enter, grows with the message and has attach and send buttons, not a formatting toolbar.
Don't rely on a shortcut for the link. There is none: the toolbar button is the way to add or remove a link.

useFor: Notes, descriptions and release notes where bold, lists and links make the text easier to scan
A reply or a comment that people format before they send it
Content that is stored as HTML and shown formatted somewhere else

useInstead.name: Textarea
useInstead.text: plain text over several lines, such as a message or feedback

useInstead.name: Prompt Input
useInstead.text: the message box of an AI chat, which is not a rich text editor

useInstead.name: Input
useInstead.text: one line of text, such as a title or a name

keyboard.intro: Every toolbar button is its own tab stop, followed by the editing area. In the text the shortcuts are the ones of the editing engine, with Cmd instead of Ctrl on a Mac, and there is none for the link.

rows.action: Moves focus through the toolbar buttons and into the editing area. Inside a list item that has an item before it, Tab indents the item and Shift+Tab outdents it; when the item cannot move, Tab leaves the editor.
On a toolbar button: turns the format on or off. Link opens the browser's prompt for the address.
Toggles bold, italic or underline on the selected text, or for the text typed next.
Turns the paragraph into a bulleted or a numbered list, or back into a paragraph.
Starts a new paragraph, or a new list item inside a list.
Inserts a line break inside the same paragraph.
Undoes and redoes the last edit.

behavior.intro: What the editor does with the text, the toolbar and the loading, and what it leaves to the page.

items.title: Loading
items.text: The editing engine is a separate chunk, so an app that never shows the editor never downloads it. A skeleton with the same frame shows until it loads, so nothing moves.

items.title: Content in and out
items.text: The content is the HTML the editor starts with, and the change handler gets the whole document as HTML after every edit. Changing the content later does nothing; a new key loads other text.

items.title: Toolbar state
items.text: Every button reads the selection and is pressed while the cursor is inside bold, italic or underlined text, a list or a link. A press keeps the focus in the text.

items.title: What it can write
items.text: Paragraphs and line breaks, bold, italic, underline, bulleted and numbered lists, and links. Other common elements such as headings and quotes survive pasting, but there is no button for them.

items.title: Links
items.text: The Link button asks for the address in the browser's prompt: an address sets the link, an empty answer removes it, Cancel leaves it. Clicking a link in the editor does not follow it.

items.title: Labelling
items.text: The editing area is a multi-line textbox, and aria-label, aria-labelledby and aria-describedby reach it. A click on a Label does not move focus into it, because labels only do that for form controls.

items.title: Focus
items.text: When the text has focus, the whole frame turns indigo with the 2 px ring, because the text itself has no outline. A toolbar button shows its own indigo border and ring.

items.title: Size
items.text: The editing area is at least 128 px tall and grows with the text, so the page scrolls, not the editor. After a list the document ends with an empty paragraph, so you can keep typing.

items.title: No disabled, read-only or invalid state
items.text: The Figma set draws disabled, read-only and invalid states, but the React editor does not take them yet. Render the saved HTML for read-only text, and colour the frame for an error.

items.title: Motion
items.text: The toolbar buttons change fill and colour quickly on hover and press. Nothing moves or scales, and typing never animates.

items.title: Reduced motion
items.text: With reduced motion the same colour change stays: it is a short fade, not movement.

minimalUsage.expected: You should see the label Meeting notes above a frame with a toolbar of six buttons and the grey placeholder. Type some text and press Bold: the button turns pressed and the HTML shows a strong tag.

RichTextEditor.content.description:
The HTML the editor starts with, for example `

Ship before Friday.

`. It is read once: later changes to the prop do not replace what was typed, so use a new `key` to load other content.

RichTextEditor.onChange.description: Called with the whole document as an HTML string after every edit. Store it, and pass it back as `content` when the person returns.

RichTextEditor.placeholder.description: The grey text shown while the editor is empty. Defaults to `Write something...`. It is not a label.

RichTextEditor.className.description: Extra classes on the frame, for example `border-error` to mark a problem or a width.

RichTextEditor.id.description: The `id` of the editing area, for `aria-labelledby` and `aria-describedby` of other elements to point at.

RichTextEditor.aria-label.description: The accessible name of the editing area when there is no visible label.

RichTextEditor.aria-labelledby.description: The id of the element that names the editing area, such as a visible `Label`. Use it instead of `htmlFor`, which does not reach a text box that is not a form control.

RichTextEditor.aria-describedby.description: The id of the element that describes the editing area, such as a helper line or an error message.

RichTextEditorSkeleton.placeholder.description: The text shown in the skeleton, so it matches the placeholder of the editor that replaces it.

RichTextEditorSkeleton.className.description: Extra classes on the frame of the skeleton, the same as on the editor.

components.title: Color Picker
components.description: Pick a colour: saturation and brightness, hue, opacity, eyedropper, HEX/RGB/HSL values and saved colours — inline or from a trigger field.
components.props: function ColorPicker({ variant, value, defaultValue, onValueChange, alpha, defaultAlpha, onAlphaChange, showAlpha, format, defaultFormat, onFormatChange, swatches, defaultSwatches, onSwatchesChange, title, onClose, className, }: ColorPickerProps): React.JSX.Element;

props.name: alpha
props.description: Opacity, 0–1. Leave out `onAlphaChange` and `alpha` to hide the opacity slider.

props.name: format
props.description: The value fields' format; the select in the picker switches it.

props.name: onClose
props.description: Shows the close button.

props.name: swatches
props.description: Saved colours; the + adds the current colour.

props.name: title
props.description: Heading of the panel. Hidden when `null`.

props.name: value
props.description: The colour as #RRGGBB.

props.name: variant
props.description: How a colour is picked: a saturation/brightness area or a grid of swatches.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Whether the popover is open by default.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name of the field.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called when the popover opens or closes.

props.name: open
props.description: The popover is open. Controlled; leave out for the field to manage it.

props.name: pickerProps
props.description: Everything else the picker takes (alpha, swatches, format …).

props.name: shape
props.description: `default`: the Input-sized field with a square swatch. `pill`: a 32 px pill with a colour dot, to sit in a row of pill-shaped colour presets.

parts.name: ColorPicker
parts.description: A 296 px wide card with a title, a colour area, hue and opacity sliders, value fields and saved colours. It holds the colour as a hex string and the opacity from 0 to 1, and it is not a native input.

parts.name: Header
parts.description: The title, Color picker by default, and a close button at the right when a close handler is set. Setting the title to null removes the title, and the whole header if there is no close handler.

parts.name: Colour area
parts.description: A two-dimensional slider: saturation runs left to right and brightness bottom to top. The grid variant is a grid of greys and nine shades of twelve hues, with arrow keys moving between swatches.

parts.name: Hue and opacity
parts.description: Two sliders under the area, with an eyedropper button at the left in browsers that have one. The opacity slider and field can be left out.

parts.name: Value
parts.description: A select for the format (HEX, RGB or HSL) and the fields for the value, followed by the opacity in percent. A field commits on Enter or blur, so typing 2 on the way to 255 does not move the colour.

parts.name: Saved colours
parts.description: A row of 24 px swatches with a plus button that saves the current colour. The chosen swatch gets a ring in its own colour, and you can set the first set or control the whole list.

parts.name: ColorPickerTrigger
parts.description: A field that opens the picker in a popover below it: a swatch, the hex value and a chevron, the size of an Input. The pill shape is a 32 px pill with a colour dot, for a row of presets.

items.text: Use ColorPickerTrigger in a form or a settings row. The field shows the colour at rest, and the panel opens only when it is needed.
Use ColorPicker on the page when the colour is the task, for example an editor with a preview beside it. Judge the colour on real content, not on a bare swatch.
Hold the colour as a hex string and the opacity as a number, each with its change handler. Leave opacity out where a colour is always opaque.
Pass the colours of your product as the default swatches, so people start from a palette they should use.
Give the trigger a label, such as Primary colour. Its accessible name is the label plus the value, because a swatch alone says nothing to a screen reader.
Don't use a native color input. Its panel is the browser's own and cannot carry your tokens, your saved colours or an opacity.
Don't use a colour as the only information. A picked colour needs its value in text, as the field and the preview line show.
Don't use it to choose from a short list of fixed colours. A row of Selector Items or a Radio Button Group is quicker and keeps people inside your palette.

useFor: A brand or accent colour in a settings page, with a preview of what it changes
A highlight, label or tag colour in an editor, where opacity matters
Any colour that people may choose freely, including from a value they paste

useInstead.name: Radio Button Group
useInstead.text: a choice from a few fixed colours

useInstead.name: Cell Color Picker
useInstead.text: a compact swatch inside a Data Table cell

useInstead.name: Input
useInstead.text: a colour that is only ever typed as text

keyboard.intro: The area and both sliders are sliders with one tab stop each. The fields, swatches and buttons are native controls.

rows.action: Moves focus through the close button, the colour area, the eyedropper, the two sliders, the format select, the value fields and the saved colours.
On the colour area: changes saturation by 1 %, and with Shift by 10 %. On a slider: changes the value by 1 %, and with Shift by 10 %.
On the colour area: changes brightness by 1 %, and with Shift by 10 %. On a slider: the same as Right and Left.
On a slider: goes to 0 % or 100 %. In the swatch grid: goes to the first or the last swatch.
In the swatch grid (`variant="grid"`): moves to the next swatch, a row at a time with Up and Down.
In a value field: commits the typed value. On a swatch, the plus or the trigger: activates it.
In the popover of a trigger: closes it and returns focus to the trigger.

behavior.intro: What the picker does with state, values, formats and motion.

items.title: Controlled or not
items.text: Value, opacity, format and swatches can each be controlled with a change handler, or kept by the picker from a default.

items.title: The value
items.text: The colour is a hex string in capitals. Opacity is separate, from 0 to 1, so the hex never carries an alpha pair.

items.title: Hue stays
items.text: The picker keeps hue, saturation and brightness itself. At zero saturation or brightness a colour has no hue, so the hue slider stays put instead of jumping to red.

items.title: Formats
items.text: The select switches the fields between HEX, RGB and HSL without changing the colour. An unreadable value is dropped when you leave the field, and an empty field returns to the last valid value.

items.title: Eyedropper
items.text: The eyedropper picks a colour from anywhere on the screen. It exists in Chromium browsers only, so elsewhere the button is left out.

items.title: Saved colours
items.text: The plus button adds the current colour to the row, unless it is already there. Choosing a swatch sets the colour.

items.title: Trigger
items.text: The field opens the picker in a popover 8 px below it. A popover that is open from the start does not pull focus on load, but one opened by pointer or keyboard takes it.

items.title: Motion
items.text: The popover fades and scales in, then fades out faster. The trigger chevron turns and the ring of a saved colour changes quickly.

items.title: Reduced motion
items.text: With reduced motion the popover keeps its fade and drops the scale. The panel has no other movement.

minimalUsage.expected: You see a panel with a colour area, a hue and an opacity slider, a value field and nine saved colours. Drag in the area or on a slider and the value follows.

ColorPicker.variant.description: `spectrum` (the default) picks in a saturation and brightness area; `grid` picks from a grid of swatches.

ColorPicker.value.description: The colour as `#RRGGBB`, to control it. Update it in `onValueChange`.

ColorPicker.defaultValue.description: The colour to start with when the picker keeps its own state. Defaults to `#555CF3`.

ColorPicker.onValueChange.description: Called with the new `#RRGGBB` colour while you drag, type or choose a swatch.

ColorPicker.alpha.description: The opacity from 0 to 1, to control it.

ColorPicker.defaultAlpha.description: The opacity to start with. Defaults to 1.

ColorPicker.showAlpha.description: Whether the opacity slider and field are shown. Defaults to true.

ColorPicker.format.description: The format of the value fields, `hex`, `rgb` or `hsl`, to control it.

ColorPicker.defaultFormat.description: The format to start with. Defaults to `hex`.

ColorPicker.onFormatChange.description: Called with the new format when the select changes.

ColorPicker.swatches.description: The saved colours, to control them.

ColorPicker.defaultSwatches.description: The saved colours to start with. Defaults to nine library hues.

ColorPicker.onSwatchesChange.description: Called with the new list when the plus button saves a colour.

ColorPicker.title.description: The heading of the panel. `null` hides it. Defaults to `Color picker`.

ColorPicker.onClose.description: Shows the close button and is called when it is pressed.

ColorPickerTrigger.value.description: The colour as `#RRGGBB`, to control it.

ColorPickerTrigger.defaultValue.description: The colour to start with. Defaults to `#555CF3`.

ColorPickerTrigger.onValueChange.description: Called with the new colour from the picker in the popover.

ColorPickerTrigger.label.description: The accessible name of the field, followed by the value. Defaults to `Colour`.

ColorPickerTrigger.pickerProps.description: Everything else the picker takes, such as `alpha`, `format`, `swatches` or `variant`.

ColorPickerTrigger.side.description: Whether the popover opens below (`bottom`, the default) or above (`top`) the field.

ColorPickerTrigger.align.description: How the popover lines up with the field: `start` (the default), `center` or `end`.

ColorPickerTrigger.shape.description: `default` is the Input-sized field with a square swatch; `pill` is a 32 px pill with a colour dot.

ColorPickerTrigger.open.description: Whether the popover is open, to control it.

ColorPickerTrigger.defaultOpen.description: Whether the popover starts open when `open` is not set.

ColorPickerTrigger.onOpenChange.description: Called with the new open state when the popover opens or closes.

ColorPickerTrigger.className.description: Extra classes for the field, for example `w-full`.

components.title: Cell Color Picker
components.description: A compact color swatch picker for inline use in a Data Table cell.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Name for screen readers, such as "Label colour". The accessible name becomes "Label colour, #6366F1". Default: "Colour #6366F1. Choose a colour".

parts.name: Table
parts.description: The table the cell sits in. The first column holds the row names, the header row names the columns, and the picker lives in a table cell.

parts.name: Column header
parts.description: The header of the colour column. It says what the colour is for, such as Colour or Chart colour.

parts.name: Row header
parts.description: The first cell of the row, marked as the row header, which says which label, calendar or series the colour belongs to. Give the swatch the same name as its aria-label.

parts.name: CellColorPicker
parts.description: A round swatch button that opens a six-colour popover. Built for a table cell, it returns the chosen colour as a hex string, and you hold the value and write it back on change.

parts.name: Swatch button
parts.description: The 24 px round trigger filled with the current colour. Its name is the label plus the hex value, and it announces a dialog.

parts.name: Popover
parts.description: The popover with the six swatches in one row. Its name comes from the aria-label, Choose a colour by default, and it stays open after a choice.

parts.name: Swatch
parts.description: One of the six colour buttons in the popover, named by its hex value. The active one has a ring and is marked pressed.

items.text: Keep the value as a hex string and store it in the change handler. The trigger names itself with that value.
Pass an aria-label that names the row, such as Billing colour, so the swatch reads Billing colour plus its hex value. Mark the first cell of each row as a row header too.
Show the effect of the choice nearby, such as a legend bar or a preview, so nobody judges the colour from a 24 px circle alone.
Give the colour column a header that says what the colour is for, and centre the swatch in a narrow column.
Don't expect colours outside the six swatches. Another value still shows on the trigger, but no swatch is marked and people can only pick from the six.
Don't use it outside a table row, since it is 24 px wide and has no visible label. Use ColorPicker for a labelled field with hex entry and opacity.
Don't use colour as the only carrier of meaning. Pair it with the name of the label or series, as the row header does.
Don't expect the Figma Editable Cell states (Edit, Changed, Saving, Error, Disabled). It only has a value and a change handler.

useFor: A colour column in a table, such as a label colour, a calendar colour or a chart series
A short fixed palette of six colours
Colours that are stored as hex strings

useInstead.name: Color Picker
useInstead.text: a free colour with hex, RGB or HSL entry and opacity

useInstead.name: Badge
useInstead.text: a status or category in a fixed set of tints that the person does not choose

useInstead.name: Cell Select
useInstead.text: a choice between named options instead of colours

keyboard.intro: The swatch button and every colour in the popover are native buttons, so the browser handles focus and activation.
keyboard.note: The popover has no arrow-key navigation. Each of the six swatches is its own Tab stop.

rows.action: Moves focus to the next or previous control in the table, row by row. Each swatch button is one Tab stop.
On the swatch button: opens the popover. Tab then moves into it, through the six colours.
On a colour: chooses it and calls `onValueChange` with its hex value. The popover stays open, so you can try another colour.
Closes the popover and returns focus to the swatch button.

behavior.intro: What the cell colour picker does itself, and what it leaves to the table around it.

items.title: Controlled
items.text: CellColorPicker keeps no state. You supply the value, a choice calls the change handler with the hex string, and nothing changes until you set the value.

items.title: The palette
items.text: The palette has six fixed colours: blue, purple, orange-red, yellow, green and pink. A value outside the set shows on the swatch button, but no popover colour is marked.

items.title: Accessible name
items.text: Without a label the button reads Colour, its hex value and Choose a colour. With a label like Billing colour it reads the label plus the hex, so mark the first row cell as a row header too.

items.title: Popover
items.text: The popover opens below the swatch and is not clipped by the table card. It stays open after a choice and closes with Escape or a click outside.

items.title: Active colour
items.text: The matching swatch is marked pressed and has a ring. A colour outside the palette marks none.

items.title: Figma states
items.text: The Figma Editable Cell set has View, Edit, Changed, Saving, Error and Disabled. CellColorPicker has no props for these states.

items.title: Motion
items.text: The popover fades and scales in, then leaves faster. A swatch grows by 10 % on hover.

items.title: Reduced motion
items.text: With reduced motion the popover opens without moving and the swatches no longer grow. Only the fade stays.

minimalUsage.intro: Then use it inside a table cell:
minimalUsage.expected: You see a 24 px blue circle in the cell. Click it to open a popover with six colours, choose one and the circle takes that colour.

CellColorPicker.value.description: The current colour as a hex string, such as `#12AFF0`. It is a controlled value. A value outside the six swatches shows on the button but marks no swatch.

CellColorPicker.onValueChange.description: Called with the hex string of the swatch the person chose. The popover stays open afterwards.

CellColorPicker.aria-label.description: The accessible name of the swatch button, such as `Billing colour`. The button is then named `<aria-label>, <hex>`; the popover uses the label as its name. Without it the button is named `Colour <hex>. Choose a colour`.

components.title: Cell Slider
components.description: A compact progress/value slider for inline use in a Data Table cell.

parts.name: Table
parts.description: The table the cell sits in. The first column holds the row names, the header row names the columns, and the bar lives in a table cell.

parts.name: Column header
parts.description: The header of the bar column. It names the measure and the unit, such as Quota used, because the bar itself has no label.

parts.name: Row header
parts.description: The first cell of the row, marked as the row header. It says whose level the bar shows.

parts.name: CellSlider
parts.description: A small bar, 112 px wide, with a number beside it. It shows a value out of a maximum (default 100) and cannot be dragged, since it is a display, not a control.

parts.name: Track
parts.description: The 4 px grey bar with fully rounded ends. It always spans the width left of the number.

parts.name: Fill
parts.description: The primary-coloured part of the track. Its width is the value divided by the maximum, capped at 100 %.

parts.name: Number
parts.description: The raw value to the right of the bar, 12 px and right-aligned in 28 px, so the bar never has to be read on its own.

items.text: Set the maximum to the real ceiling, such as 5 for a 5-point score or the seat limit of the row. The fill is clamped to the track, but the number still shows the raw value.
Put it in a column whose header names the measure and the unit, such as Quota used. The bar and number have no label or role of their own.
Mark the first cell of each row as a row header, so the number is read with its row.
Pair it with a control when the level can change, such as a button that completes a task. The slider then follows the value.
Don't build an editable cell around it. It has no handler, keyboard support or ARIA role, so use a Slider with an aria-label in the cell instead.
Don't use it for one task or upload with a label and a status. Progress has the role and the text for that.
Don't rely on the bar for values outside 0 to the maximum. It draws an empty or full bar there, and only the number shows the real figure.
Don't count on the Figma Editable Cell Slider states (View, Edit, Changed, Saving, Error, Disabled). The React cell shows a level only.

useFor: Showing a level inside a table row, such as a quota used, a score or a share
A column of bars that people compare at a glance
Values that are set somewhere else and only read here

useInstead.name: Slider
useInstead.text: a value the person changes by dragging or with the arrow keys

useInstead.name: Progress
useInstead.text: the completion of one task or upload, with a label and a role

useInstead.name: Meter
useInstead.text: a value in a known range with thresholds, such as disk usage

behavior.intro: What the cell slider shows and what it leaves out.

items.title: Read-only
items.text: CellSlider takes only a value and a maximum. It has no handler, cannot be focused or dragged and takes no key, so change the bar by changing the value.

items.title: Fill
items.text: The fill is clamped between 0 and 100 %: empty at 0 or below, full at the maximum or above. The number always shows what you passed, so 130 of 100 fills the bar and still reads 130.

items.title: No role, no name
items.text: The bar has no ARIA role or label, so a screen reader reads only the number. Name the measure in the column header and the row in a row header, and put the unit in the header.

items.title: Number
items.text: The number is the raw value in a 28 px box, right-aligned. Up to three digits line up in a column, and longer ones widen the box and shorten the bar.

items.title: Width
items.text: The cell is 112 px wide. Give its column about 160 px so the header and the bar line up.

items.title: Figma states
items.text: The Figma Editable Cell set shows a draggable Slider in six states, but in React CellSlider only displays a level. For a value people change, use Slider in the cell.

items.title: Motion
items.text: Nothing moves. The fill changes width in one step when the value changes.

items.title: Reduced motion
items.text: There is no movement to remove, so reduced motion changes nothing.

minimalUsage.intro: Then use it inside a table cell:
minimalUsage.expected: You see a thin grey bar with a primary-coloured fill and the number to its right. At a value of 68 the fill covers 68 % of the bar.

CellSlider.value.description: The level to show. The bar is clamped to 0 to `max`: a negative value draws an empty bar and a value above `max` a full one. The number beside the bar always shows the value as given.

CellSlider.max.description: The value that fills the whole bar. The default is 100. Set it to the real ceiling, such as 5 for a 5-point score. A `max` of 0 or less draws an empty bar.

components.title: Cell Select
components.description: A compact select for inline use in a Data Table cell.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Name for screen readers — a combobox is not named by its current value.

parts.name: Table
parts.description: The table the cell sits in. The first column holds the row names, the header row names the columns, and the select lives in a table cell.

parts.name: Row header
parts.description: The first cell of the row, marked as the row header. It says which row the select belongs to, so a screen reader reads it with the select.

parts.name: CellSelect
parts.description: A compact select for a table cell: a 32 px trigger, 128 px wide, with a plain list of strings as options. You hold the value and write it back on change.

parts.name: Trigger
parts.description: The button that shows the current value and opens the list. It has no visible label, so give it an aria-label (default Choose a value).

parts.name: Value
parts.description: The current value on one line in 12 px text. A value longer than the trigger is cut with an ellipsis.

parts.name: Chevron
parts.description: The down chevron at the right edge of the trigger. It stays inside the border at every value length.

parts.name: Options list
parts.description: The popup under the trigger, as wide as the trigger. A long option wraps onto more lines here, so the full text is always readable.

parts.name: Option
parts.description: One row of the list for each option string. The highlighted option takes the page background and the chosen one shows a check.

items.text: Set an aria-label per row and column, such as Role of Nora Lindgren. A trigger that shows only its value does not name itself to a screen reader.
Pass options as the exact strings you store, and keep the value one of them. The value is the text, with no separate label.
Keep options short, up to about 14 characters. The trigger shows one line in 128 px and cuts the rest with an ellipsis.
Mark the first cell of each row as a row header, so a screen reader reads the row, the column and the value together.
Don't use it for long lists or options that need a description. It has no search or groups, so use a Combobox.
Don't use it in a form with a label. There NativeSelect with its Label and helper text is the right control.
Don't pass a value that is not in the options. No option is checked and the list has no starting point.
Don't expect a saving, error or disabled look. CellSelect has no such props, unlike the Editable Cell states in Figma.

useFor: Editing one value of a row in place, such as a role, a status, a priority or a team
Short lists of three to eight options that people know
A column where every row picks from the same options

useInstead.name: Select
useInstead.text: a select in a form, with a visible label and helper text

useInstead.name: Combobox
useInstead.text: a long list or options that people need to search

useInstead.name: Radio Group
useInstead.text: two or three options that should all stay visible

keyboard.intro: The trigger is a button with the combobox role. The list is the Base UI select popup, so it traps focus while open.
keyboard.note: In this version, typing a letter does not jump to the option that starts with it.

rows.action: Moves focus to the next or previous control in the table, row by row. Each trigger is one Tab stop.
On the closed trigger: opens the list with the current value highlighted.
In the open list: moves the highlight to the next or previous option.
In the open list: chooses the highlighted option, calls `onValueChange` and returns focus to the trigger.
Closes the list without a change and returns focus to the trigger.

behavior.intro: What the cell select does itself, and what it leaves to the table around it.

items.title: Controlled
items.text: CellSelect keeps no state. You supply the value, a choice calls the change handler with the option string, and nothing changes until you set the value.

items.title: Options are strings
items.text: Options are a list of strings, and the value is one of them. For a label that differs from the stored value, use NativeSelect with its own items.

items.title: Accessible name
items.text: A combobox is not named by its current value, and a cell has no visible label. Set an aria-label per row and column, such as Role of Nora Lindgren, since the default is the same in every row.

items.title: Table context
items.text: With the first cell marked as a row header, a screen reader in table mode reads row, column and value together. In forms mode only the trigger is read, so its label must carry row and column.

items.title: Width and long values
items.text: The trigger is 32 px high and 128 px wide, in 12 px text, and a value that does not fit is cut with an ellipsis. The list is as wide as the trigger, so a long option wraps and stays readable.

items.title: The list
items.text: The list opens below the trigger, never over it, and is not clipped by the table card. The chosen option shows a check, and the highlighted one takes the page background.

items.title: Focus
items.text: The trigger shows the focus ring (an indigo border and a 2 px ring) and a primary border while the list is open.

items.title: Figma states
items.text: The Figma Editable Cell set has View, Edit, Changed, Saving, Error and Disabled, but CellSelect has no props for them. For a disabled or invalid select, use NativeSelect in the cell.

items.title: Motion
items.text: The list fades and scales out of its anchor and leaves faster. The trigger border changes quickly.

items.title: Reduced motion
items.text: With reduced motion the list opens and closes without a transition.

minimalUsage.intro: Then use it inside a table cell:
minimalUsage.expected: You see a small select showing Editor. Click it or press Enter to open a list of Admin, Editor and Viewer with a check on Editor, and choose one to change the value.

CellSelect.value.description: The current option. It is a controlled value and must be one of `options`; write the new one back in `onValueChange`.

CellSelect.onValueChange.description: Called with the option string the person chose. It is not called for an empty value.

CellSelect.options.description: The options as plain strings. Each string is shown in the list and is also the value that is stored.

CellSelect.aria-label.description: The name for screen readers. A cell has no visible label, so give each select its row and column, such as `Role of Nora Lindgren`. The default is `Choose a value`.

components.title: Cell Switch
components.description: A compact switch for inline use in a Data Table cell.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Name for screen readers — a cell has no visible label of its own.

parts.name: Table
parts.description: The table the cell sits in. The first column holds the row names, the header row names the columns, and the switch lives in a table cell.

parts.name: Column header
parts.description: The header of the switch column. It says what the switch changes, such as Email alerts, and aligns the same way as the cell.

parts.name: Row header
parts.description: The first cell of the row, marked as the row header. It says whose or which setting this is, so a screen reader reads it with the switch.

parts.name: CellSwitch
parts.description: A Switch with a default aria-label of Toggle, made for a table cell with no visible label. You hold the checked state and write it back on change.

parts.name: Track
parts.description: The 32 by 18 px pill. It is brand-coloured when on and grey when off, and it carries the switch role and checked state.

parts.name: Knob
parts.description: The 16 px circle that slides from one end of the track to the other. It swings slightly past the end before it settles.

items.text: Name every switch by its row and column, such as Email alerts for Nora Lindgren. The default Toggle is the same in every row and tells a screen-reader user nothing.
Mark the first cell of each row as a row header and give the switch column a header that says what it changes. The cell is then read as row, column and state.
Keep the checked state in your own state and save in the same handler that writes it back. The cell keeps no state.
Align the switch like its column header: centred in a narrow column, left beside text. Use the same alignment class on the header and the cell.
Don't use CellSwitch outside a table. Without a visible label the switch has no context, so use Switch with a Label, or a Selector Item.
Don't use a switch for an action that needs a confirmation, such as deleting data. A switch applies at once.
Don't put two switches in one cell. One cell holds one value, so give each value its own column.
Don't expect a saving, error or disabled look from CellSwitch. For rows that need them, use a Switch with those states inside the cell.

useFor: An on/off column in a table, such as enabled, notify or public
A matrix of switches, where each row and column pair is one setting
Settings that apply at once, with no Save button

useInstead.name: Switch
useInstead.text: a setting outside a table, with a visible label

useInstead.name: Checkbox
useInstead.text: a row you select for a bulk action, or a value that is sent with a form

useInstead.name: Selector Item
useInstead.text: a setting with a title and a description in a card

keyboard.intro: Each switch is one tab stop in its cell. It is a Switch, so the browser and Base UI handle focus and activation.
keyboard.note: Arrow keys do not move between table cells. Every switch in a column is its own Tab stop, in row order.

rows.action: Moves focus to the next or previous control in the table, row by row. The table cells around the switch take no focus.
Toggles the focused switch and calls `onCheckedChange` with the new value.

behavior.intro: What the cell switch does itself, and what it leaves to the table around it.

items.title: Controlled
items.text: CellSwitch keeps no state. You supply the checked value, every toggle calls the change handler with the new boolean, and nothing changes until you set it.

items.title: Accessible name
items.text: A cell has no visible label, so the switch is named by its aria-label. The default Toggle is the same in every row, so set one per row, such as Email alerts for Nora Lindgren.

items.title: Table context
items.text: With the first cell marked as a row header, a screen reader in table mode reads row, column and state together. In forms mode only the control is read, so its label must carry row and column.

items.title: Size and hit area
items.text: It is the default Switch, 32 by 18 px. The click area reaches 12 px to the sides and 8 px above and below, so a near miss still toggles it and two rows in a 36 px row never overlap.

items.title: Alignment
items.text: The switch is an inline control. Centre or right alignment on the cell moves it, and the column header should use the same alignment.

items.title: Hover and pressed
items.text: An off track gets a rim on hover and a darker grey while pressed. A brand track darkens on hover and darkens again while pressed.

items.title: Figma states
items.text: The Figma Editable Cell set has View, Edit, Changed, Saving, Error and Disabled, but CellSwitch is always editable. For a pending save or a disabled row, put a Switch with those states in the cell.

items.title: Motion
items.text: The track changes colour quickly, and the knob slides, swings slightly past the end and settles. A second click reverses it from wherever it is.

items.title: Reduced motion
items.text: With reduced motion the knob jumps to the other end instead of sliding. The colour change stays.

minimalUsage.intro: Then use it inside a table cell:
minimalUsage.expected: You see a small brand-coloured switch in the cell, turned on. Click it or press Space to turn it off, and the track turns grey as the knob moves left.

CellSwitch.checked.description: Whether the switch is on. It is a controlled value: write the new one back in `onCheckedChange`.

CellSwitch.onCheckedChange.description: Called with the new value, `true` or `false`, when the person toggles the switch with a click, Space or Enter.

CellSwitch.aria-label.description: The name for screen readers. A cell has no visible label, so give each switch its row and column, such as `Email alerts for Nora Lindgren`. The default is `Toggle`.

components.title: Selector Item
components.description: A list row pairing a leading icon/avatar and label/description with a trailing radio, checkbox, or switch.

props.name: action
props.description: Secondary action beside the row. Rendered outside the label; clicking it never toggles the control.

props.name: announceError
props.description: Announce the error at once (`role="alert"`). Set it only for an error that appears after an action such as a failed submit; leave it off for an error that is already there when the page loads, or it is read twice.

props.name: badge
props.description: Small pill next to the title, for example "Recommended".

props.name: control
props.description: The RadioGroupItem, Checkbox or Switch of the row. Not needed (and ignored) when `href` is set.

props.name: controlPosition
props.description: Which side of the label the control sits on.

props.name: error
props.description: Error text below the row; marks the control invalid. It is linked with aria-describedby, so a screen reader reads it when the control gets focus.

props.name: helper
props.description: Hint text below the row.

props.name: href
props.description: Link mode: the whole row is an anchor with a trailing chevron and no control.

props.name: icon
props.description: Icon in a 40 px tint-indigo tile, in front of the text (no rim). Ignored when `leading` is set.

props.name: layout
props.description: `card` is the bordered row; `inline` is a 24 px row without border or padding.

props.name: metadata
props.description: Short secondary text next to the control (a price, a count). Not interactive.

props.name: onSelect
props.description: Link mode: called on click. Without a real `href` the click does not jump to "#".

props.name: selected
props.description: Shows the selected look without a checked control, for example the current choice of a link list. A checked control does it on its own.

props.name: aria-describedby
props.description: Extra description for the control, for example the id of a hint under the row.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Names the control (radio, checkbox) or the link when the row has no visible text to name it.

props.name: aria-labelledby
props.description: Names the control by another element, for a row whose label is somewhere else.

props.name: badge
props.description: Small badge next to the title, e.g. "Recommended"

props.name: disabled
props.description: Dims the row once (the row, not its control as well), turns the control or link off and takes it out of the arrow-key order. A disabled `OptionRowGroup` disables every row in it.

props.name: icon
props.description: Leading icon (rendered in a 40px tint-indigo tile with a tint-text rim for variant="icon")

props.name: value
props.description: Required for radio/checkbox variants — the RadioGroupItem / Checkbox value.

props.name: variant
props.description: radio (default) · checkbox · link (chevron, no control) · icon (icon box + trailing radio)

props.name: aria-describedby
props.description: Extra description, for example the id of a hint. The error message is added to it.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Names the radiogroup. Give this or `aria-labelledby`, or wrap the group in a fieldset with a legend.

props.name: aria-labelledby
props.description: Names the radiogroup by another element, for example a heading.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables every row in the group. Disabled rows are skipped by the arrow keys.

props.name: error
props.description: Error message under the list; marks the group invalid and is linked with `aria-describedby`. Announced when it appears.

props.name: invalid
props.description: Marks the group invalid (`aria-invalid`) and gives the rows that are not chosen the error tint. Implied by `error`.

props.name: name
props.description: Name of the group in a form: the chosen value is submitted under it (the radios carry hidden inputs).

props.name: required
props.description: A choice is required before the form can be submitted (`aria-required`, and native validation on submit).

props.name: aria-describedby
props.description: Extra description, for example the id of a hint. The error message is added to it.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Names the radiogroup. Give this or `aria-labelledby`, or wrap the group in a fieldset with a legend.

props.name: aria-labelledby
props.description: Names the radiogroup by another element, for example a heading.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables every row in the group. Disabled rows are skipped by the arrow keys.

props.name: error
props.description: Error message under the list; marks the group invalid and is linked with `aria-describedby`. Announced when it appears.

props.name: invalid
props.description: Marks the group invalid (`aria-invalid`) and gives the rows that are not chosen the error tint. Implied by `error`.

props.name: name
props.description: Name of the group in a form: the chosen value is submitted under it (the radios carry hidden inputs).

props.name: required
props.description: A choice is required before the form can be submitted (`aria-required`, and native validation on submit).

props.name: value
props.description: Radio mode: the chosen value. Setting any of `value`, `onValueChange`, `name`, `required`, `disabled`, `invalid` or `error` turns the group into a radiogroup.

parts.name: SelectorItem
parts.description: The bordered row with 12 px corners, all of it except the action one label, so a click anywhere toggles the control. The row takes the indigo tint and a 1.5 px rim when chosen.

parts.name: SelectorItemGroup
parts.description: A vertical stack of rows with an 8 px gap, so several options read as one list.

parts.name: Leading
parts.description: An optional icon, avatar or logo before the text. The slot is at least 32 px wide and centres its content, so text starts at the same x in every row.

parts.name: Icon tile
parts.description: The `icon` prop: a 40 px tile with a tint-indigo fill and the icon in tint-text, with no rim. It sits in the leading slot.

parts.name: Title
parts.description: One line of 14 px medium text. It names the control for assistive technology and is cut with an ellipsis when too long.

parts.name: Description
parts.description: One line of secondary text, 4 px below the title. It describes the control for assistive technology.

parts.name: Badge
parts.description: The `badge` prop: a light pill next to the title, such as Recommended.

parts.name: Metadata
parts.description: Short secondary text before the control, such as a price or a count. It sits inside the label and is plain text, not interactive.

parts.name: Control
parts.description: The radio, checkbox or switch you pass as the control. It is the one tab stop of the row and keeps its own focus ring.

parts.name: Action
parts.description: A secondary button such as Edit. It sits outside the label, so clicking it never toggles the control, and it has its own tab stop.

parts.name: Group error
parts.description: The `error` of a radio group: a 14 px red line under the list with `role="alert"`, linked to the group.

items.text: Use it for choices needing a title and an explanation: delivery methods, plans, a switch setting. For a short label by a box use Checkbox with Label, for button-sized options Radio Button Group.
Pass the matching control: a radio inside a RadioGroup, or a Checkbox or Switch alone. The border follows the control's checked state, so the row needs no props for it.
Keep the title to one line and put the detail in the description. Both are truncated, so long text is cut with an ellipsis.
Put a secondary button in the action slot, not in the title or description. It stays outside the label and has its own tab stop.
Use the error prop for a row that cannot be chosen or must be ticked. It turns the row red, marks the control invalid and links the message to it.
Don't put a link or button in the title or description. The row is one label, and a click on it toggles the control.
Don't mix controls in one list, such as a switch row between radio rows. People read one control as one kind of choice.
Don't use card rows for a long list. Switch to the inline layout, or to a Select, once there are more than about six options.

useFor: Choices that need a title and an explanation, such as a delivery method or a plan
A settings row with a switch, a description and an optional action
A list of people or items to pick from, each with an avatar or an icon

useInstead.name: Checkbox
useInstead.text: a short label next to a single box

useInstead.name: Radio Group
useInstead.text: a list of plain radios with a label each

useInstead.name: Radio Button Group
useInstead.text: one choice from a few short options shown as buttons

useInstead.name: Item Card
useInstead.text: a card that opens something instead of choosing it

keyboard.intro: A row has one tab stop for its control and one for its action. The keys that change the row are the keys of the control inside it.

rows.action: Moves focus to the control of the row, then to its action when it has one, and on to the next row. In a radio group only the chosen radio, or the first one when nothing is chosen, is a tab stop.
In a radio group, moves focus to the next or previous row and chooses it. From the last row it wraps to the first. Checkboxes and switches ignore these keys.
Toggles the focused checkbox or switch, or chooses the focused radio. A disabled control is skipped.
Toggles the focused switch and presses the focused action. A checkbox and a radio ignore it.

behavior.intro: What the row does itself, and what it leaves to the page.

items.title: One label
items.text: The leading element, title, description, metadata and control are one label, so a click on any of them toggles the control. The action and the helper or error text sit outside it.

items.title: Names
items.text: Base UI controls are not named by a surrounding label. The row links the title as the name and the description, helper and error as the description, unless the control has its own label.

items.title: Selected
items.text: The row reads the checked state from the control. A chosen radio or checkbox turns the border indigo and the fill subtle, while a switch only moves its thumb, since on is not a selection.

items.title: Hover and pressed
items.text: Hover turns the fill to the page tone, and pressing turns it subtle. A chosen row keeps the subtle fill on hover.

items.title: Helper and error
items.text: Helper text sits under the row in secondary text, and an error turns the row red, marks the control invalid and shows under the row. Announce an error only if it appears after an action.

items.title: Layouts
items.text: The card layout is a bordered row with 16 px vertical and 12 px horizontal padding. The inline layout is a 24 px row without border or padding for menus and panels, and it does not tint on error.

items.title: Disabled
items.text: Disabling the control dims the row to 40 %, shows a not-allowed pointer and stops hover. The action is separate and stays active unless you disable it too.

items.title: Motion
items.text: Border and fill change quickly. Nothing moves, so the row has no layout animation.

items.title: Reduced motion
items.text: With reduced motion the colour changes still fade. Nothing in the row moves, so nothing else changes.

minimalUsage.expected: You see two bordered rows: Standard delivery with the indigo border and a filled radio, and Express delivery plain. A click anywhere on a row chooses it, and arrow keys move between them.

SelectorItem.title.description: The text that names the control, on one line. It becomes the accessible name of the control and is cut with an ellipsis when it is too long.

SelectorItem.description.description: A line of detail under the title. It describes the control for assistive technology and is cut with an ellipsis when it is too long.

SelectorItem.control.description: The control that the row toggles: a `RadioGroupItem` inside a `RadioGroup`, a `Checkbox` or a `Switch`. The row adds `aria-labelledby`, `aria-describedby` and, with `error`, `aria-invalid` to it.

SelectorItem.controlPosition.description: Which side of the text the control sits on. `trailing` puts it after the text and the metadata, `leading` puts it in front of the leading element.

SelectorItem.leading.description: An icon tile, an avatar or a logo before the text. The slot is at least 32 px wide and centres whatever you pass.

SelectorItem.metadata.description: Short secondary text before the control, such as a price or a count. It is inside the label and is not interactive.

SelectorItem.action.description: A secondary control beside the row, such as an Edit button. It is outside the label, so a click on it never toggles the control, and it has its own tab stop.

SelectorItem.helper.description: A hint under the row. It is linked to the control with `aria-describedby`.

SelectorItem.error.description: An error message under the row. It turns the card row red, marks the control `aria-invalid` and is linked to it with `aria-describedby`, so a screen reader reads it when the control gets focus.

SelectorItem.announceError.description: Reads the error at once with `role="alert"`. Set it only for an error that appears after an action, such as a failed submit; leave it off for an error that is there when the page loads.

SelectorItem.layout.description: `card` is the bordered row. `inline` is a 24 px row without border and padding.

SelectorItem.className.description: Extra classes for the row that holds the label and the action, merged with its own. Use it for spacing, not to recolour the row.

SelectorItemGroup.className.description: Extra classes, merged with the group's own `flex flex-col gap-2`. Use `min-w-0` when the group sits inside a flex row.

SelectorItem.icon.description: An icon in a 40 px tint-indigo tile in front of the text, with no rim. Ignored when `leading` is set.

SelectorItem.badge.description: A small pill next to the title, for example Recommended.

SelectorItem.badgeColor.description: The colour of the badge. `green` by default.

SelectorItem.selected.description: Shows the selected look (indigo tint, 1.5 px tint-text rim) without a checked control, for the current item of a link list. A checked radio or checkbox does it on its own.

SelectorItem.href.description: Link mode: the row is an anchor with a trailing chevron and no control. A `#` or empty href does not jump to the top.

SelectorItem.onSelect.description: Link mode: called when the row is pressed.

SelectorItemGroup.value.description: Radio mode: the chosen value. Setting any group prop turns the group into a radiogroup; without them it stays a plain list.

SelectorItemGroup.onValueChange.description: Called with the value of the row that was chosen.

SelectorItemGroup.name.description: The name under which the chosen value is submitted with a form.

SelectorItemGroup.required.description: A choice is required before the form can be sent.

SelectorItemGroup.disabled.description: Disables every row. The arrow keys skip disabled rows.

SelectorItemGroup.invalid.description: Marks the group invalid and gives the rows that are not chosen the error tint. Implied by `error`.

SelectorItemGroup.error.description: An error message under the list. It marks the group invalid, is linked with `aria-describedby` and is announced with `role="alert"`.

SelectorItemGroup.aria-label.description: Names the radiogroup. Give this or `aria-labelledby`.

parts.name: Label
parts.description: A native label in a row, 8 px between children, in 14 px medium text. Join it to a control by id, by wrapping the control, or with FieldLabel inside a Field; clicking it focuses the control.

parts.name: Requirement note
parts.description: A short word after the name, Required or Optional, in 12 px tertiary text. It sits inside the label, so it is part of the accessible name and a screen reader reads it too.

parts.name: Control
parts.description: The field the label names: an Input, a Textarea, a Checkbox. A label without a control is just text, and in a Field the label dims when the control is disabled.

items.text: Use a Label for every control with a visible name: above a field, to the left in a settings row, or to the right of a checkbox. Name a group of controls with a Fieldset legend, not a Label.
Join every label to its control: FieldLabel inside a Field, otherwise a matching id and htmlFor. The words then become a click target as large as the row.
Write the label as a short noun (Work email) and put a rule or an example in the helper line below the field. A label is a name, not a sentence.
Mark what is unusual: the optional fields in a mostly required form, the required ones in a mostly optional form. Put the note inside the label so it is read with the name.
Keep a label for a compact control and hide it visually. A search field without a visible label still has a name and a click target for assistive technology.
Keep buttons out of the label. An info tip next to a label is a sibling in the row, so clicking it doesn't focus the field.
Don't use a placeholder as the label. It is gone with the first keystroke and is not announced as a name on every screen reader.
Don't mark required with a colour or an asterisk alone. The word Required is readable by everyone; an asterisk needs an explanation on the page.
Don't leave a label unjoined. Text that looks like a label but has no link to the control gives it no name and no click target.

useFor: The visible name of an Input, a Textarea or a Checkbox
A requirement note, a link or an info tip on the row of a field
A name that only assistive technology sees (visually hidden)

useInstead.name: Field
useInstead.text: a label, control, helper and error line that are joined for you (FieldLabel)

useInstead.name: Fieldset
useInstead.text: the legend of a group of related controls

useInstead.name: Checkbox
useInstead.text: a checkbox with its label and description in one clickable row

useInstead.name: Tooltip
useInstead.text: a longer explanation next to a label, which does not fit in the helper line

behavior.intro: What the label does itself, and what it leaves to the page.

items.title: A native label
items.text: Label renders a native label, so linking by id, wrapping a control and click-to-focus are all the browser's doing. It isn't a tab stop; the control is.

items.title: Three ways to join
items.text: Three ways to join: an id with htmlFor, the control inside the label, or FieldLabel inside a Field, which joins the two for you. Pick one per control.

items.title: Accessible name
items.text: The label text, with the requirement note inside it, is the control's name. Full name Required is announced as the name, which is why the note is a plain word.

items.title: Row layout
items.text: A label is a flex row with 8 px between children, so a note sits after the name on the same line. A control inside the label needs a column layout to sit below it.

items.title: Disabled
items.text: Inside a Field, a label dims to 40 % when its control is disabled. Next to a control marked peer, a disabled control dims it too; elsewhere, dim it yourself.

items.title: Selection
items.text: The label text isn't selectable, so quick repeated clicks on it, as a person makes to focus a field, never select the words.

items.title: Hidden label
items.text: A visually hidden label stays in the page and out of the layout. It still names the control and still focuses it when a click lands on it.

items.title: Motion
items.text: A label does not move or change colour on its own.

minimalUsage.expected: You see the words Full name above a white field. Clicking the words focuses the field and turns its border indigo.
