parts.name: Field
parts.description: The wrapper of one control: a column with 4 px between its parts. It owns the name, invalid, disabled and validation state, and every part inside reads them.

parts.name: FieldLabel
parts.description: The visible name of the control, in 14 px medium text with 4 px below it. It is linked to the control, so a click on it focuses the control, and it dims with a disabled field.

parts.name: Control
parts.description: The control itself. An Input joins the Field by itself, any other control such as a Textarea joins through FieldControl, and the Field passes it the invalid and described-by attributes.

parts.name: FieldDescription
parts.description: The hint under the control in 12 px tertiary text. It is linked to the control, so a screen reader reads it after the label, and it dims with a disabled field.

parts.name: FieldError
parts.description: The error message in 12 px error text. It shows only while the field is invalid, is linked to the control and is left out while the field is disabled, so hide the hint while it shows.

items.text: Use Field around every control with a label, hint or error. It draws no box; put Fields in a Fieldset for a group, and use Form to send data and take server errors.
Put the label first, then the control, then the hint or the error. A label is a noun (Work email) and a hint is a full sentence.
Give each Field a name when it sits in a Form. The name is how an error you pass to the Form finds its field.
Write the error as an instruction: Enter an email address like name@company.com, not Invalid. Show it after the person leaves the field or sends the form, and keep what they typed.
Render the hint only while there is no error, so the error takes its place. Keep a line of room for the message so the controls below do not jump.
Mark an exception on the label row (Optional), not in the placeholder. A placeholder is gone once the person starts to type.
Don't build the label, hint and error by hand with label, p and ids. You lose the links that Field sets and the state that reaches every part.
Don't put two controls in one Field. The label names one control; two controls need a Fieldset with a legend.
Don't disable only the control and leave the Field enabled. The label and hint then stay at full strength next to a dimmed control.

useFor: A control that needs a label, a hint or an error message
A form where the state (invalid, disabled) must reach the label and the messages
A control that is not an Input, such as a Textarea, that should join a label and a hint

useInstead.name: Fieldset
useInstead.text: a group of related controls that share one legend, such as an address or a set of checkboxes

useInstead.name: Textarea
useInstead.text: a Textarea that brings its own label, helper line and error

useInstead.name: Checkbox
useInstead.text: one checkbox with its label and description in a single row

useInstead.name: Form
useInstead.text: the form that holds the Fields: submit, validation mode and server errors

behavior.intro: What Field does itself, and what it leaves to the page.

items.title: Label wiring
items.text: The label is linked to the control with generated ids, so you never write htmlFor. An Input inside an Input Group is still found, so the label points to the input and not the group.

items.title: Description and error wiring
items.text: The description and error register with the Field, and the control gets them as its description. A screen reader reads the label, the control, then the hint, and the error while it shows.

items.title: Invalid
items.text: Marking the Field invalid sets the invalid state on the Input, turns the border and focus ring red, and shows the error. The fill of the control stays white.

items.title: FieldError
items.text: The error shows only while the field is invalid, unless a match setting shows it at once or for one rule. Without children it prints the failed check's message.

items.title: Disabled
items.text: Disabled reaches the control, dims the label and hint to 40% and skips the control in the tab order. A Field inside a disabled Fieldset is disabled too.

items.title: Form
items.text: Inside a Form, give the Field a name. Errors passed to the Form by that name make the Field invalid and stay until you pass new ones, so clear them after the next submit.

items.title: Read-only
items.text: Read-only belongs to the control: set it on the Input. The control stays readable, focusable and copyable, and is filled with the subtle tone.

items.title: Motion
items.text: The Field adds no motion of its own. The control fades its border colour on the fast duration, and messages appear without moving the controls around them when you keep a line of room.

items.title: Reduced motion
items.text: Nothing moves, so there is nothing to reduce. The colour change of the control stays: it is a short fade, not movement.

minimalUsage.expected: You see the label Work email above a white field with a grey placeholder, and the hint below it. A click on the label focuses the field, and the border turns indigo.

Field.name.description: Identifies the field in a form. In a `Form` it is the key that the `errors` object uses to find this field, and the name of the value that `onFormSubmit` receives.

Field.invalid.description: Marks the field invalid. The control gets `aria-invalid`, the border and the ring turn red, and `FieldError` shows. Use it when you decide the state yourself; a Form's `errors` set it for you.

Field.disabled.description: Disables the control, dims the label and the hint to 40 % and skips the control in the tab order. It also takes the place of `disabled` on the control.

Field.validate.description: A function for a check of your own. It gets the value and the form values and returns a message (or an array of messages) when the value is wrong, and `null` when it is fine.

Field.validationMode.description: When `validate` runs: `onSubmit` (the default) checks on submit and again on every change after that, `onBlur` checks when the control loses focus, `onChange` checks on every change. It takes precedence over the same prop on the Form.

FieldLabel.nativeLabel.description: Whether the label is a native `<label>` element. It is by default. Set it to `false` when you replace the element through `render` with something that is not a label, such as a `div`, so it does not inherit label behaviour.

FieldControl.defaultValue.description: The value the control starts with when it keeps its own value. A plain `Input` takes `defaultValue` itself.

FieldError.match.description: When the error shows. `true` shows it at once, a validity key such as `valueMissing` or `typeMismatch` shows it for that rule only, and without it the error shows whenever the field is invalid.

parts.name: Fieldset
parts.description: The group: a native fieldset with the group role. By default it is a card with a thin border, 12 px corners and 16 px padding, and its legend is the accessible name of the group.

parts.name: FieldsetLegend
parts.description: The name of the group in 14 px semibold text. It can sit anywhere inside the fieldset, for example on a row with a note, and it dims with a disabled fieldset.

parts.name: Hint
parts.description: A line under the legend in 12 px tertiary text that states the rule. Link it to the fieldset so a screen reader reads it with the group.

parts.name: Controls
parts.description: The related controls: checkbox rows, a radio group or fields. Keep 12 px between rows of one kind and 16 px between columns.

parts.name: Legend note
parts.description: A word such as Required beside the legend, in 12 px tertiary text. It is for sighted readers, so put the rule itself in the hint where a screen reader hears it.

parts.name: Group error
parts.description: One message under the controls that says what to do, with a 14 px alert icon. Link it to the fieldset and mark the fieldset as invalid: the card then takes the red border and tint.

items.text: Use a Fieldset when several controls answer one question: a set of checkboxes, the radios of one choice, the fields of an address. One control with its own label needs a Field.
Write the legend as the question or the noun of the group, such as Notification channels or Shipping address. It is read before every control, so keep it short.
State the rule in a hint under the legend and link it to the fieldset. Say it before the person breaks it: Choose where we send alerts.
Show one error for the group, not one per control, and say what to do: Select at least one option to continue. Show it after the first try to continue, and keep what was chosen.
Use the plain surface when the group sits straight on the page, and the card when it must stand apart, such as an address block in a long form.
To switch a group off, disable the Fieldset. For a checkbox or radio group also disable the control, or wrap each in a Field, because only Fields read the Fieldset.
Don't use a Fieldset to draw a box around unrelated content. It names a group for assistive technology; use a Card for a visual container.
Don't nest a Fieldset in a Fieldset to indent. Nest only when the inner group has a name of its own.
Don't leave the legend out and put the question in a heading next to the group. The group then has no name for a screen reader.

useFor: A set of checkboxes that answer one question
The radios of one choice, or the fields of an address, under one name
A group that must be switched off or marked invalid as a whole

useInstead.name: Field
useInstead.text: one control with its own label, hint and error

useInstead.name: Card
useInstead.text: a visual container for unrelated content

useInstead.name: Radio Group
useInstead.text: the radio buttons themselves, when you need no legend, hint or error around them

useInstead.name: Form
useInstead.text: the form that holds the fieldsets: submit, validation mode and server errors

keyboard.intro: A fieldset takes no focus and has no keys of its own. Tab moves through the controls in it as it does anywhere, and a radio group inside it keeps its arrow keys.

rows.action: Moves focus to the next or previous control inside the group. A disabled fieldset takes its fields out of the order.
Inside a radio group in the fieldset, moves the choice to the next or previous option. The legend plays no part.

behavior.intro: What the fieldset does itself, and what it leaves to the page.

items.title: Group semantics
items.text: A native fieldset has the group role, and the legend links to it, so a screen reader says Notification channels, group when focus enters. The legend is a div, so it can sit on a row with a note.

items.title: Hint and error
items.text: The fieldset sets no description of its own. Give the hint and group error an id and list them on the fieldset, and announce the error or move focus when it appears, since it is not a live region.

items.title: Invalid
items.text: There is no invalid prop: set the invalid data attribute for a red border and tint. The controls inside decide for themselves, so mark checkboxes, radio groups or Fields invalid too.

items.title: Disabled
items.text: Disabled dims the legend to 40% and disables every Field inside and all native controls. A Checkbox or Radio Group outside a Field does not read the fieldset, so disable it too.

items.title: Surface
items.text: The default is a card with a border, 12 px corners and 16 px padding, with 20 px between its children. Remove the border, background and padding with a class name to get the plain group.

items.title: Motion
items.text: The fieldset has no motion of its own. The controls inside change their colours on the fast duration with the entrance curve.

items.title: Reduced motion
items.text: Nothing moves, so there is nothing to reduce. The colour changes of the controls stay: they are short fades, not movement.

minimalUsage.expected: You see a card with the legend Notification channels and two checkbox rows. A screen reader announces the group name when focus enters the first box.

FieldsetLegend.className.description: Extra classes for the legend, for example `mb-1`. Put the legend and a note on one row by wrapping both in a `div` with `flex items-baseline gap-2`.

parts.description: The row of buttons at the end, built with FormActions. The submit button sends the form, and so does Enter in a text field.

items.text: Use a Form for everything a person sends together. A single field that acts at once, like a search box, needs no Form, and a setting that applies immediately is a Switch.
Give every Field a name and handle the send in the submit handler. It gets the values by name and only runs when every field is valid, so Enter and the Save button take the same path.
Say what to do in the message: Enter a work email address, like name@company.com, not Invalid input. Show it under the field and keep what the person typed.
After a failed send, move focus to the first invalid field, and add an error summary to long forms. The summary jumps to each field and never replaces the message at the field.
Show the work: a pending Save with its own label (Saving…), the way out disabled, and a confirmation when done. Say All changes saved in the status line, not only with colour.
Keep the default: validate on submit, then re-check as the person corrects. Validate on blur for fields that are costly to get wrong, such as an address.
Don't disable the submit button to flag an invalid form, since it gives no reason. Let the person press it and tell them what is wrong; disable it only when there is nothing to send.
Don't clear the fields after an error or a server failure. Name the problem, keep the entries and offer Try again.
Don't run the check from a click handler on the submit button. Use the submit handler so keyboard and mouse users take the same path.

useFor: A group of fields that are sent together, such as a profile, an address or a payment
A form that has to check its fields, show what is wrong and say when it has saved
A form whose rules only the server knows, such as a name that is already taken

useInstead.name: Field
useInstead.text: one labelled control with a helper and an error line, inside a form or on its own

useInstead.name: Fieldset
useInstead.text: a group of related fields that share a legend, such as an address

useInstead.name: Switch
useInstead.text: a setting that takes effect at once, without a save

keyboard.intro: A form adds no keys of its own. Keyboard behaviour comes from the order of its controls and the browser's implicit submit.

rows.action: Moves through the fields and buttons in the order they are written. A disabled button is skipped; a pending button stays in the order.
In a text field, sends the form through its submit button. If a field is invalid, focus goes to the first one and its message shows. In a textarea it starts a new line.
On a focused button, presses it. On the summary lines, moves focus to the field that is named.

behavior.intro: What the form does itself, and what it leaves to the page.

items.title: A native form
items.text: Form renders a native form element, so action, method and onSubmit all work. It turns off the browser's own validation bubbles so fields show their own messages.

items.title: Submit
items.text: The submit handler runs when every field is valid and gets an object with the value of each named field. It also stops the page from reloading, so name every Field: the name is the key.

items.title: When fields are checked
items.text: Validation mode sets when fields are checked: on submit (default, then re-checks as the person types), on blur, or on every change. A Field can set its own mode.

items.title: Errors from outside
items.text: Pass server errors as field names and messages, and the matching Field turns invalid and shows its message. Clear it when the person edits the field, or the red state stays.

items.title: Focus after a failed send
items.text: After a failed send, focus moves to the first invalid field in page order, and that field is marked invalid. If you check fields yourself, move focus the same way.

items.title: Pending and success
items.text: While the send runs, the main Button is pending: it keeps its place, shows a spinner and ignores presses, and the way out is disabled. When it ends, show the result in an Alert and the status line.

items.title: Pristine and unsaved
items.text: A form with nothing to send, like a settings form without changes, may keep Save disabled. Once a field differs from what is saved, the status line says unsaved and Save is available.

items.title: Status messages
items.text: The status line is a polite live region: changes are announced after the current speech and never take focus. The error summary is an alert and is announced at once.

items.title: Motion
items.text: The form doesn't move. Field borders change colour quickly and the spinner in a pending button turns.

items.title: Reduced motion
items.text: With reduced motion, border colours still change as a short fade and spinners stop turning. The pending label still says what is happening.

import { Button } from "@/components/ui/button"
import { Field, FieldError, FieldLabel } from "@/components/ui/field"
import { Form } from "@/components/ui/form"
import { Input } from "@/components/ui/input"

export function Subscribe() {
  return (
    <Form onFormSubmit={(values) => console.log(values)}>
      <Field name="email">
        <FieldLabel>Work email</FieldLabel>
        <Input type="email" required placeholder="name@company.com" />
        <FieldError match="valueMissing">Enter your work email address.</FieldError>
        <FieldError match="typeMismatch">Enter an email address like name@company.com.</FieldError>
      </Field>
      <Button type="submit" variant="gradient">
        Subscribe
      </Button>
    </Form>
  )
}
minimalUsage.expected: You see a label, a white field and a Subscribe button. With the field empty, pressing it turns the field red and shows its message; with an address, the form sends.

Form.onFormSubmit.description: Called with the values of the named fields when every field is valid. `values` is an object keyed by the `name` of each Field. It stops the page from reloading for you. `details.event` is the submit event.

Form.errors.description: Errors that come from outside, usually from a server after a send. The keys are Field names and the values are the message or messages. The Field with that name turns invalid and its `FieldError` shows the message. Clear it when the person edits the field.

Form.validationMode.description: When the fields are checked. `onSubmit` (the default) checks at the first send and re-checks as the person types afterwards, `onBlur` checks when a field loses focus and `onChange` checks on every change. The `validationMode` of a Field takes precedence.

Form.actionsRef.description: A ref to imperative actions. `validate()` checks every field and `validate("name")` checks one, for example before the next step of a wizard.

Form.className.description: Classes for the form. They replace the default stack (`flex flex-col gap-5`) where they conflict, so `gap-4` tightens it. It also takes a function of the form state.

Form.render.description: Replaces the `<form>` element with another element or component, for example a framework's own form component. It also takes a function that returns the element.

Form.style.description: Inline style for the form, or a function of the form state that returns one.

parts.name: InputGroup
parts.description: The bordered frame: 1 px border, 8 px corner, white fill, 36 px high. It owns the hover border, the focus ring and the red invalid border, so the input inside loses its own.

parts.name: Leading content
parts.description: An icon or short text before the value, such as a search icon, a mail icon or https://. It isn't interactive, uses the tertiary text colour and keeps icons at 16 px.

parts.name: Input
parts.description: The field itself: a plain Input or any native input as a direct child. It fills the remaining space with no border, fill or padding of its own, and the frame reads its invalid and disabled state.

parts.name: Trailing content
parts.description: A unit, shortcut or button after the value: USD, a key hint, show or hide, clear, copy. A button here is a 32 px IconButton set 2 px inside the frame with a 6 px corner, concentric with the group.

parts.description: The ready-made copy field: a read-only input and a Copy button inside one group. The button turns into a check with Copied for 1.5 s and a polite live region says so. It replaces InviteLinkRow.

items.text: Use an Input Group when something belongs inside the field's border: an icon, a fixed part of the value or a small action on it. Other actions are buttons beside the field.
Put the input as a direct child of the group. The group styles direct child inputs and can't reach one wrapped in another element.
Keep the corners concentric. A 32 px IconButton in a 36 px group sits 2 px inside the border, so give it a 6 px corner and trim the group's padding on that side.
Name the button with aria-label and use aria-pressed for a toggle such as show or hide. An icon alone is not a name.
Set aria-invalid and disabled on the input, not on the group. The group reads them and turns the border red or dims itself.
For the other sizes, give the group a height class for the small or large field height. The inner button stays 32 px, so use it in the default and large sizes.
Don't put the main action of a form inside the field. Apply, Send and Subscribe are buttons of their own, next to the field.
Don't put a second field or a long text in an addon. An addon is a unit, an icon or a short word.
Don't rely on the addon text for the field's name. https:// is part of the value; the field still needs a Label.

useFor: A field with an icon, a prefix or a unit, such as a search field, https:// or USD
A small action on the value: clear, copy, show or hide, a stepper, retry
A shortcut hint at the end of a field

useInstead.text: a plain field with no content inside it

useInstead.name: Number Field

useInstead.name: Select

useInstead.name: Combobox

keyboard.intro: The group isn't a tab stop. Focus goes to the input and then to each button inside, in the order they are written.

rows.action: Moves into the input, then to each button inside the group, then on. A disabled input and its buttons are skipped. The frame draws the ring while the input has focus.
In the input, sends the form that holds it. On a button, presses it.
Presses a focused button, such as show or hide, and toggles its `aria-pressed`.

behavior.intro: What the group does itself, and what it leaves to the page.

items.title: The frame draws the border
items.text: The group owns the border, white fill and corner. A direct child input is made transparent and borderless, so the addons sit flush inside one box.

items.title: Hover and focus
items.text: The border darkens when the pointer is over the group. When the input has keyboard focus, the group border turns indigo with a 2 px ring; clicking an addon doesn't focus the input.

items.title: Invalid
items.text: An input marked invalid turns the border red, and the ring turns red on focus. The fill stays white, and the message is yours to write in an error under the group.

items.title: Disabled and read-only
items.text: A disabled input dims the group to 40 % and blocks the pointer. Read-only does neither, so give the group a subtle fill to look read-only; it stays focusable and copyable.

items.title: Height and size
items.text: The group is 36 px tall at the default density. Use the small or large field height for 32 or 40 px; in comfortable density the same tokens give 36, 44 and 52 px.

items.title: Addons
items.text: An addon is a flex slot that keeps its size, with tertiary text and 16 px icons. It has no hover or press state, so use an IconButton for an action.

items.title: Buttons inside
items.text: A 32 px ghost IconButton fits inside the 36 px group with 2 px of air and a 6 px corner (the group's 8 px minus that gap). Trim the group's padding on that side so the air is even.

items.title: Loading
items.text: There is no loading prop. Put a Spinner in a trailing addon, set aria-busy on the input and keep it editable, so a background check never blocks typing.

items.title: Motion
items.text: The border colour changes quickly when the pointer enters or the input takes focus. Nothing moves or scales.

items.title: Reduced motion
items.text: With reduced motion the border colour change stays as a short fade, and a spinner in an addon stops turning.

parts.name: Label
parts.description: The visible name of the field: a Label whose htmlFor matches the NumberField id, so a click on it focuses the input. A field with no room for a label takes an aria-label on the input.

parts.name: NumberField
parts.description: The root. It holds the number (null when empty), the limits, the steps and the format, and it has no element of its own; its id goes on the input.

parts.name: NumberFieldGroup
parts.description: The bordered frame around the buttons and input: 36 px high, 8 px corner, 1 px dividers. It carries the hover border, the indigo focus ring and the red error state.

parts.name: NumberFieldDecrement
parts.description: The minus button on the left, 36 px wide. It lowers the value by one step and dims at the minimum; its default name is Decrease, so name it after what it changes.

parts.name: NumberFieldInput
parts.description: The text input, 64 px wide by default with the number centred. It accepts only number characters, formats on blur and answers arrow keys, Home and End.

parts.name: NumberFieldIncrement

items.text: Give the field a visible label joined by htmlFor and the NumberField id. Where a column header already names it, put an aria-label on the input.
Set min, max and step to the real limits, such as 1 to 50. The buttons stop at the edges and Home and End jump to them.
Name the buttons after what they change, such as Add a seat and Remove a seat. The defaults, Increase and Decrease, do not say what grows.
Put the unit in the format (for example kilograms) or in the label, so the number is never read without it. Widen the input when the formatted text is longer than 64 px.
Treat the value as a number or null. A field the person emptied reports null, not 0; show an error under it and mark the input invalid.
Don't use it for a number nobody steps in small amounts, such as a year or a phone number. Use an Input with a numeric keyboard.
Don't use it for a count of one to ten where there is no typing. Number Stepper is a smaller control for that.
Don't leave the input without a name. The buttons have names; the input needs a label or an aria-label.

keyboard.intro: The input is a text field that knows numbers. Arrow keys step the value; Shift and Alt change the step size.

rows.action: Moves focus into the input and out of it. The plus and minus buttons are not tab stops: the keyboard path is the arrow keys in the input. A disabled field is skipped.
Raises or lowers the value by `step`. At `min` or `max` it stops.
Steps by `largeStep`, 10 by default.
Steps by `smallStep`, 0.1 by default.
Jumps to `min` or to `max`. It only works when that limit is set.
Types a number. Letters and other characters are not taken, and the formatted text is read back into a number when you leave the field.

behavior.intro: What the field does with its value, its limits, errors and motion.

items.title: Value or null
items.text: The change handler gets a number, or null when the field is empty. The field never turns an empty input into 0.

items.title: Format and locale
items.text: The format takes Intl.NumberFormat options such as currency, percent or unit. Text follows the locale and is read back when you leave the field, and a percent is a fraction: 0.15 shows as 15%.

items.title: Limits
items.text: A typed value outside the limits is corrected when you leave the field; arrow keys and buttons never pass them. Allow out-of-range values if you want to report them yourself.

items.title: Buttons at the edge
items.text: At the minimum the minus button and at the maximum the plus button are disabled and dim to 40%. The buttons are for the pointer and are not tab stops; the keyboard uses the arrow keys.

items.title: Error
items.text: Set aria-invalid on the input and the frame turns red, with a red focus ring. Put the message in an element and point aria-describedby at it; the white fill stays.

items.title: Disabled and read-only
items.text: Disabled dims the whole frame to 40% and takes it out of the tab order. A read-only field cannot be stepped, its buttons are disabled, and the frame dims the same way.

items.title: Width
items.text: The group is as wide as its parts: 36 px per button and 64 px for the input. Give the input a width class for longer values, or make the group full width to fill a column.

items.title: Scroll wheel
items.text: The wheel does not change the value. Turn on wheel scrubbing to let it change the value while the field is focused and the pointer is over it.

items.title: Motion
items.text: The border and the button fills change colour quickly. Nothing moves.

items.title: Reduced motion
items.text: There is no movement to remove, so reduced motion changes nothing. The colour changes stay.

parts.name: Label
parts.description: The visible name of the code: a Label whose htmlFor matches the OtpField id. It names the group and the first slot, and a click on it focuses the field.

parts.name: OtpField
parts.description: The group of slots: it holds the code as one string, moves focus and reports when the last slot is filled. A hidden input submits the code with the form.

parts.name: OtpFieldInput
parts.description: One slot per character: a native input, 40 px square with an 8 px corner. Only one slot is in the tab order, so give every slot after the first an aria-label such as Digit 2 of 6.

parts.name: Message
parts.description: The 12 px line under the slots: a FieldDescription with the rule, a FieldError with what to do, or a status for an expired, pending or verified code. An error replaces the helper.

parts.name: OtpFieldCode
parts.description: The ready-made code field: 4 or 6 boxes of 56 by 64 px with an 8 px gap in a named group, every digit announced as Digit n of N. Use it instead of assembling OtpField and OtpFieldInput yourself; it replaces OtpCodeInput.

items.text: Use an OTP Field for a short code typed once: an email or SMS code, an authenticator code, a PIN. For dashed codes, long letter codes or a recovery key, use an Input.
Render one OtpFieldInput per character and set the same number as the length. A six-digit code needs six slots.
Give the field a visible Label whose htmlFor matches the id, and name every slot after the first with an aria-label such as Digit 2 of 6, so a screen reader announces the position.
Leave autoComplete at its one-time-code default, so a phone offers the code from the message. The first slot takes the paste and spreads it across the slots.
Check the code in the complete handler, or turn on auto-submit inside a form. The person should not have to find a button after the last digit.
Say what to do when a code fails, with a message like That code is not correct, or one for an expired code with a Resend action. Keep what was typed so one digit can be fixed.
Don't change the length while the person is typing, and don't mix code lengths in one field. Render another field instead.
Don't use an OTP Field for a long or free-form value. A long code is hard to check by eye in slots; use an Input.
Don't use real or reused codes in examples, tests or screenshots. Use demo values such as 470921.

useFor: A one-time code sent by email or SMS, typed once to confirm an address or a phone
A code from an authenticator app when someone signs in with two steps
A short PIN of 4 to 8 digits, masked or visible

useInstead.name: Input
useInstead.text: a code with dashes, a license key or any value longer than a few characters

useInstead.name: Number Field
useInstead.text: a quantity that people step up and down

useInstead.name: Field
useInstead.text: the label, message and validation around any control, including this one

keyboard.intro: The group is one tab stop, with focus on the next empty slot or on the last one when the code is complete. Inside it the keys move between slots.

rows.action: Moves focus into and out of the group. The slots are not separate tab stops, so one Tab passes the whole code. A disabled field is skipped; a read-only one keeps its place.
Types a character into the focused slot and moves to the next. A character that the `validationType` rejects is ignored and reported in `onValueInvalid`.
Clears the focused slot and moves to the previous one. In an empty slot it clears the previous slot first.
Removes the character of the focused slot. The characters after it move one slot forward.
Clears the whole code and puts focus on the first slot.
Moves focus to the previous or next slot. With Ctrl or Cmd it jumps to the first slot, or to the next empty one.
Moves focus to the first slot.
Moves focus to the next empty slot, or to the last slot when the code is complete.
Pastes into the focused slot and the ones after it. Characters the `validationType` rejects, and spaces, are dropped; a code that is too long is cut at `length`.
Sends the form that holds the field, like any native input. With `autoSubmit` the form is sent by itself when the last slot is filled.

behavior.intro: What the field does with the value, the focus and the label, and what it leaves to the page.

items.title: One value
items.text: The field holds the code as one string, not one value per slot. Control it with a value and change handler, or let a default value keep it.

items.title: Auto-advance
items.text: Typing moves focus to the next slot, Backspace moves it back, and arrow keys, Home and End move it freely. Clicking focuses a slot, and only the active slot is in the tab order.

items.title: Paste and autofill
items.text: A paste spreads over the slots from the focused one, after rejected characters are removed. The first slot offers one-time-code autofill, so a phone can fill the whole code in one step.

items.title: Characters
items.text: The validation type is numeric by default, or alpha, alphanumeric or none, and it sets the phone keyboard and filters typing and pasting. Mask turns the slots into password inputs for a PIN.

items.title: Completion
items.text: The complete handler fires with the code when the last slot is filled, and again when a full code is pasted over a full one. Auto-submit sends the form at that moment.

items.title: Labelling
items.text: The Label names the group and the first slot; slots after the first need your aria-label, or a screen reader calls them unnamed. FieldDescription and FieldError describe the group.

items.title: Invalid
items.text: Inside an invalid Field every slot gets a red border and focus ring, and the fill stays white. The message is yours: write it in a FieldError under the slots, which replaces the helper line.

items.title: Disabled and read-only
items.text: Disabled dims the slots to 40%, takes them out of the tab order and leaves the code out of the form data. Read-only keeps them focusable, blocks typing and paste, and uses the subtle tone.

items.title: Expired, verifying and verified
items.text: No prop covers these states: expired is a read-only field with a warning and a Resend action, pending sets aria-busy with a spinner message, and verified is read-only with a check message.

items.title: Form data
items.text: OtpField renders a hidden input that carries the whole code under the name, with required and form applied to it. The slots have no name, so the code is submitted once.

items.title: Motion
items.text: The border colour of a slot changes quickly on hover and focus. Nothing moves or scales, and typing never animates.

items.title: Reduced motion
items.text: With reduced motion the colour change stays, since it is a short fade and not movement. The spinner in a verifying message stops turning.

minimalUsage.expected: You see the label Verification code above six empty boxes. Typing 470921 moves focus from box to box and logs the code, and pasting six digits into the first box fills all six.

OtpField.length.description: The number of slots, and so the length of the code. Required: the group uses it to cut a paste, detect completion and render the hidden input before the slots mount. Render the same number of `OtpFieldInput`.

OtpField.value.description: The code, for a controlled field. A string with at most `length` characters; a shorter string leaves the last slots empty.

OtpField.defaultValue.description: The code the field starts with, for an uncontrolled field.

OtpField.onValueChange.description: Called with the new code and the reason (`input-change`, `input-clear`, `input-paste` or `keyboard`) whenever a character is typed, pasted or removed.

OtpField.onValueComplete.description: Called with the code when the last slot is filled, or when a complete code is pasted over a complete one. It runs after `onValueChange`, so check the code here.

OtpField.onValueInvalid.description: Called with the attempted text when typed or pasted characters are rejected by `validationType` or `normalizeValue`, before the value changes. Use it to show a hint such as `Digits only`.

OtpField.validationType.description: Which characters the slots take: `numeric` (default), `alpha`, `alphanumeric` or `none`. It filters typing and paste and sets the keyboard on a phone.

OtpField.normalizeValue.description: A function that changes the code after the filter, for example `(value) => value.toUpperCase()`. It runs on typed, pasted, controlled and default values.

OtpField.mask.description: Shows the characters as dots by making the slots password inputs. Use it for a PIN. It does not change what the form submits.

OtpField.autoSubmit.description: Sends the form around the field when the code is complete, by calling `requestSubmit` on it.

OtpField.autoComplete.description: The `autocomplete` of the first slot and the hidden input. Defaults to `one-time-code`; the other slots are always `off`.

OtpField.inputMode.description: The virtual keyboard of the slots. The `validationType` sets a fitting one (`numeric` for digits, `text` for letters); set it only to override that.

OtpField.disabled.description: Dims the field to 40 %, removes it from the tab order and leaves the code out of the form data.

OtpField.readOnly.description: Keeps the field readable and focusable but blocks typing, paste and Backspace. It is submitted with the form.

OtpField.required.description: Marks the field as required. The form cannot be sent until every slot is filled.

OtpField.name.description: The name under which the whole code is submitted with a form, through the hidden input.

OtpField.form.description: The `id` of a form elsewhere in the page that the hidden input belongs to, for a field that sits outside its form.

OtpField.id.description: The `id` of the first slot; the others get `{id}-2`, `{id}-3` and so on. Use it as the `htmlFor` of the label.

OtpFieldInput.className.description: Extra classes on the slot, for example a different size. The default is 40 px square.

OtpFieldCode.length.description: The number of boxes, 4 or 6. 6 by default.

OtpFieldCode.value.description: The code, for a controlled field. A string of at most `length` digits.

OtpFieldCode.onValueChange.description: Called with the code whenever a digit is typed, pasted or removed.

OtpFieldCode.onComplete.description: Called with the code once the last box is filled. Check the code here.

OtpFieldCode.invalid.description: Marks every box invalid: a red border and `aria-invalid`. The field shows no message, so write the text yourself.

OtpFieldCode.disabled.description: Dims the boxes to 40 % and takes them out of the tab order.

OtpFieldCode.autoFocus.description: Focuses the first box on mount.

OtpFieldCode.aria-label.description: Names the group for a screen reader. Each box is announced as Digit n of N. "One-time code" by default.

OtpFieldCode.className.description: Extra classes on the group, for example `justify-center` so the boxes centre in a narrow column.

parts.name: Combobox
parts.description: The root. It holds the chosen value, the typed text, the items and the filter, and the value is an item or null, or an array with multiple.

parts.name: ComboboxInputGroup
parts.description: The bordered frame around the input and the chevron, 36 px high with an 8 px corner. It draws the border and focus ring, dims when disabled and turns red when the input is invalid.

parts.name: ComboboxInput
parts.description: The text input: typing filters the list, arrow keys move through it, Enter chooses and Escape closes. Give it a visible label or an aria-label.

parts.name: ComboboxTrigger
parts.description: The chevron button that opens and closes the whole list. It is named Show options and is not in the tab order, because the keyboard opens the list from the input.

parts.name: ComboboxPopup
parts.description: The list panel. It brings its own portal and positioner, matches the width of the field and scrolls when it runs out of room.

parts.name: ComboboxList
parts.description: Renders the entries. Pass a render function as the child, so the filtered list, not the full one, is mapped, and with groups it receives one group at a time.

parts.name: ComboboxGroup
parts.description: Holds the entries of one group under a group label. A group without a match disappears with its label.

parts.name: ComboboxGroupLabel
parts.description: The heading of a group, in 12 px medium muted text. It is not an entry, so arrow keys skip it.

parts.name: ComboboxItem
parts.description: One entry, 32 px high for a single line, whose value is what the field holds when chosen. A row can hold an icon, or an avatar and a second line, and the highlighted row takes the page fill.

parts.name: Check
parts.description: A 16 px check at the right of the chosen entry. With multiple, every chosen entry shows one.

parts.name: ComboboxEmpty
parts.description: A centred line shown in place of the list when nothing matches. It is hidden while it has no content.

parts.name: ComboboxPortal
parts.description: Moves the list to the end of the document. The popup already renders it, so you only need it for a custom container.

items.text: Give the input a visible label that points at it. The placeholder is a hint such as Search projects, not the name of the field.
Always include an empty-state line with a sentence such as No projects match, so a list without matches never looks broken.
Keep the state as a value or null. It is null while nothing is chosen and after the choice is cleared.
With multiple, show the chosen entries next to the field, as a count or a list. The field only shows what people type.
Group a long list by what people already know, such as an area or a team, and pass the groups as the items.
Don't use it for free text. Text that is not an entry is dropped when the field loses focus, so use an Autocomplete when any value is valid.
Don't use it for a short list people can see at a glance. A Select is quicker when there are about a dozen options or fewer.
Don't turn on multiple and then hide the choices. People cannot tell what is selected from a closed field with a placeholder.

useFor: Choosing one entry from a long list people can search, such as a country, a project or a person
Choosing several entries, such as the teams to filter a table by
Any field whose value must be one of the entries

useInstead.name: Select
useInstead.text: a short list where typing is not needed

useInstead.name: Autocomplete
useInstead.text: free text that only gets suggestions

useInstead.name: Radio Group
useInstead.text: two to four options that should all be visible

keyboard.intro: The input is a native text field, so the browser handles focus, typing and the caret. Focus stays in the input while the list is open, and the chevron button is not in the tab order.

rows.action: Moves focus into the field and out of it. Leaving closes the list. Text that was typed but not chosen is dropped, and the field shows the chosen entry again.
Typing opens the list and keeps the entries that match.

Opens the list if it is closed, then moves the highlight to the next or previous entry. With an entry chosen the list opens with it highlighted. At the end of the list focus goes back to the text with nothing highlighted.
Chooses the highlighted entry: the field shows its label and the list closes. With `multiple` it toggles the entry and the list stays open.
Closes the list. Pressed again, it clears the choice.

behavior.intro: What the field does with its value, the typed text, the list and motion.

items.title: A value from the list
items.text: The value is an entry of the items, or null while nothing is chosen. Typing alone never sets it, so the value changes only when an entry is chosen.

items.title: Opening
items.text: The list opens on a click in the field, on typing, on the chevron and on Arrow Down. The chevron button opens and closes it.

items.title: Filtering
items.text: An entry matches when it contains the typed text, ignoring case and accents. You can replace the rule or cap the list, and after a choice the list opens unfiltered.

items.title: Groups
items.text: Pass groups as items with a label and entries, and render a group and group label for each. The filter works across groups, and a group with no match disappears with its label.

items.title: Single and multiple
items.text: By default one entry is chosen and the list closes. With multiple the value is an array, the list stays open and every chosen entry shows a check, but the field does not list them.

items.title: Objects as items
items.text: Items can be objects. Give each item the object as its value, the root a function for the field text, and an equality check when the objects are not the same references.

items.title: Position and size
items.text: The list opens 4 px below the field, as wide as the field, and flips above when there is no room below. It scrolls when it is taller than the room left.

items.title: Invalid and disabled
items.text: Marking the input invalid turns the border and focus ring red, so say why in a line under the field. Disabling the root dims the field to 40 % and it ignores pointer and keyboard.

items.title: Previews in these docs
items.text: The list normally floats over the page, but the previews here draw it inside the card. Point at a card or focus it, and the field behaves like the real one.

items.title: Motion
items.text: The list appears and disappears at once. Nothing else on the field moves, and the border and focus ring change colour quickly.

items.title: Reduced motion
items.text: There is no movement to remove, so reduced motion changes nothing. The colour change is a short fade and stays.

Combobox.items.description: The entries: a flat array, an array of groups (`{ label, items }`) or a collection from `Combobox.createItems()`. A flat array or groups give `Value` its type.

Combobox.value.description: The chosen entry, or `null` while nothing is chosen. With `multiple` it is an array. It is a controlled value: update it in `onValueChange`.

Combobox.defaultValue.description: The entry that is chosen when you do not control the value.

Combobox.onValueChange.description: Called with the new choice: the entry, or `null` when the choice is cleared. With `multiple` it is the whole array.

Combobox.multiple.description: Lets people choose several entries. The value becomes an array, the list stays open while they choose, and each chosen entry shows a check.

Combobox.inputValue.description: The text in the field, when you control it. Pair it with `onInputValueChange`.

Combobox.defaultInputValue.description: The text the field starts with when you do not control it.

Combobox.onInputValueChange.description: Called with the new text each time the person types or the field changes to show a choice.

Combobox.filter.description: Replaces the matching rule. It receives an entry, the typed text and the function that turns an entry into text, and returns whether the entry stays in the list. `null` switches filtering off.

Combobox.itemToStringLabel.description: Turns an object entry into the text of the field and the text the filter matches against. Needed when the entries are objects.

Combobox.isItemEqualToValue.description: Decides whether an entry is the chosen value. Needed when entries are objects that are not the same references as the value.

Combobox.autoHighlight.description: Highlights the first matching entry while people type, so Enter chooses it.

Combobox.limit.description: The most entries the list shows. `-1`, the default, shows every match.

Combobox.openOnInputClick.description: Opens the list when the field is clicked. On by default.

Combobox.open.description: Whether the list is open, when you control it. Pair it with `onOpenChange`.

Combobox.defaultOpen.description: Whether the list starts open when you do not control it.

Combobox.onOpenChange.description: Called when the list opens or closes, with the reason, such as typing, a key press, an outside press or choosing an entry.

Combobox.disabled.description: Disables the field: it dims to 40 % and ignores the pointer and the keyboard.

Combobox.readOnly.description: Keeps the value but stops people from choosing another entry.

Combobox.required.description: Marks the field as required for the form it belongs to.

Combobox.name.description: The name the chosen value is submitted under in a form.

ComboboxInputGroup.className.description: Extra classes for the frame, for example `w-72` for a fixed width or `h-(--field-lg)` for the large height.

ComboboxInput.className.description: Extra classes for the input inside the frame.

ComboboxInput.disabled.description: Disables this input only. Prefer `disabled` on the root, which also dims the frame.

ComboboxTrigger.className.description: Extra classes for the chevron button.

ComboboxPopup.className.description: Extra classes for the list panel, for example `min-w-64` to make it wider than the field.

ComboboxPopup.finalFocus.description: Where focus goes when the list closes. It stays in the input by default.

ComboboxPopup.initialFocus.description: Where focus goes when the list opens. It stays in the input by default, so people can keep typing.

ComboboxList.children.description: A render function that receives the entries that match, or the groups that have a match, and returns the rows.

ComboboxList.className.description: Extra classes for the list element inside the panel.

ComboboxGroup.items.description: The entries of this group. Pass the group's own `items` so the list can tell which entries belong to it.

ComboboxGroup.className.description: Extra classes for the group wrapper.

ComboboxGroupLabel.className.description: Extra classes for the group heading.

ComboboxItem.value.description: The entry this row stands for, the same string or object as in `items`. It is what the field holds when the row is chosen.

ComboboxItem.disabled.description: Stops the row from being highlighted or chosen.

ComboboxItem.onClick.description: Called when the row is clicked or chosen with Enter.

ComboboxItem.className.description: Extra classes for the row, for example `gap-3` for a row with an avatar.

ComboboxEmpty.className.description: Extra classes for the line shown when nothing matches.

ComboboxPortal.container.description: The element the list is moved into. The end of the document by default.

ComboboxPortal.keepMounted.description: Keeps the list in the DOM while it is closed.

parts.name: Autocomplete
parts.description: The root. It holds the field's text, the items and the filter and renders nothing itself; the value is the text in the input, not a chosen item.

parts.name: AutocompleteInputGroup
parts.description: The bordered frame around the input, 36 px high with an 8 px corner. It draws the border and focus ring, dims when disabled and turns red when invalid, so put an icon beside the input inside it.

parts.name: AutocompleteInput
parts.description: The text input. Typing filters the suggestions, arrow keys move through them, Enter takes one and Escape closes the list; give it a visible label or an aria-label.

parts.name: AutocompletePopup
parts.description: The suggestion panel. It brings its own portal and positioner, matches the field's width and scrolls when it runs out of room.

parts.name: AutocompleteList
parts.description: Renders the items. Pass a render function as the child so the filtered list, not the full one, is mapped.

parts.name: AutocompleteItem
parts.description: One suggestion, 32 px high for a single line, whose value fills the field when chosen. A row can hold an icon, or an avatar and a second line, and the highlighted row gets the page fill.

parts.name: AutocompleteEmpty
parts.description: A centred line shown in place of the list when nothing matches. It is hidden while it has no content.

parts.name: AutocompletePortal
parts.description: Moves the list to the end of the document. The popup already uses it; you only need it for a custom container.

items.text: Give the input a visible label. The placeholder is a hint such as Search cities, not the name of the field.
Always add an empty-state line with a sentence like No cities match, so a list without matches never looks broken.
Control the value with state when the text drives something else, such as a server search. The value is the text of the field, never an item object.
Keep the suggestions few, five to eight, and one line each. Cap a long list with a limit; people pick by reading, so rows with several lines or controls slow them down.
Don't treat the value as validated. Text that matches no suggestion still ends up in the value, so check it on submit or use a Combobox.
Don't use it for a choice that must come from the list. A Combobox keeps the field on a value of the list and tells people when nothing matches.
Don't use it as a menu of actions. Suggestions fill a field; actions belong in a Dropdown Menu.

useFor: Free text with help, such as a city, a search term or a label that may be new
A field where any value is valid and the suggestions only save typing
Search boxes whose suggestions come from your own data

useInstead.name: Combobox
useInstead.text: the answer must be one of the entries

useInstead.name: Select
useInstead.text: a short, fixed list, with no typing

useInstead.name: Dropdown Menu
useInstead.text: a list of actions, not a value for a field

keyboard.intro: The input is a native text field, so the browser provides focus, typing and the caret. The list is not in the tab order: arrow keys reach it from the input, and focus stays there.

rows.action: Moves focus into the field and out of it. Leaving closes the list and keeps the text.
Typing opens the list and keeps the suggestions that match. Clearing the field closes it again.

Opens the list if it is closed, then moves the highlight to the next or previous suggestion. At the end of the list focus goes back to the text with nothing highlighted, and one more press starts at the other end.
Takes the highlighted suggestion: it fills the field and closes the list. With nothing highlighted Enter does what it does in any text field, so a form around the field is submitted.
Closes the list. Pressed again, it clears the text.

behavior.intro: What the field does with text, matching, the list and motion.

items.title: Text, not a choice
items.text: The value is the text in the field. Choosing a suggestion fills it with that text, text that matches nothing stays as typed, and you should check it on submit when only some values are valid.

items.title: Opening
items.text: The list opens when the person types or presses Arrow Down or Arrow Up, and closes when the field is empty. It can also open on click, and the field keeps focus while it is open.

items.title: Matching
items.text: A suggestion matches when it contains the typed text, ignoring case and accents. You can replace the rule, highlight the first match so Enter takes it, and cap the number of suggestions.

items.title: Objects as items
items.text: Items can be objects. Give each item the object as its value, and the root a function that turns it into the field's text.

items.title: No match
items.text: The empty line shows in the list when nothing matches and is hidden while it has no content. Give it a sentence so a list without matches never looks broken.

items.title: Position and size
items.text: The list opens below the field, 4 px away and as wide as the field (12 rem at least). It flips above when there is no room below and scrolls when it is taller than the room left.

items.title: Highlight
items.text: The pointer and the keyboard share one highlight, drawn with the page fill of a hovered row. Moving the pointer over a row highlights it; you can switch that off.

items.title: Invalid and disabled
items.text: Mark the input invalid to turn the border and focus ring red, and say why in a line under the field linked with aria-describedby. Disabled dims the field to 40 % and ignores pointer and keyboard.

items.title: Previews in these docs
items.text: The list is portalled to the end of the document and floats over the page. The previews here draw it inside the card so it stays contained, and show it only while the whole card is on screen.

items.title: Motion
items.text: The list appears and disappears at once. Nothing else moves: the border and focus ring change colour quickly.

items.title: Reduced motion
items.text: There is no movement to remove, so reduced motion changes nothing. The colour change is a short fade and stays.

minimalUsage.expected: You should see a text field with the placeholder Search cities. Type li and the list keeps Berlin and Lisbon; press Arrow Down and Enter and the field fills with Berlin.

components.title: Calendar
components.description: A month grid for picking one date or a range, with keyboard navigation and optional min, max and disabled days.

props.description: Header style: a plain label or clickable month/year buttons.

props.description: Shows the range preview up to this day as if it were hovered.

props.name: markedDays
props.description: Days that get a dot under the number.

props.description: Label appended to marked days' aria-label.

props.name: max
props.description: Latest day that can be picked. Keyboard focus stops here and later months cannot be opened.

props.name: min
props.description: Earliest day that can be picked. Keyboard focus stops here and earlier months cannot be opened.

props.name: navigation
props.description: Which navigation arrows to show. Hidden arrows keep their slot.

props.name: reasonDefaultOpenDay
props.description: The day whose disabled tooltip starts open (for documentation).

props.name: size
props.description: The size of the day cells.

props.name: status
props.description: Status of the calendar data. Anything but "ready" prevents picking.

parts.name: Calendar
parts.description: An inline month grid, Monday first, for a single day or a range, with 32 px or 40 px days. For a field with a popover, use DatePicker.

parts.name: CalendarHeader
parts.description: The month title between the previous and next buttons, as a plain label or two buttons that open the month and year picker. A hidden arrow keeps its slot, so the title stays centred.

parts.name: Weekday labels
parts.description: Seven weekday labels, Mo to Su, each read as the full weekday by screen readers. The grid always shows six weeks, so its height never changes.

parts.name: CalendarDay
parts.description: One button per day: selection, today, outside days and unavailable days describe the date, while hover, pressed and focus describe the pointer. The figure marks the start of a range.

parts.name: Range band
parts.description: In range mode, days between start and end form one connected tint band with filled, rounded ends. While only the start exists, hovering a later day previews the band.

parts.name: Marked day
parts.description: A dot under the number of a day that has data, such as an event or an open slot. The dot is never the only cue: a label is added to the day's accessible name.

parts.name: Today
parts.description: Today has a ring on top of any selection. You can override today's date, which helps in demos and tests.

parts.name: CalendarPeriodPicker
parts.description: A 3 by 4 grid of months or twelve years with its own previous and next buttons. It opens from the month and year header and also works on its own.

parts.name: Restriction
parts.description: A blocked day can show its reason in a tooltip and in its accessible name. A loading, empty or error status blocks every day, and the banner that explains it sits next to the calendar.

parts.name: CalendarPeriodCell
parts.description: One month or year button in the period picker.

items.text: Use Calendar to show a month inline, next to a schedule or in your own popover. To pick a date in a form field, use DatePicker.
In range mode the first click sets the start, the second the end, and a third starts a new range. A range without an end is a draft, so say in the interface what is missing.
Use the larger size (40 px days) when the calendar is the main control and the smaller one (32 px) in dense panels.
Use the month and year header for birth dates and other far dates, so nobody pages month by month. Set the starting month, or control the month when two calendars must move together.
Limit the choice with a minimum and maximum, and block single days with a list or a rule such as weekends. Say why in a tooltip or in the text nearby.
Mark days that carry data and name the meaning, for example has events or has open slots.
While data loads or fails, set the status and show a banner beside the calendar that explains why and offers a retry.
Don't rely on a dot alone to show that a day has events. Name its meaning and list the events next to the calendar.
Don't show hover, pressed or the range preview as a confirmed choice. A confirmed day never changes on hover, and the preview band is lighter.
Don't block days without saying why. Screen readers announce a blocked day as unavailable, but a sighted person sees only a dimmed number.

useFor: Showing a month next to a schedule, with a dot on the days that have events
Picking one day, or a start and an end day, where the calendar is the main control
A booking window with days that are blocked, booked or still open

useInstead.name: Date Picker
useInstead.text: a date in a form field, where the calendar opens in a popover

useInstead.name: Agenda
useInstead.text: a list of events grouped by day

useInstead.name: Timeline
useInstead.text: events in the order they happened

keyboard.intro: The day grid is one Tab stop with roving focus. Tab enters on the chosen day, today or the first of the month, and the keys below move inside the grid.

rows.action: Moves focus into the grid once, then on to the next control. The header buttons are separate tab stops before the grid.
Moves focus one day back or forward. At the edge of the month it opens the neighbouring month.
Moves focus one week back or forward.
Moves focus to the first or the last day of the week.
Moves focus one month back or forward, keeping the day of the month where it exists. With Shift it moves one year.
Picks the focused day. A blocked day stays reachable with the arrow keys but is not picked, and nothing is picked while `status` is not `ready`.
In the month or year picker: goes back to the days.

behavior.intro: What the calendar does with state, the grid, restrictions and motion.

items.title: Controlled or not
items.text: You can control the selection and the visible month, or let the calendar keep them. The month starts on the default month, the chosen day or today.

items.title: Six weeks
items.text: The grid always shows six weeks, Monday first, so the height stays the same in every month. Days of neighbouring months are dimmed but still clickable.

items.title: Range
items.text: In range mode a click before the start swaps the two ends. While only the start exists, days up to the hovered or focused day show a preview band.

items.title: Limits
items.text: Days outside the minimum and maximum are blocked and the month arrows lock at the edge. Blocked days are dimmed, announced as unavailable and skipped by Enter, but arrow keys still reach them.

items.title: Status
items.text: A loading, empty or error status blocks every day, and loading marks the grid as busy. The calendar draws no banner itself.

items.title: Names
items.text: Each day is named with its full date, such as Thursday, November 12, 2026, plus its marked label or blocked reason. The grid is named by its month heading.

items.title: Motion
items.text: A day changes its fill quickly on hover and press. Only colour changes and nothing moves.

items.title: Reduced motion
items.text: With reduced motion nothing changes, since the calendar has no movement. The Tooltip on a blocked day keeps its own motion.

minimalUsage.expected: You see the current month as a six-week grid with today chosen. Click another day to move the choice, and use the arrows or arrow keys to change the month.

Calendar.mode.description: `single` picks one day and `range` picks a start and an end. It also decides the shape of `selected` and `onSelect`: a `Date`, or `{ from, to }`.

Calendar.selected.description: The chosen day (`single`) or range (`range`). The calendar does not keep it: update it in `onSelect`.

Calendar.onSelect.description: Called with the day that was picked, or in `range` mode with the new `{ from, to }`. A range without `to` is a draft.

Calendar.month.description: The visible month, to control it. Use it with `onMonthChange` when two calendars must move together.

Calendar.defaultMonth.description: The month to open on when `month` is not set. Defaults to the month of the chosen day, else today.

Calendar.onMonthChange.description: Called with the first day of the new month when the arrows, the keyboard or the period picker change it.

Calendar.min.description: The earliest day that can be picked. Keyboard focus stops here and earlier months cannot be opened.

Calendar.max.description: The latest day that can be picked. Keyboard focus stops here and later months cannot be opened.

Calendar.disabled.description: Days inside `min` and `max` that cannot be picked: a list of dates, or a function that returns true for a blocked day. They stay reachable with the arrow keys and are announced as unavailable.

Calendar.size.description: The size of the day cells: `sm` is 32 px (the default) and `md` is 40 px.

Calendar.header.description: `label` shows the month as a title; `month-year` shows two buttons that open the month and year picker.

Calendar.navigation.description: Which arrows to show: `both` (the default), `previous`, `next` or `none`. A hidden arrow keeps its slot.

Calendar.markedDays.description: Days that get a dot under the number: a list of dates, or a function that returns true for a marked day.

Calendar.markedLabel.description: Words added to the accessible name of a marked day, for example `has events`. Defaults to `marked`.

Calendar.disabledReason.description: When set, every blocked day shows this text in a tooltip and in its accessible name.

Calendar.status.description: The state of the data behind the calendar: `ready` (the default), `loading`, `empty` or `error`. Anything but `ready` blocks every day.

Calendar.today.description: Overrides the date of today, which defaults to `new Date()`. Use it for demos and tests.

Calendar.hoverDay.description: Shows the range preview up to this day as if it were hovered. For documentation.

Calendar.reasonDefaultOpenDay.description: The blocked day whose `disabledReason` tooltip starts open. For documentation.

Calendar.className.description: Extra classes for the calendar root.

CalendarDay.selection.description: What the day means in the choice: `none`, `single`, `start`, `middle`, `end` or `preview` (the lighter band while a range is being chosen).

CalendarDay.today.description: Rings the day as today, on top of any selection.

CalendarDay.outside.description: Dims the day because it belongs to the neighbouring month.

CalendarDay.unavailable.description: Dims the day and blocks the pointer. Set it for days outside `min` and `max`, blocked days and every day while the data is not ready.

CalendarDay.marked.description: Draws a dot under the number.

CalendarDay.interaction.description: Forces the look of a pointer state (`rest`, `hover`, `pressed`, `focus`) for documentation. Real hover, press and focus need no prop.

CalendarDay.size.description: The size of the cell: `sm` is 32 px and `md` is 40 px.

CalendarHeader.type.description: `label` for a title, `month-year` for two buttons.

CalendarHeader.size.description: `sm` or `md`, to match the size of the days.

CalendarHeader.previousDisabled.description: Disables the previous button, for example at the minimum date.

CalendarHeader.nextDisabled.description: Disables the next button, for example at the maximum date.

CalendarHeader.onPrevious.description: Called when the previous button is pressed.

CalendarHeader.onNext.description: Called when the next button is pressed.

CalendarHeader.onMonthClick.description: Called when the month button of the `month-year` header is pressed.

CalendarHeader.onYearClick.description: Called when the year button of the `month-year` header is pressed.

CalendarHeader.headingId.description: The id of the title, so the grid can name itself by it.

CalendarHeader.className.description: Extra classes for the header row.

CalendarPeriodPicker.type.description: `month` shows the twelve months of a year, `year` shows twelve years.

CalendarPeriodPicker.month.description: The reference month: its year is shown, or the window of twelve years that contains it.

CalendarPeriodPicker.selected.description: The chosen month or year, filled in the grid.

CalendarPeriodPicker.onSelect.description: Called with the first day of the chosen month, or with a date in the chosen year.

CalendarPeriodPicker.onNavigate.description: Called with the new reference date when the previous or next button moves to another year or window.

CalendarPeriodPicker.today.description: Overrides the date of today, which gets the ring.

CalendarPeriodPicker.min.description: Months or years before this are unavailable.

CalendarPeriodPicker.max.description: Months or years after this are unavailable.

CalendarPeriodPicker.className.description: Extra classes for the picker root.

CalendarPeriodCell.selected.description: Fills the cell as the chosen month or year.

CalendarPeriodCell.current.description: Rings the cell as the current month or year.

CalendarPeriodCell.unavailable.description: Dims the cell and blocks the pointer.

CalendarPeriodCell.interaction.description: Forces the look of a pointer state for documentation.

components.title: Date Picker
components.description: A Calendar inside a Popover, with Cancel/Apply actions.
components.props: function DatePicker(props: DatePickerProps): React.JSX.Element;

props.name: disabled
props.description: Days that cannot be picked: a list of dates or a test (passed to Calendar).

props.name: max
props.description: Latest day that can be picked (passed to Calendar).

props.name: min
props.description: Earliest day that can be picked (passed to Calendar).

props.name: numberOfMonths
props.description: Months shown side by side. Defaults to 2 for range mode.

props.name: presets
props.description: Quick-select sidebar (Figma: Type=presets). `true` uses the built-in presets.

parts.name: DatePicker
parts.description: The trigger and the popover in one component. It looks like a plain button or, as a field, adds a label, a format hint and an error line, and it picks a single date or a range.

parts.name: Trigger
parts.description: The element that opens the popover: a button, a field, or a text field you can type in. It shows Pick a date or the format hint while empty, then the chosen date or range.

parts.name: DatePickerPanel
parts.description: The popover content: calendars, presets and footer. A range shows two months side by side, a single date one, and the popover is as wide as its content (312 px for one month).

parts.name: Presets
parts.description: A column of quick ranges at the left, such as Last 7 days. Use the eight built-in ones or your own; choosing one fills the draft and Apply still confirms.

parts.name: Calendar
parts.description: A medium Calendar with its own header and arrows: two calendars for a range, one for a single date. See the Calendar page for its keys and states.

parts.name: Summary
parts.description: The line at the left of the footer. It says what is missing, explains an error, or shows the choice, with the length of a range in days or nights.

parts.name: Cancel and Apply
parts.description: Cancel closes the popover and drops the draft. Apply commits it and closes, and stays disabled while nothing valid can be committed.

parts.name: DatePickerField
parts.description: The closed field alone, without a popover, with its label and helper line. It is what the picker draws as a field, and is useful next to an inline panel.

parts.name: DatePickerFooter
parts.description: The summary line with Cancel and Apply, as its own part for panels you compose yourself.

items.text: Use the default button for a filter in a toolbar, and the field in a form, where it needs a label, a hint and an error line.
Let people type dates far in the past or future, such as a date of birth. Typing beats paging, and the field takes MM/DD/YYYY or a written date like Nov 12, 2026.
Use range mode with presets for reporting, where people usually want Last 7 days or Month to date. The picker shows one month below 830 px on its own.
Use instant confirmation for a single date that is easy to change, such as a due date. Keep Apply and Cancel for ranges and for dates that trigger work, such as a booking.
Limit the choice with min, max and disabled days. They block days in the calendar and are enforced when a date is typed.
Say what an unfinished or invalid range needs. The field shows Select an end date to finish the range, or the error, and Apply stays off until the range is valid.
Don't use instant confirmation with a range. Without the footer there is nothing to commit it.
Don't use a Date Picker for a month shown next to your content. Use Calendar, which has no popover.
Don't leave the label out of a field. The format hint disappears once a date is chosen, but the label stays.

useFor: One date in a form, such as a due date, a delivery date or a date of birth
A date range that filters a report, with quick ranges such as Last 30 days
A date with limits, such as weekdays only or the next three months

useInstead.name: Calendar
useInstead.text: a month shown on the page, for example next to a schedule

useInstead.name: Input
useInstead.text: free text that is not a date

useInstead.name: Select
useInstead.text: a choice from a short fixed list, such as a month or a year

keyboard.intro: The trigger is a native button or text field. The popover is not modal: Tab moves through its presets, calendar and buttons, and Escape closes it.

rows.action: Moves focus to the trigger. In a typeable field it goes to the calendar icon in front of the text first (the button that opens the calendar), then into the text. Inside the open popover it moves through the presets, the calendar and the footer buttons.
On the trigger or the calendar button: opens the popover. On a day: picks it. On Cancel or Apply: runs it.
In a typeable field: commits the typed date. A text that is not a date, or lies outside `min` and `max`, shows an error and keeps the old value. Leaving the field commits too.
Closes the popover, drops the draft and returns focus to the trigger.
In the calendar: move by day, week and month. See the Calendar page for Home, End and the year keys.

behavior.intro: What the picker does with state, drafts, typing, limits and motion.

items.title: Controlled or not
items.text: Pass a value and a change handler to hold the date or range, and an open state to hold the popover. Without them the picker keeps its own state, starting from the defaults you give.

items.title: Draft and commit
items.text: By default the days you click are a draft. Apply commits it and closes the popover, while Cancel, Escape or a click outside drops it, and it reopens from the committed value.

items.title: Instant
items.text: With instant confirmation a single date commits on the click and closes the popover, with no footer. It does not apply to a range.

items.title: Range
items.text: The first click sets the start, the second the end, and a click before the start swaps them. A range without an end is incomplete, so Apply stays off, and an end before the start is an error.

items.title: Typing
items.text: A typeable field parses MM/DD/YYYY and dates like Nov 12, 2026, and for a range two dates joined by a dash. It commits on Enter or blur, and a bad entry shows an error and keeps the last good value.

items.title: Limits
items.text: Min, max and disabled days block days in the calendar, dim presets that fall outside, and reject typed dates.

items.title: Presets
items.text: A preset fills the draft and moves the calendar to its start. The preset that matches the draft shows as selected.

items.title: Narrow screens
items.text: Below 830 px a range with presets shows one month, and below 650 px a range without presets stacks its two months. There is no separate mobile version.

items.title: Focus
items.text: The popover sits below the trigger, or below the text box of a typeable field. Closing it returns focus to the trigger.

items.title: Motion
items.text: The popover fades and scales in, and out a step faster. The calendar and buttons inside change colour on the fast duration.

items.title: Reduced motion
items.text: With reduced motion the popover keeps its fade and drops the scale. Colour changes on days and buttons are not movement and stay.

minimalUsage.expected: You see a button that says Pick a date. Press it, choose a day and press Apply: the button shows the date, for example Nov 12, 2026.

DatePicker.mode.description: `single` picks one date and `range` picks a start and an end. It also decides the shape of `value`: a `Date`, or `{ from, to }`.

DatePicker.value.description: The date or the range, to control it. Update it in `onValueChange`.

DatePicker.defaultValue.description: The date or range to start with when the picker keeps its own state.

DatePicker.onValueChange.description: Called with the committed date or range: on Apply, on a click in `instant` mode, or when a typed entry is accepted. It is called with `undefined` when a typed field is cleared.

DatePicker.appearance.description: `button` (the default) is a plain button; `field` is a form field with a label, a format hint and an error line.

DatePicker.label.description: The visible label of a `field`. Without it the field is named `Date` or `Date range` for screen readers.

DatePicker.helperText.description: The line under a `field`. It defaults to the format hint, and `false` hides it.

DatePicker.error.description: An error message for a `field`. It turns the field red, shows the message under it and keeps Apply off.

DatePicker.fieldState.description: `default`, `disabled` (dimmed, does not open) or `readonly` (focusable, shows the value, does not open).
